children.translated_text: <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> with <s>Gauḍapāda</s>'s Commentary (<s>Bhāṣya</s>)
Salutations to that <s>Kapila</s>, by whom, for the world sinking in the ocean of ignorance,
out of compassion, the ship of <s>Sāṃkhya</s> was provided for crossing over.
A treatise that is concise, clear, and equipped with valid means of knowledge, established doctrines, and reasonings —
I shall expound in summary for the benefit of students.
From the affliction of the threefold suffering arises the desire to know the means for its removal.
If [you say] that [inquiry] is pointless because [remedies] are observed [in ordinary life] — no, because [such remedies] are not certain and permanent. || 1 ||

children.text: duḥkhatrayeti / asyā āryyāyā upodghātaḥ kriyate / iha bhagavānbrahmasutaḥ kapilo nāma / tadyathā -

children.translated_text: <s>Sanaka</s> and <s>Sananda</s>, and the third, <s>Sanātana</s>,
<s>Āsuri</s> and <s>Kapila</s>, and likewise <s>Voḍhu</s> and <s>Pañcaśikha</s> —

children.text: ityete brahmaṇaḥ putrāḥ sapta proktā maharṣayaḥ //
children.translated_text: these seven are proclaimed as the great sages, sons of <s>Brahmā</s>.
'<s>Duḥkhatraya</s>' — An introduction to this <s>āryā</s> verse is given. Here, the Blessed One, son of <s>Brahmā</s>, is named <s>Kapila</s>. As follows:

children.text: kapilasya sahotpannā dharmmo jñānaṃ vairāgyamaiśvaryyañceti / evaṃ sa utpannaḥ sannandhatamasi majjajjagadālokya saṃsārapāramparyyeṇa satkāruṇyo jijñāsamānāya āsurisagotrāya brahmaṇāyedaṃ pañcaviṃśatitattvānāṃ jñānamuktavān / yasya jñānādduḥkhakṣayo bhavati /

children.translated_text: One who knows the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s>, wherever and in whichever stage of life he may dwell,

children.text: jaṭī muṇḍī śikhī vāpi mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ //
children.translated_text: whether wearing matted locks, shaven-headed, or bearing a topknot — he is liberated; there is no doubt about this.

Together with <s>Kapila</s> arose <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), and <s>aiśvarya</s> (lordship). Thus, having arisen and seeing the world sinking in the darkness of blind ignorance, out of compassion through the succession of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration), he taught this knowledge of the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s> (principles) to one of the lineage of <s>Āsuri</s>, a Brahmin who desired to know. By the knowledge of which, the destruction of suffering occurs.

children.text: tadidamāhuḥ / duḥkhatrayābhighātājjijñāseti / tatra duḥkhatrayaṃ- ādhyātmikaṃ ādhibhautikaṃ ādhidaivikaṃ ceti / tatrādhyātmikaṃ dvividhaṃ - śārīraṃ mānasaṃ ceti / śārīraṃ vātapittaśleṣmaviparyyayakṛtaṃ jvarātīsārādi / mānasaṃ priyaviyogāpriyasaṃyogādi / ādhibhautikaṃ caturvidhaṃ - bhūtagrāmanimittaṃ manuṣyapaśumṛgapakṣisarīsṛpadaṃśamaśakayūkāmatkuṇamatsyamakaragrāhasthāvarebhyo jarāyujāṇḍajasvedajodbhijjebhyaḥ sakāśādupajāyate / ādhidaivikaṃ - devānāmidaṃ daivikam / divaḥ prabhavatīti vā daivaṃ tadadhikṛtya yadupajāyate śītoṣṇavātavarṣāśanipātādikam / evaṃ yathā duḥkhatrayābhijñātājjijñāsā kāryyā kva / tadabhighātake hetau / tasya duḥkhatrayasya abhighātako yo 'sau hetustatreti / dṛṣṭe sāpārthā cet / dṛṣṭe hetau duḥkhatrayābhighātake sā jijñāsāpārthā cedyadi / tatrādhyātmikasya dvividhasyāpi āyurvedaśāstrakriyayā priyasamāgamāpriyaparihārakaṭutiktakaṣāyādikvāthādibhirdṛṣṭa eva ādhyātmikopāyaḥ / ādhibhautikasya rakṣādinābhighāto dṛṣṭaḥ / dṛṣṭe sāpārthā cedevaṃ manyase / na / ekāntyātyantato 'bhāvāt / yata ekāntato 'vaśyaṃ atyantato nityaṃ dṛṣṭena hetunābhighāto na bhavati tasmādanyatra ekāntātyantābhighātake hetau jijñāsā vividiṣā kāryeti // 1 //
children.translated_text: This they say: 'From the affliction of the threefold suffering arises the desire to know.' Therein, the threefold suffering is: <s>ādhyātmika</s> (pertaining to the self), <s>ādhibhautika</s> (pertaining to created beings), and <s>ādhidaivika</s> (pertaining to the gods). Of these, <s>ādhyātmika</s> is twofold: bodily and mental. The bodily is caused by the derangement of <s>vāta</s> (wind), <s>pitta</s> (bile), and <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm) — such as fever, dysentery, and the like. The mental is separation from the beloved, contact with the unpleasant, and so forth. <s>Ādhibhautika</s> is fourfold — caused by the classes of beings: it arises from humans, cattle, wild animals, birds, serpents, mosquitoes, gnats, lice, bedbugs, fish, crocodiles, alligators, and plants — from womb-born, egg-born, sweat-born, and sprout-born creatures. <s>Ādhidaivika</s> — this pertains to the gods, hence 'divine'; or because it originates from heaven — what arises therefrom, such as cold, heat, wind, rain, lightning-strike, and the like. Thus, the desire to know arising from the affliction of the threefold suffering should be directed where? 'In the means for its removal.' The means that removes that threefold suffering — therein [the inquiry should be directed]. 'If [you say that inquiry] is pointless because [remedies] are observed' — if you think that inquiry is pointless because observable means for removing the threefold suffering exist — for the <s>ādhyātmika</s>, of both kinds, through the practice of <s>Āyurveda</s> (medical science), reunion with the beloved, removal of the unpleasant, and decoctions of bitter, astringent substances and the like — the observable remedy for <s>ādhyātmika</s> suffering is seen. For <s>ādhibhautika</s>, removal through protective charms and the like is observed. If you think thus — that 'it is pointless because [remedies] are observed' — no. 'Because [such remedies] are not certain and permanent' — since by observable means, the removal [of suffering] does not occur certainly (inevitably) and permanently (for all time); therefore, inquiry — the desire to know — should be directed elsewhere, toward a means that provides certain and permanent removal.

children.text: yadi dṛṣṭānyatra jijñāsā kāryyā tato 'pi naiva yata ānuśraviko heturduḥkhatrayābhighātakaḥ / anuśravatītyanuśravastatrabhavaḥ ānuśravikaḥ sa ca āgamātsiddhaḥ / yathā

children.translated_text: 'We have drunk the <s>Soma</s>; we have become immortal; we have attained the light; we have found the gods.
What now can the enemy do to us? What indeed is the harm of death to an immortal?'

If you say inquiry should be directed toward scriptural [means] — not so either, because the <s>ānuśravika</s> (scriptural) means also removes the threefold suffering [only imperfectly]. That which is heard [through scripture] is <s>anuśrava</s>; what pertains to it is <s>ānuśravika</s>, and that is established from <s>āgama</s> (scripture). As [the Vedic hymn says]:

children.text: kadācidindrādīnāṃ devānāṃ kalpa āsīt / kathaṃ vayamamṛtā abhūmeti vicāryyāmuṃ yasmādvayamapāma somaṃ pītavantaḥ somaṃ tasmādamṛtā abhūma amarā bhūtavanta ityarthaḥ kiṃca aganma jyotiḥ gatavato labdhavato jyotiḥ svargamiti / avidāma devān divyān viditavantaḥ / evaṃ ca kinnūnamasmān kṛṇavadarātiḥ nūnaṃ niścitaṃ kiṃ arātiḥ śatrurasmān kṛṇavat kartteti kimu dhūrttiramṛtamartyasya dhūrttirjarā hiṃsā vā kiṃ kariṣyati amṛtamartyasya / anyacca śrūyate ātyantikaṃ phalaṃ paśuvadhena / sarvvaṃllokāñjayati mṛtyuṃ tarati pāpmānaṃ tarati brahmahatyāṃ tarati yo yo 'śvamedhena yajata iti / ekāntātyantike eva vedokte apārthe 'vajijñāsā iti na / ucyate /
children.translated_text: Once upon a time, in a <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age), the gods led by <s>Indra</s> deliberated: 'How have we become immortal?' Having considered thus — 'Because we drank <s>Soma</s>, therefore we have become immortal, meaning we have become deathless'; furthermore, 'we have attained the light' — meaning 'we have gone to, obtained, the light, that is, heaven'; 'we have found the gods' — meaning 'we have known the divine ones.' And thus, 'what now can the enemy do to us?' — surely, certainly, what can the enemy do to us? 'What indeed is the harm of death to an immortal?' — what can old age or injury do to an immortal mortal? Moreover, it is heard that the eternal fruit [is obtained] through animal sacrifice: 'One conquers all worlds, crosses over death, crosses over sin, crosses over the sin of killing a Brahmin — whoever sacrifices with the <s>Aśvamedha</s>' (horse sacrifice). If you think there should be no inquiry because the Vedic [means], which is certain and permanent, is not purposeless — it is replied:
The scriptural [means] is like the observable; for it too is connected with impurity, decay, and inequality.
Superior to both is [the knowledge] arising from the discriminative knowledge of the manifest, the unmanifest, and the knower. || 2 ||

children.text: dṛṣṭavadānuśravika iti dṛṣṭena tulyo dṛṣṭavat / ko 'sau ānuśravikaḥ kasmātsa yasmādaviśuddhikṣayātiśayayuktaḥ / aviśuddhiyuktaḥ paśughātāt tathā coktam /

children.translated_text: 'Six hundred animals are consecrated on the middle day
of the <s>Aśvamedha</s> [sacrifice], as stated, minus three.'

'The scriptural is like the observable' — equal to the observable, hence 'like the observable.' What is that? The <s>ānuśravika</s> (scriptural means). Why? Because it too is connected with impurity, decay, and inequality. It is connected with impurity due to the slaughter of animals. As it is stated:

children.text: yadyapi śrutismṛtivihito dharmmastathāpi miśrībhāvādaviśuddhiyukta iti / yathā

children.translated_text: 'Many thousands of <s>Indras</s> and gods, age after age,
have passed away with time; for time is insurmountable.'
Although the <s>dharma</s> is enjoined by <s>śruti</s> (revelation) and <s>smṛti</s> (tradition), nevertheless, because of admixture [with violence], it is connected with impurity. As:

children.text:
evamindrādināśātkṣayayuktaḥ / tathātiśayo viśeṣastena yuktaḥ / viśeṣaguṇādarśanāditarasya duḥkhaṃ syāditi / evamānuśraviko 'pi heturdṛṣṭavat / kastarhi śreyāniti cet / ucyate /
tadviparītaḥ śreyān tābhyāṃ dṛṣṭānuśravikābhyāṃ viparītaḥ śreyān praśasyatara iti / aviśuddhikṣayātiśayāyuktatvāt / sa kathamityāha /
vyaktāvyaktajñavijñānāt tatra vyaktaṃ mahadādibuddhirahaṃkāraḥ pañca tanmātrāṇi ekādaśendriyāṇi pañcamahābhūtāni / avyaktaṃ pradhānam / jñaḥ puruṣaḥ / evametāni pañcaviṃśatitattvāni vyaktāvyaktajñāni kathyante etadvijñānācchreya ityuktaṃ ca pañcaviṃśatitattvajña iti // 2 //
children.translated_text:
Thus, because of the destruction of <s>Indra</s> and others, [the scriptural means] is connected with decay. And inequality means distinction — connected with that; from the perception of special qualities in another, suffering would arise [for the lesser being]. Thus the scriptural means too is like the observable. If you ask, 'What then is superior?' — it is replied:
'Superior to both' — superior, more praiseworthy, than both the observable and scriptural [means], is that which is the opposite of those [two]. Why? Because it is not connected with impurity, decay, and inequality. How is that [attained]? It is replied:
'From the discriminative knowledge of the manifest, the unmanifest, and the knower' — therein, the 'manifest' is <s>Mahat</s> (the Great) and what follows: <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-sense), the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements), the eleven <s>indriyas</s> (sense organs), and the five <s>mahābhūtas</s> (gross elements). The 'unmanifest' is <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter). The 'knower' is <s>Puruṣa</s> (consciousness). Thus these twenty-five <s>tattvas</s> are called the manifest, the unmanifest, and the knower. From the discriminative knowledge of these comes the highest good — as stated: 'One who knows the twenty-five tattvas.' // 2 //
Now, what is the distinction among the manifest, the unmanifest, and the knower? It is stated:
The root <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) is uncreated; the seven — <s>Mahat</s> and the rest — are both <s>prakṛtis</s> (creative) and <s>vikṛtis</s> (created).

children.text: ṣoḍaśakastu vikāro na prakṛtirna vikṛtiḥ puruṣaḥ || 3 ||
children.translated_text: The group of sixteen is merely created (<s>vikāra</s>); <s>Puruṣa</s> is neither <s>prakṛti</s> nor <s>vikṛti</s>. || 3 ||

children.text: mūlaprakṛtiḥ pradhānam / prakṛtivikṛtisaptakasya mūlabhūtatvāt / mūlaṃ ca sā prakṛtiśca mūlaprakṛtiravikṛtiḥ / anyasmānnotpadyate tena prakṛtiḥ kasyacidvikāro na bhavati / mahadādyāḥ prakṛtivikṛtayaḥ sapta / mahābhūtāditi buddhiḥ buddhyādyāḥ sapta buddhi 1 ahaṃkāraḥ 2 pañcatanmātrāṇi 5 etāni saptaprakṛtivikṛtayaḥ / tadyathā / pradhānādbuddhirutpadyate tena vikṛtiḥ pradhānasya vikāra iti saivāhaṃkāramutpādayati ataḥ prakṛtiḥ / ahaṃkāro 'pi buddherutpadyata iti vikṛtiḥ sa ca pañcatanmātrāṇyutpādayatīti prakṛtiḥ / tatra śabdatanmātramahaṃkārādutpadyata iti vikṛtistasmādākāśamutpadyata iti prakṛtiḥ / tathā sparśatanmātramahaṃkārādutpadyata iti vikṛtistadevaṃ vāyumutpādayatīti prakṛtiḥ / gandhatanmātramahaṃkārādutpadyata iti vikṛtistadevaṃ pṛthivīmutpādayatīti prakṛtiḥ / rūpatanmātramahaṃkārādutpadyata iti vikṛtistadevaṃ teja utpādayatīti prakṛtiḥ / rasatanmātramahaṃkārādutpadyata iti vikṛtistadevaṃ āpa utpādayatīti prakṛtiḥ / evaṃ mahadādyāḥ sapta prakṛtayo vikṛtayaśca / ṣoḍaśakaśca vikāraḥ pañcabuddhīndriyāṇi pañcakarmmendriyāṇi ekādaśaṃ manaḥ pañcamahābhūtāni eṣa ṣoḍaśako gaṇo vikṛtireva / vikāro vikṛtiḥ / na prakṛtirna vikṛtiḥ puruṣaḥ // 3 //
children.translated_text: The root <s>Prakṛti</s> is <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter). Because it is the root of the group of seven <s>prakṛti-vikṛtis</s>, [it is called] 'root.' It is both a root and a <s>prakṛti</s>, hence 'root <s>Prakṛti</s>.' It is 'uncreated' (<s>avikṛti</s>) — it does not arise from anything else, hence it is a <s>prakṛti</s>; it is not a modification of anything. 'The seven — <s>Mahat</s> and the rest — are both <s>prakṛtis</s> and <s>vikṛtis</s>.' '<s>Mahat</s> and the rest' means <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect); the seven beginning with <s>Buddhi</s> are: <s>Buddhi</s> (1), <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-sense) (2), and the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) (5) — these seven are both <s>prakṛtis</s> and <s>vikṛtis</s>. That is to say: <s>Buddhi</s> arises from <s>Pradhāna</s>, so it is a <s>vikṛti</s> — a modification of <s>Pradhāna</s>; and that same [<s>Buddhi</s>] produces <s>Ahaṃkāra</s>, so it is a <s>prakṛti</s>. <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> too arises from <s>Buddhi</s>, so it is a <s>vikṛti</s>; and it produces the five <s>tanmātras</s>, so it is a <s>prakṛti</s>. Therein, the <s>śabda-tanmātra</s> (sound-subtle-element) arises from <s>Ahaṃkāra</s>, so it is a <s>vikṛti</s>; from it arises <s>ākāśa</s> (space), so it is a <s>prakṛti</s>. Likewise, the <s>sparśa-tanmātra</s> (touch-subtle-element) arises from <s>Ahaṃkāra</s>, so it is a <s>vikṛti</s>; it produces <s>vāyu</s> (air), so it is a <s>prakṛti</s>. The <s>gandha-tanmātra</s> (smell-subtle-element) arises from <s>Ahaṃkāra</s>, so it is a <s>vikṛti</s>; it produces <s>pṛthivī</s> (earth), so it is a <s>prakṛti</s>. The <s>rūpa-tanmātra</s> (form-subtle-element) arises from <s>Ahaṃkāra</s>, so it is a <s>vikṛti</s>; it produces <s>tejas</s> (fire), so it is a <s>prakṛti</s>. The <s>rasa-tanmātra</s> (taste-subtle-element) arises from <s>Ahaṃkāra</s>, so it is a <s>vikṛti</s>; it produces <s>āpas</s> (water), so it is a <s>prakṛti</s>. Thus, the seven beginning with <s>Mahat</s> are both <s>prakṛtis</s> and <s>vikṛtis</s>. And the group of sixteen is a modification: the five <s>buddhīndriyas</s> (cognitive sense organs), the five <s>karmendriyas</s> (organs of action), <s>manas</s> (mind) as the eleventh, and the five <s>mahābhūtas</s> (gross elements) — this group of sixteen is merely <s>vikṛti</s> (modification). <s>Vikāra</s> means <s>vikṛti</s>. <s>Puruṣa</s> is neither <s>prakṛti</s> nor <s>vikṛti</s>. // 3 //

children.text: evameṣāṃ vyaktāvyaktajñānāṃ trayāṇāṃ padārthānāṃ kaiḥ kiyadbhiḥ pramāṇaiḥ kena kasya vā pramāṇena siddhirbhavati / iha loke prameyavastu pramāṇena sādhyate yathā prasthādibhirvrīhayastulayā candanādi / tasmāt pramāṇamabhidheyam /
children.translated_text: Thus, by how many and by which <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge) is the establishment of these three categories — the manifest, the unmanifest, and the knower — achieved? In this world, an object of knowledge is established through a <s>pramāṇa</s>, just as rice [is measured] by the <s>prastha</s> measure and sandalwood [is weighed] by a balance. Therefore, the <s>pramāṇa</s> should be stated:
Perception, inference, and reliable testimony — since all <s>pramāṇas</s> are established [within these three],
the <s>pramāṇa</s> is accepted as threefold; for the establishment of objects of knowledge is through <s>pramāṇa</s>. || 4 ||

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ yathā śrotraṃ tvak cakṣurjihvā ghrāṇamiti pañcabuddhīndriyāṇi śabdasparśarūparasagandhā eṣāṃ pañcānāṃ pañcaiva viṣayā yathāsaṃkhyaṃ śabdaṃ śrotraṃ tvak sparśaṃ cakṣū rūpaṃ jihvā rasaṃ ghrāṇaṃ gandhamiti / etaddṛṣṭamityucyate pramāṇam / pratyakṣeṇānumānena va yo 'rtho na gṛhyate sa āptavacanādgrāhyaḥ / yathendroḥ devarājaḥ uttarāḥ kuravaḥ svarge 'psarasa ityādi / pratyakṣānumānāgrāhyamathāptavacanādgṛhyate / api coktam /

children.translated_text: <s>Āgama</s> (scripture) is indeed <s>āptavacana</s> (reliable testimony); an <s>āpta</s> (reliable person) is known from the destruction of defects.
One whose defects are destroyed would not speak a false statement, because there would be no cause [for doing so].

'Observed' (<s>dṛṣṭa</s>) — namely, the ear, skin, eye, tongue, and nose are the five <s>buddhīndriyas</s> (cognitive sense organs); sound, touch, form, taste, and smell — these are the five objects of these five [senses], in respective order: the ear [perceives] sound, the skin touch, the eye form, the tongue taste, the nose smell. This is called the 'observed' <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge), that is, perception. An object that cannot be grasped by either perception or inference should be grasped through <s>āptavacana</s> (reliable testimony) — for example, that <s>Indra</s> is the king of the gods, that the Northern <s>Kurus</s> exist, that in heaven there are <s>Apsarases</s>, and so on — what cannot be grasped by perception or inference is grasped through <s>āptavacana</s>. And it is stated:
One who is devoted to his own duty, free from attachment and aversion,
always honored by those of similar [character] — such a one should be known as an <s>āpta</s> (reliable authority).

children.text: eteṣu pramāṇeṣu sarvapramāṇāni siddhāni bhavanti / ṣaṭ pramāṇāni jaiminiḥ / atha kāni tānyapramāṇāni / arthāpattiḥ sambhavaḥ abhāvaḥ pratibhā aitihyaṃ upamānaṃ ceti ṣaṭ pramāṇāni / tatrārthāpattirdvividhā dṛṣṭā śrutā ca / tatra dṛṣṭā / ekasmin pakṣe ātmabhāvo gṛhītaścedanyasminnapyātmabhāvo gṛhyata eva / śrutā yathā / divā devadatto na bhuṅkte atha ca pīno dṛśyate ato 'vagamyate rātrau bhuṅkta iti / sambhavo yathā / prastha ityukte catvāraḥ kuḍavāḥ sambhāvyante / abhāvo nāma / prāgitaretarātyantasarvābhāvalakṣaṇaḥ / prāgabhāvo yathā devadattaḥ kaumārayauvanādiṣu / itaretarābhāvaḥ paṭe ghaṭābhāvaḥ / atyantābhāvaḥ kharaviṣāṇavandhyāsutakhapuṣpavaditi / sarvābhāvaḥ pradhvaṃsābhāvo dagdhapaṭavaditi / yathā śuṣkadhānyadarśanadvṛṣṭerabhāvo 'vagamyate / evamabhāvo 'nekadhā / pratibhā yathā / dakṣiṇena vindhyasya sahyasya ca yaduttaram / pṛthivyāmāsamudrāyāṃ sa pradeśo manoramaḥ / evamukte tasmin pradeśe śobhanāḥ guṇāḥ santīti pratibhotpadyate pratibhānvāsasaṃjñānamiti / aitihyaṃ yathā / bravīti loko yathātra vaṭe yakṣiṇī pravasatītyeva aitihyam / upamānaṃ yathā / gauriva gavayaḥ samudra iva taḍāgam / etāni ṣaṭ pramāṇāni triṣu dṛṣṭādiṣvantarbhūtāni / tatrānumāne tāvadarthāpattirantarbhūtā / sambhavābhāvapratibhaitihyopamāścāptavacane / tasmāttriṣveva sarvapramāṇasiddhatvāt trividhaṃ pramāṇamiṣṭaṃ tadāha tena trividhena pramāṇena pramāṇasiddhirbhavatītita vākyaśeṣaḥ / prameyasiddhiḥ pramāṇāddhi / prameyaṃ pradhānaṃ buddhirahaṃkāraḥ pañcatanmātrāṇi ekādaśendriyāṇi pañcamahābhūtāni puruṣa iti etāni pañcaviṃśatitattvāni vyaktāvyaktajñānyucyante / tatra kiñcit pratyakṣeṇa sādhyaṃ kiñcidanumānena kiñcidāgameneti trividhaṃ pramāṇamuktaṃ // 4 //
children.translated_text: Within these [three] <s>pramāṇas</s>, all <s>pramāṇas</s> are established. <s>Jaimini</s> [holds that there are] six <s>pramāṇas</s>. Now, what are those [additional] <s>pramāṇas</s>? <s>Arthāpatti</s> (presumption), <s>sambhava</s> (inclusion), <s>abhāva</s> (non-existence), <s>pratibhā</s> (intuition), <s>aitihya</s> (tradition), and <s>upamāna</s> (analogy) — these are the six [additional] <s>pramāṇas</s>. Of these, <s>arthāpatti</s> is twofold: observed and heard. The observed: if the existence of something is grasped in one case, then in another case too its existence is grasped. The heard: for example, <s>Devadatta</s> does not eat during the day, yet he is seen to be fat; from this it is understood that he eats at night. <s>Sambhava</s>: for example, when a <s>prastha</s> [measure] is mentioned, four <s>kuḍavas</s> are implied. <s>Abhāva</s> (non-existence) is characterized as: prior non-existence, mutual non-existence, absolute non-existence, and total non-existence. Prior non-existence: as of <s>Devadatta</s> in [the stages of] childhood, youth, and so on. Mutual non-existence: the absence of a pot in a cloth. Absolute non-existence: like a hare's horn, a barren woman's son, or a sky-flower. Total non-existence (<s>pradhvaṃsābhāva</s>): like a burnt cloth. Just as from the sight of dried grain, the absence of rain is understood — thus non-existence is of many kinds. <s>Pratibhā</s> (intuition): for example, [when one hears:] 'South of the <s>Vindhya</s> and north of the <s>Sahya</s>, on the earth up to the ocean, that region is delightful' — upon hearing this, the intuition arises that 'there must be beautiful qualities in that region.' <s>Pratibhā</s> is called 'intuitive cognition.' <s>Aitihya</s> (tradition): for example, the world says, 'In this banyan tree a <s>Yakṣiṇī</s> dwells' — this is <s>aitihya</s>. <s>Upamāna</s> (analogy): for example, 'a <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox) is like a cow,' or 'a lake is like an ocean.' These six <s>pramāṇas</s> are included within the three [pramāṇas] beginning with perception. Of these, in inference
What is its characteristic? He says:
The ascertainment of each object is perception; inference, which is declared to be threefold,
is based on a mark (<s>liṅga</s>) and a bearer of the mark (<s>liṅgin</s>); and reliable scripture (<s>āptaśruti</s>) is <s>āptavacana</s> (reliable testimony). || 5 ||

children.text:
prativiṣayeṣu śrotrādināṃ śabdādiviṣayeṣu adhyavasāyo dṛṣṭaṃ pratyakṣamityarthaḥ / trividhamanumānamākhyātaṃ śeṣavat pūrvavat sāmānyato dṛṣṭaṃ ceti / pūrvamasyāstīti pūrvavad yathā meghonnatyā vṛṣṭiṃ sādhayati pūrvavṛṣṭitvāt / śeṣavadyathā samudrādekaṃ jalapalaṃ lavaṇamāsādya śeṣasyāpyasti lavaṇabhāva iti / sāmānyato dṛṣṭam / deśāntarāddeśāntaraṃ prāptaṃ dṛṣṭam / gatimaccandratārakaṃ caitravat / yathā caitranāmānaṃ deśāntarāddeśāntaraṃ prāptamavalokya gatimānayāmīti tadvaccandratārakamiti tathā puṣpitāmradarśanādanyatrapuṣpitāmrā iti sāmānyato dṛṣṭena sādhayati / etatsāmānyadṛṣṭam /
kiñca talliṅgaliṅgipūrvakamiti tadanumānaṃ liṅgapūrvakaṃ yatra liṅgena liṅgī anumīyate yathā daṇḍena yatiḥ / liṅgipūrvakaṃ ca yatra liṅginā liṅgamanumīyate yathā dṛṣṭvā yatimasyedaṃ tridaṇḍamiti / āptaśrutirāptavacanaṃ ca / āptā ācāryyā brahmādayaḥ / śrutirvedaḥ / āptaśca śrutiśca āptaśrutī taduktamāptavacanamiti // 5 //
children.translated_text: The ascertainment regarding each object — the ear's objects such as sound, and so forth — is perception (<s>dṛṣṭa</s>), meaning direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>). Inference is declared to be threefold: <s>śeṣavat</s> (from the remainder), <s>pūrvavat</s> (from the antecedent), and <s>sāmānyato dṛṣṭa</s> (from general observation). '<s>Pūrvavat</s>' — that which has a prior [instance]: just as one infers rain from the rising of clouds, because rain has been previously [associated with clouds]. '<s>Śeṣavat</s>' — for example, having tasted one drop of ocean water and finding it salty, one [infers] that the remainder too has the quality of saltiness. '<s>Sāmānyato dṛṣṭa</s>' (from general observation) — seeing that something has moved from one place to another. The moon and stars have motion, like [a man named] <s>Caitra</s>; just as, seeing <s>Caitra</s> having moved from one place to another, one concludes 'he has motion,' so too with the moon and stars — similarly

children.text: evaṃ trividhaṃ pramāṇamuktaṃ tatra kena pramāṇena kiṃ sādhyamucyate /
children.translated_text: Thus the threefold <s>pramāṇa</s> has been stated. Now, by which <s>pramāṇa</s> is what to be established? This is stated:
But through inference from general observation, the establishment of what is beyond the senses [is achieved];
and what is not established even thereby — that which is remote — is established through reliable scripture (<s>āptāgama</s>). || 6 ||

children.text: sāmānyato dṛṣṭādanumānādatīndriyāṇamindriyāṇyatītyavarttamānānāṃ siddhiḥ pradhānapuruṣāvatīndriyau sāmānyato dṛṣṭenānumānena sādhyete yasmānmahadādiliṅgaṃ triguṇam / yasyedaṃ triguṇaṃ kāryaṃ tatpradhānamiti / yataścātenaṃ cetanamivābhāti ato 'nyo 'dhiṣṭhātā puruṣa iti / vyaktaṃ pratyakṣasādhyam / tasmādapi cāsiddhaṃ parokṣamāptāgamāt siddhaṃ yathendro devarājaḥ uttarāḥ kuravaḥ svarge 'psarasa iti parokṣamāptavacanāt siddham // 6 //
children.translated_text: Through inference from general observation (<s>sāmānyato dṛṣṭa</s>), the establishment of things beyond the senses — things that transcend the senses — [is achieved]. <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) and <s>Puruṣa</s> (consciousness), being beyond the senses, are established through inference from general observation. Since <s>Mahat</s> (the Great) and the rest constituting the <s>liṅga</s> (manifest indicator) are constituted of three <s>guṇas</s>, that of which this three-<s>guṇa</s> [manifest] is the effect is <s>Pradhāna</s>. And since the non-sentient appears as if sentient, there must be another controller — namely <s>Puruṣa</s>. The manifest is established by perception. 'And what is not established even thereby — that which is remote — is established through reliable scripture' — as for instance, <s>Indra</s> is the king of the gods, the Northern <s>Kurus</s> exist, in heaven there are <s>Apsarases</s> — the remote is established through reliable testimony. // 6 //

children.text: atra kaścidāha pradhānaḥ puruṣo vā nopalabhyate yaśca nopalabhyate loke tannāsti tasmāttāvapi na staḥ / yathā dvitīyaṃ śirastṛtīyo bāhuriti / taducyate / atra satāmapyarthānāmaṣṭadhopalabdhirna bhavati tadyathā /
children.translated_text: Here someone objects: <s>Pradhāna</s> or <s>Puruṣa</s> is not perceived; and what is not perceived in the world does not exist; therefore those two do not exist either — just as a second head or a third arm [do not exist]. To this it is replied: Here, even for things that exist, there are eight [reasons for] non-perception, namely:
Because of excessive distance, proximity, impairment of the senses, inattention of the mind,
because of subtlety, concealment, being overpowered, and admixture with what is similar. || 7 ||

children.text: iha satāmapyarthānāmatidūrādanupalabdhirdṛṣṭā / yathā deśāntarasthānāṃ caitramaitraviṣṇumitrāṇām / sāmīpyādyathā cakṣuṣo 'ñjanānupalabdhiḥ / indriyābhighātādyathā badhirāndhayoḥ śabdarūpānupalabdhiḥ / mano 'navasthānādyathā vyagracittaḥ samyakkathitamapi nāvadhārayati / saukṣmyādyathā dhūmoṣmajalanīhāraparamāṇavo gaganagatā nopalabhyante / vyavadhānādyathā kuḍyena pihitaṃ vastu nopalabhyate / abhibhavādyathā sūryatejasābhibhūtā grahanakṣatratārakādayo nopalabhyante / samānābhihārādyathā mudgarāśau mudgaḥ kṣiptaḥ kuvalayāmalakamadhye kuvalayāmalake kṣipte kapotamadhye kapoto nopalabhyate sanānadravyamadhyāhṛtatvāt / evamaṣṭadhānupalabdhiḥ satāmarthānāmiha dṛṣṭā // 7 //
children.translated_text: Here, non-perception of things that exist is observed due to excessive distance — as of persons named <s>Caitra</s>, <s>Maitra</s>, and <s>Viṣṇumitra</s> residing in another place. Due to proximity — as the non-perception of collyrium applied to the eye. Due to impairment of the senses — as the non-perception of sound and form by the deaf and blind. Due to inattention of the mind — as when one who is distracted does not grasp even what is properly spoken. Due to subtlety — as particles of smoke, steam, water-mist, and atoms in the sky are not perceived. Due to concealment — as an object hidden behind a wall is not perceived. Due to being overpowered — as the planets, constellations, and stars are not perceived when overpowered by the radiance of the sun. Due to admixture with what is similar — as lentils

children.text: evaṃ cāsti kimabhyupagamyate pradhānapuruṣayorapyetayorvānupalabdhiḥ kena hetunā kena copalabdhistaducyate /
children.translated_text: If this is so, what is maintained — that <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> also have non-perception? By what cause? And how is their apprehension [established]? To this it is replied:
Because of subtlety, the non-perception of that [<s>Pradhāna</s>]; not because of non-existence; its apprehension is through [its] effects.

children.text: mahadādi tacca kāryaṃ prakṛtivirūpaṃ svarūpaṃ ca || 8 ||
children.translated_text: The effect is <s>Mahat</s> (the Great) and the rest; and that effect is both different from <s>Prakṛti</s> in form and similar in form. || 8 ||

children.text: saukṣmyāttadanupalabdhiḥ pradhānasyetyarthaḥ / pradhānaṃ saukṣmyānnopalabhyate yathākāśe dhūmoṣmajalanīhāraparamāṇavaḥ santo 'pi nopalabhyante / kathaṃ tarhi tadupalabdhiḥ / kāryatastadupalabdhiḥ / kāryaṇa dṛṣṭvā kāraṇamanumīyate / asti pradhānaṃ kāraṇaṃ yasyedaṃ kāryam / buddhirahaṃkārapañcatanmātrāṇi ekādaśendriyāṇi pañcamahābhūtāni eva tatkāryam / tacca kāryaṃ prakṛtivirūpam / prakṛtiḥ pradhānaṃ tasya virūpaṃ prakṛterasadṛśaṃ svarūpaṃ ca samānarūpaṃ ca tathā loke 'pi pitustulya eva putro bhavatyatulyaśca / yena hetunā tulyamatulyaṃ tadupariṣṭādvakṣyāmaḥ // 8 //
children.translated_text: Because of subtlety, the non-perception of that — meaning of <s>Pradhāna</s>. <s>Pradhāna</s> is not perceived because of subtlety, just as particles of smoke, steam, water-mist, and atoms in the sky, though existing, are not perceived. How then is its apprehension [possible]? Its apprehension is through [its] effects. By seeing the effect, the cause is inferred: <s>Pradhāna</s> exists as the cause of which this is the effect — <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-sense), the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements), the eleven <s>indriyas</s> (sense organs), and the five <s>mahābhūtas</s> (gross elements) — these are its effects. And that effect is different from <s>Prakṛti</s> in form — <s>Prakṛti</s> is <s>Pradhāna</s>; its 'different form' means dissimilar to <s>Prakṛti</s>. And it is also 'similar in form' — having the same form. So too in the world, a son is indeed similar to the father.

children.text: yadidaṃ mahadādikāryaṃ tatkiṃ pradhāne sadutādahosvidasadācāryavipratipatterayaṃ saṃśayaḥ / yato 'tra sāṃkhyadarśane satkāryaṃ bauddhādīnāmasatkāryam / yadi sadasanna bhavatyasatsanna bhavatīti vipratiṣedhastatrāha /
children.translated_text: Now, does this effect beginning with <s>Mahat</s> exist in <s>Pradhāna</s> [before its production], or does it not exist? This doubt arises because of the disagreement among teachers — since in the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> system the effect pre-exists [in the cause] (<s>satkāryavāda</s>), while for the Buddhists and others the effect does not pre-exist (<s>asatkāryavāda</s>). If it is [argued that the effect being both] existent and non-existent does not arise, and a non-existent [effect] does not arise — to resolve this contradiction he says:
Because the non-existent cannot be produced; because a material cause is selected; because not everything [is produced from everything];
because the capable [cause] produces what it is capable [of producing]; and because of the nature of the cause — therefore the effect pre-exists [in the cause] (<s>satkārya</s>). || 9 ||

children.text: asadakaraṇānna sadasato 'karaṇaṃ tasmātsatkāryaṃ ihaloke 'satkaraṇaṃ nāsti yathā sikatābhyastailotpattistasmātsataḥ karaṇādasti prāgu(tpa)pteḥ / pradhāne vyaktamataḥ satkāryam / kiṃ cānyadupādānagrahaṇādupādānaṃ kāraṇaṃ tasya grahaṇādihaloke yo yenārthī sa tadupādānagrahaṇaṃ karoti dadhyarthī kṣīrasya na tu jalasya tasmāt satkāryam / itaśca sarvasambhavābhāvāt sarvasya sarvatrasambhavo nāsti yathā suvarṇasya rajatādau tṛṇapāṃśusikatāsu tasmāt sarvasambhavābhāvāt satkāryam / itaśaca śaktasya śakyakaraṇāt / iha kulālaḥ śakto mṛddaṇḍacakracīvararajjunīrādikaraṇopakaraṇaṃ vā śakyameva ghaṭāṃ mṛtpiṇḍādutpādayati tasmāt satkāryam / itaśca kāraṇabhāvācca satkāryam / kāraṇaṃ yallakṣaṇaṃ tallakṣaṇameva kāryameva yathā yavebhyo 'pi yavāḥ vrīhībhyo vrīhayaḥ yadāsatkāryaṃ syāttataḥ kodravebhyaḥ śālayaḥ syurna ca santīti tasmāt satkāryam / evaṃ pañcabhirhetubhiḥ pradhāne mahadādiliṅgamasti tasmātsata utpattirnāsata iti // 9 //
children.translated_text: 'Because the non-existent cannot be produced' — it is not the case that the existent is not produced; therefore the effect pre-exists. In this world, the production of the non-existent does not occur — for example, the production of oil from sand [is impossible]; therefore, since [there is] production from what exists, [the effect] exists prior to [its] production. The manifest exists in <s>Pradhāna</s>; hence the effect pre-exists. Moreover, 'because a material cause is selected' — the <s>upādāna</s> (material cause) is the cause; its 'selection' means: in this world, whoever desires something selects the appropriate material cause — one desiring yogurt selects milk, not water; therefore the effect pre-exists. Furthermore, 'because not everything [is produced from everything]' — it is not the case that everything arises from everywhere; for example, gold does not [arise] from silver, grass, dust, or sand; therefore, because of the impossibility of everything [arising from everything], the effect pre-exists. Furthermore, 'because the capable [cause] produces what it is capable [of producing]' — here, a potter, being capable, with instruments such as earth, staff, wheel, cloth, rope, water, and the like, produces a pot from a lump of clay that is capable [of being so shaped]; therefore the effect pre-exists. Furthermore, 'because of the nature of the cause' — the effect has the very same characteristics as the cause; just as from barley grains come barley, from rice grains come rice; if the effect did not pre-exist, then rice would arise from millet — but it does not; therefore the effect pre-exists. Thus, by these five reasons, the <s>liṅga</s> (manifest) beginning with <s>Mahat</s> exists in <s>Pradhāna</s>; therefore production is from what exists, not from what does not exist. // 9 //
Regarding what was stated — that [the effect] is both 'different in form from <s>Prakṛti</s>' and 'similar in form' — how is this? It is stated:
The <s>liṅga</s> (manifest) has a cause, is non-eternal, non-pervasive, active, manifold, dependent,
has parts, and is subordinate — [such is] the manifest; the unmanifest is the opposite. || 10 ||

children.text: vyaktaṃ mahadādikāryyaṃ hetumaditi heturasyāsti hetumat / upādānaṃ hetuḥ kāraṇaṃ nimittamiti paryāyāḥ / vyaktasya pradhānaṃ heturasti ato hetumadvyaktaṃ bhūtaparyyantaṃ hetumadbuddhimattvaṃ pradhānena hetumānahaṃkāro buddhyā pañcatanmātrāṇi ekādaśendriyāṇi hetumantyahaṃkāreṇa / ākāśaṃ śabdatanmātreṇa hetumat / vāyuḥ sparśatanmātreṇa hetumān / tejo rūpatanmātreṇa hetumat / āpo rasatanmātreṇa hetumatyaḥ / pṛthivī gandhatanmātrena hetumatī / evaṃ bhūtaparyyantaṃ vyaktaṃ hetumat / kiṃ cānyadanityaṃ yasmādanyasmādutpadyate yathā mṛtpiṇḍādutpadyate ghaṭaḥ sa cānityaḥ / kiṃ cāvyāpyasarvvagamityarthaḥ yathā pradhānapuruṣau sarvvagatau naiva vyaktam / kiṃcānyat sakriyaṃ saṃsārakāle saṃsarati trayodaśavidhena karaṇena saṃyuktaṃ sūkṣmaṃ śarīramāśritya saṃsarati tasmāt sakriyam / kiṃcānyadanekaṃ buddhirahaṃkāraḥ pañcatanmātrānyekādaśendriyāṇi ca pañcamahābhūtāni pañcatanmātrāśritāni / kiṃca liṅgaṃ layayuktaṃ layakāle pañcamahābhūtāni tanmātreṣu līyante tānyekādaśendriyaiḥ sahāhaṃkāre sa ca buddhau sā ca pradhāne layaṃ yātīti / tathā sāvayavaṃ avayavāḥ śabdasparśarasarūpagandhāḥ taiḥ saha / kiṃca paratantraṃ nātmanaḥ prabhavati yathā pradhānatantrā buddhiḥ buddhitantro 'haṃkāraḥ ahaṃkāratantrāṇi tanmātrāṇīndriyāṇi ca tanmātratantrāṇi pañcamahābhūtāni ca / evaṃ paratantraṃ parāyattaṃ vyākhyātaṃ vyaktam / atho 'vyaktaṃ vyākhyāmaḥ / viparītamavyaktam / etaireva guṇairyathoktairviparītamavyaktaṃ hetumadvyaktamuktam / nahi pradhānāt paraṃ kiñcidasti yataḥ pradhānasyānutpattiḥ tasmādahetumadavyaktam / tathānityaṃ ca vyaktaṃ nityamavyaktamanutpādyatvāt nahi bhūtāni kutaścidutpadyanteti pradhānam / kiṃ cāvyāpi vyaktaṃ vyāpi pradhānaṃ kāryyaṃ syāt / tathā vyaktaṃ liṅgamaliṅgamavyaktaṃ nityatvānmahadādi liṅgaṃ pralayakāle parasparaṃ pralīyate naivaṃ pradhānaṃ tasmādaliṅgaṃ pradhānam / tathā sāvayavaṃ vyaktaṃ niravayavamavyaktaṃ nahi śabdasparśarasarūpagandhāḥ pradhāne santi / tathā paratantraṃ vyaktaṃ svatantramavyaktaṃ prabhavatyātmanaḥ // 10 //
children.translated_text: The manifest — the effect beginning with <s>Mahat</s> — 'has a cause' means it has a cause (<s>hetu</s>). <s>Upādāna</s> (material cause), <s>hetu</s> (cause), <s>kāraṇa</s> (instrument), and <s>nimitta</s> (occasion) are synonyms. The manifest has <s>Pradhāna</s> as its cause; hence the manifest 'has a cause' — up to the [gross] elements, all have causes: <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect) has <s>Pradhāna</s> as cause; <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-sense) has <s>Buddhi</s> as cause; the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) and eleven <s>indriyas</s> (sense organs) have <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> as cause; <s>ākāśa</s> (space) has the <s>śabda-tanmātra</s> (sound-subtle-element) as cause; <s>vāyu</s> (air) has the <s>sparśa-tanmātra</s> (touch-subtle-element) as cause; <s>tejas</s> (fire) has the <s>rūpa-tanmātra</s> (form-subtle-element) as cause; <s>āpas</s> (water) has the <s>rasa-tanmātra</s> (taste-subtle-element) as cause;

children.text: evaṃ vyaktāvyaktayorvaidharmmyamuktaṃ sādharmmyamucyate yaduktaṃ sarūpaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Thus the dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmya</s>) of the manifest and the unmanifest has been stated; now their similarity (<s>sādharmya</s>) is stated — referring to what was said: 'similar in form also.'
Constituted of three <s>guṇas</s>, undifferentiated, objective, common, non-sentient, productive —

children.text: vyaktaṃ tathā pradhānaṃ tadviparītastathā ca pumān || 11 ||
children.translated_text: so is the manifest; and so too is <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter); <s>Puruṣa</s> (consciousness) is the opposite of that. || 11 ||

children.text: triguṇaṃ vyaktaṃ sattvarajastamāṃsi trayo guṇā yasyeti / aviveki vyaktaṃ na viveko 'syāstīti / idaṃ vyaktamime guṇā iti na vivekakarttuṃ yāti ayaṃ gaurayamaśva iti yathā ye guṇāstadvyaktaṃ yadvyaktaṃ te ca guṇā iti / tathā viṣayo vyaktaṃ bhojyamityarthaḥ sarvapuruṣāṇāṃ viṣayabhūtatvāt / tathā sāmānyaṃ vyaktaṃ mūlyadāsīvat sarvasādhāraṇatvāt / acetanaṃ vyaktaṃ sukhaduḥkhamohānna cetayatītyarthaḥ / tathā prasavadharmi vyaktaṃ tadyathā buddherahaṃkāraḥ prasūyate tasmāt pañcatanmātrāṇi ekādaśendriyāṇi ca prasūyante tanmātrebhyaḥ pañcamahābhūtāni / evamete vyaktadharmāḥ prasavadharmāntā uktā evamebhiravyaktaṃ sarūpaṃ yathā vyaktaṃ tathā pradhānamiti / tatra triguṇaṃ vyaktamavyaktamapi triguṇaṃ yasyaitanmahadādi kāryaṃ triguṇam / iha yadātmakaṃ kāraṇaṃ tadātmakaṃ kāryamiti yathā kṛṣṇatantukṛtaḥ kṛṣṇa eva paṭo bhavati / tathāviveki vyaktaṃ pradhānamapi guṇairna bhidyate anye guṇā anyat pradhānameva vivaktuṃ na yāti tadaviveki pradhānam / tathā viṣayo vyaktaṃ pradhānamapi sarvapuruṣaviṣayabhūtatvādviṣaya iti / tathā sāmānyaṃ vyaktaṃ pradhānamapi sarvasādhāraṇatvāt / tathācetanaṃ vyaktaṃ pradhānamapi sukhaduḥkhamohānna cetayatīti kathamanumīyata iha hyacetanānmṛtpiṇḍādacetano ghaṭā utpadyate / evaṃ pradhānamapi vyākhyātam / idānīṃ tadviparītastathā pumānityetadvyākhyāyate / sadviparītastābhyāṃ vyaktāvyaktābhyāṃ viparītaḥ pumān / tadyathā triguṇaṃ vyaktamavyaktaṃ cāguṇaḥ puruṣaḥ / aviveki vyaktamavyaktaṃ ca vivekī puruṣaḥ / tathā viṣayo vyaktamavyaktaṃ cāviṣayaḥ puruṣaḥ / tathā sāmānyaṃ vyaktamavyaktaṃ cāsāmānyaḥ puruṣaḥ / acetanaṃ vyaktamavyaktaṃ ca cetanaḥ puruṣaḥ sukhaduḥkhamohāṃścetayati saṃjānīte tasmāccetanaḥ puruṣa iti / prasavadharmi vyaktaṃ pradhānaṃ cāprasavadharmī puruṣo nahi kiñcit puruṣāt prasūyate / tasmāduktaṃ tadviparītaḥ pumāniti / taduktaṃ tathā ca pumāniti / tat pūrvasyāmāryāyāṃ pradhānamahetumadyathā vyākhyātaṃ tathā ca pumān tadyathā hetumadananityamityādi vyaktaṃ tadviparītamavyaktaṃ tatra hetumadvyaktamahetumat pradhānaṃ tathā ca pumānahetumānanutpādyatvāt / anityaṃ vyaktaṃ nityaṃ pradhānaṃ tathā ca nityaḥ pumān / akriyaḥ sarvagatatvādeva / anekaṃ vyaktamekamavyaktaṃ tathā pumānyapyekaḥ / āśritaṃ vyaktamanāśritamavyaktaṃ tathā ca pumānanāśritaḥ / liṅgaṃ vyaktamaliṅgaṃ pradhānaṃ tathā ca pumānapyaliṅgaḥ / na kvacillīyata iti / sāvayavaṃ vyaktaṃ niravayavamavyaktaṃ tathā ca pumān niravayavaḥ / nahi puruṣe śabdādayo 'vayavāḥ santi / kiṃca paratantraṃ vyaktaṃ svatantramavyaktaṃ tathā ca pumānapi svatantraḥ / ātmanaḥ prabhavatītyarthaḥ / evametadavyaktapuruṣayoḥ sādharmyaṃ vyākhyātaṃ pūrvasyāmāryāyām / vyaktapradhānayoḥ sādharmyaṃ puruṣasya vaidharmyaṃ ca triguṇamavivekītyādi prakṛtyāryāyāṃ vyākhyātam // 11 //
children.translated_text: The manifest is 'constituted of three <s>guṇas</s>' — <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> are the three <s>guṇas</s> of which it is possessed. It is 'undifferentiated' (<s>aviveki</s>) — meaning the manifest has no [absolute] differentiation [from the <s>guṇas</s>]: one cannot discriminate 'this is the manifest, these are the <s>guṇas</s>' [as separate things], just as one says 'this is a cow, this is a horse' [as distinct objects], but [here] the <s>guṇas</s> are the manifest and the manifest is the <s>guṇas</s>. Likewise, the manifest is an 'object' (<s>viṣaya</s>) — meaning it is something to be experienced (<s>bhojya</s>), because it exists as an object for all <s>Puruṣas</s>. Likewise, the manifest is 'common' (<s>sāmānya</s>) — like a publicly purchased slave-woman, because it is common to all. The manifest is 'non-sentient' (<s>acetana</s>) — meaning it does not experience happiness, suffering, or delusion.

children.text: tatra yaduktaṃ triguṇamiti vyaktamavyaktaṃ ca tat ke te guṇā iti tat svarūpapratipādanāyedamāha /
children.translated_text: Therein, regarding what was stated — that the manifest and the unmanifest are 'constituted of three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities)' — what are those <s>guṇas</s>? To establish their essential nature, he says:
Having the nature of pleasure, displeasure, and despondency; having the purposes of illumination, activity, and restraint;
[and characterized by] mutual dominance, support, generation, coupling, and functioning — [such are] the <s>guṇas</s>. || 12 ||

children.text: prītyātmakā aprītyātmakāḥ viṣādātmakāśca guṇāḥ sattvarajastamāṃsītyarthaḥ / tatra prītyātmakaṃ sattvaṃ prītiḥ sukhaṃ tadātmakamiti / aprītyātmakaṃ rajaḥ / viṣādātmakaṃ tamaḥ / viṣādo mohaḥ / tathā prakāśapravṛtti niyamārthāḥ / arthaḥ śabdaḥ sāmarthyavācī prakāśārthaṃ sattvaṃ prakāśasamarthamityarthaḥ / pravṛttyarthaṃ rajo niyamārthaṃ tamaḥ sthitau samarthamityarthaḥ prakāśakriyāsthitiśīlā guṇā iti / tathānyonyābhibhavāśrayajananamithunavṛttayaśca / anyonyābhibhavāḥ anyonyāśrayāḥ anyonyajananāḥ anyonyamithunāḥ anyonyavṛttayaśca te tathoktāḥ / anyonyābhibhavā iti anyonyaṃ parasparamabhibhavantīti prītyaprītyādibhirdharmmairāvirbhavanti yathā yadā sattvamutkaṭaṃ bhavati tadā rajastamasī aprītipravṛttidharmmeṇa yadā tamastadā sattvarajasī viṣādasthityātmakena iti / tathānyonyāśrayāśca dvyaṇukavadguṇāḥ / anyonyajananāḥ yathā mṛtpiṇḍo ghaṭaṃ janayati / tathānyonyamithunāśca yathā strīpuṃsau anyonyamithunau tathā guṇāḥ / uktaṃ ca /
rajaso mithunaṃ sattvaṃ sattvasya mithunaṃ rajaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Sattva</s> is the partner of <s>rajas</s>; <s>rajas</s> is the partner of <s>sattva</s>;
<s>tamas</s> is said to be the partner of both <s>sattva</s> and <s>rajas</s>.

The <s>guṇas</s> having the nature of pleasure, displeasure, and despondency are <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> — this is the meaning. Therein, <s>sattva</s> has the nature of pleasure — pleasure is happiness, and [<s>sattva</s>] has that as its nature. <s>Rajas</s> has the nature of displeasure. <s>Tamas</s> has the nature of despondency; despondency is delusion. Likewise, they have the purposes of illumination, activity, and restraint. '<s>Artha</s>' (purpose) here is a word denoting capability — <s>sattva</s> has illumination as its purpose, meaning it is capable of illumination. <s>Rajas</s> has activity as its purpose; <s>tamas</s> has restraint as its purpose, meaning it is capable of keeping [things] stationary. The <s>guṇas</s> have the dispositions of illumination, activity, and stasis. And likewise they are characterized by mutual dominance, support, generation, coupling, and functioning — they mutually dominate one another, mutually support one another, mutually generate one another, mutually couple with one another, and mutually function in relation to one another. They are said to be thus. 'Mutual dominance' — they dominate each other reciprocally; they manifest through their respective properties of pleasure, displeasure, and so on. Namely, when <s>sattva</s> becomes predominant, then <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> [are dominated] through the properties of displeasure and activity; when <s>tamas</s> [is predominant], then <s>sattva</s> and <s>rajas</s> [are dominated] through the properties of despondency and stasis — and so on. And likewise they mutually support one another, like a dyad of atoms: so do the <s>guṇas</s>. They mutually generate one another, just as a lump of clay generates a pot. And they are mutual partners, just as a woman and a man are partners to each other, so too are the <s>guṇas</s>. And it is stated:

children.text: parasparasahāyā ityarthaḥ / anyonyavṛttayaśca parasparaṃ varttante guṇāḥ guṇeṣu varttanta iti vacanāt / yathā surūpā suśīlā strī sarvvasukhahetuḥ sapatnīnāṃ saiva duḥkhahetuḥ saiva rāgiṇāṃ mohaṃ janayati eva satvaṃ rajastamasorvṛttiheturyathā rājā sadodyuktaḥ prajāpālane duṣṭanigrahe śiṣṭānāṃ sukhamutpādayati duṣṭānāṃ duḥkhaṃ mohaṃ ca evaṃ rajassattvatamasorvṛttiṃ janayati / tathā tamaḥ svarūpeṇāvaraṇātmakena sattvarajasorvṛttiṃ janayati yathā meghāḥ khamāvṛtya jagataḥ sukhamutpādayanti te vṛṣṭyā karṣukāṇāṃ karṣaṇodyogaṃ janayanti virahiṇāṃ mohamevamanyonyavṛttayo guṇāḥ // 12 //
children.translated_text: The meaning is that they are mutual helpers. And they mutually function in relation to one another — the <s>guṇas</s> operate reciprocally among themselves, as stated in the saying 'the <s>guṇas</s> operate among the <s>guṇas</s>.' Just as a beautiful and virtuous woman is the cause of all happiness, [yet] for her co-wives she is the very cause of suffering, and for the lustful she generates delusion — so <s>sattva</s> is the cause of the functioning of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>. Just as a king, constantly engaged in the protection of his subjects and the punishment of the wicked, produces happiness for the virtuous and suffering and delusion for the wicked — so <s>rajas</s> generates the functioning of <s>sattva</s> and <s>tamas</s>. Likewise, <s>tamas</s>, through its own nature of obstruction, generates the functioning of <s>sattva</s> and <s>rajas</s>. Just as clouds, covering the sky, produce happiness for the world, and through rain generate the activity of plowing for farmers, and delusion for those separated [from their beloveds] — so the <s>guṇas</s> mutually function [in relation to each other]. // 12 //
Moreover:

children.text: sattvaṃ laghu prakāśakamiṣṭamupaṣṭambhakaṃ calaṃ ca rajaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Sattva</s> is light and illuminating; <s>rajas</s> is stimulating and restless;
<s>tamas</s> is heavy and obstructing indeed; like a lamp, their functioning is for a [common] purpose. || 13 ||

children.text: sattvaṃ laghu prakāśakaṃ ca yadā sattvamutkaṭaṃ bhavati tadā laghūnyaṅgāni buddhiprakāśaśca prasannatendriyāṇāṃ bhavati / upaṣṭambhakaṃ calaṃ ca rajaḥ upaṣṭambhātītyupaṣṭambhakamudyotakaṃ yathā vṛṣo vṛṣadarśane utkaṭamupaṣṭambhaṃ karoti eva rajovṛttiḥ / tathā rajaśca calaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ rajovṛttiścalacitto bhavati / guru varaṇamekameva tamaḥ yadā tama utkaṭaṃ bhavati tadā gurūṇyaṅgānyāvṛtānīndriyāṇi bhavanti svārthāsamarthāni / atrāha yadi guṇāḥ parasparaṃ viruddhāḥ svamatenaiva kamarthaṃ niṣpādayanti tarhi kathaṃ pradīpavaccārthato vṛttiḥ pradīpena tulyaṃ pradīpavadarthataḥ sādhanā vṛttiriṣṭā yathā pradīpaḥ parasparaviruddhatailāgnivarttisaṃyogādarthaprakāśān janayati evaṃ sattvarajastamāṃsi parasparaṃ viruddhānyarthaṃ niṣpādayanti // 13 //
children.translated_text: <s>Sattva</s> is light and illuminating — when <s>sattva</s> becomes predominant, then the limbs become light and the illumination of the intellect and the clarity of the senses arise. <s>Rajas</s> is stimulating and restless — that which stimulates is 'stimulating,' meaning it activates; just as a bull, upon seeing another bull, vigorously stimulates [itself to action] — so is the functioning of <s>rajas</s>. And <s>rajas</s> is observed to be restless — one in whom the functioning of <s>rajas</s> [predominates] becomes restless-minded. <s>Tamas</s> is heavy and obstructing alone — when <s>tamas</s> becomes predominant, then the limbs become heavy and the senses become obstructed, incapable of their proper functions. Here the objection arises: if the <s>guṇas</s> are mutually opposed, how do they accomplish a purpose even by their own doctrine? The answer: 'Like a lamp, their functioning is for a [common] purpose' — like a lamp, functioning for a purpose; just as a lamp, from the combination of mutually opposed oil, fire, and wick, produces the illumination of objects — so <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>, though mutually opposed, accomplish a [common] purpose. // 13 //

children.text: antarapraśno bhavati triguṇamaviveki viṣaya ityādi pradhānaṃ vyaktaṃ ca vyākhyātaṃ tatra pradhānamupalabhyamānaṃ mahadādi ca triguṇamavivekyādīti ca kathamavagamyate tatrāha /
children.translated_text: An intermediate question arises: the <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter), described as 'constituted of three <s>guṇas</s>, undifferentiated,' and so forth, and the manifest (<s>vyakta</s>) have been explained. Now, how is it ascertained that <s>Pradhāna</s> is imperceptible, while <s>Mahat</s> (the Great) and the rest are constituted of three <s>guṇas</s>, undifferentiated, and so on? To this he says:
The [existence of] the undifferentiated [<s>Pradhāna</s>] and the rest is established because of its being constituted of three <s>guṇas</s>, and because of the absence of a contrary [state];
because the effect has the nature of the <s>guṇas</s> of the cause — the unmanifest too is established. || 14 ||

children.text: yo 'yamavivekyādirguṇaḥ sa traiguṇyānmahadādau 'vyaktenāyaṃ siddhyati / atrocyate tadviparyayābhāvāttasya viparyayastadviparyayastasyābhāvastadviparyayābhāvastasmāt siddhamavyaktam / yathā yatraiva tantavastatraiva paṭaḥ / anye tantavo 'nyaḥ paṭo na kutastadviparyayābhāvāt / evaṃ vyaktāvyaktasampanno bhavati dūraṃ pradhānamāsannaṃ vyaktaṃ yo vyaktaṃ paśyati sa pradhānamapi paśyati tadviparyayābhāvāt / itaścāvyaktaṃ siddhaṃ kāraṇaguṇātmakatvāt kāryasya / loke yadātmakaṃ kāraṇaṃ tadātmakaṃ kāryamapi tathā kṛṣṇebhyastantubhyaḥ kṛṣṇa eva paṭo bhavati / evaṃ mahadādiliṅgamavivekiviṣayaḥ sāmānyacetanaṃ prasavadharmi yadātmakaṃ liṅgaṃ tadātmakamavyaktamapi siddham // 14 //
children.translated_text: This quality of being undifferentiated and so forth is established in <s>Mahat</s> and the rest from [their] being constituted of three <s>guṇas</s>; the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) is established through this. Here it is stated: 'Because of the absence of a contrary [state]' — the contrary of that [<s>vyakta</s>] is the opposite of it (<s>tadviparyaya</s>); the absence of that contrary means the absence of a state opposite to [the <s>vyakta</s>]; therefore the unmanifest is established. Just as wherever the threads are, there too is the cloth — the threads are not separate and the cloth something else — why? Because of the absence of a contrary state. Thus, the manifest and unmanifest are connected — the <s>Pradhāna</s> is remote while the manifest is proximate; one who sees the manifest sees the <s>Pradhāna</s> too, because of the absence of a contrary state. Furthermore, the unmanifest is established because the effect has the nature of the <s>guṇas</s> of the cause. In the world, whatever nature the cause has, the effect has that same nature — just as from black threads, the cloth too is black. Thus, <s>Mahat</s> and the rest constituting the <s>liṅga</s> (manifest indicator) — being undifferentiated, having common sentience, endowed with the disposition of production — whatever nature the <s>liṅga</s> has, the unmanifest too is established as having that same nature. // 14 //

children.text: traiguṇyādavivekyādirvyakte siddhastadviparyayābhāvāt / evaṃ kāraṇaguṇātmakatvāt kāryasyāvyaktamapi siddhamityetanmithyā loke yannopalabhyate tannāsti evaṃ pradhānamapyasti kiṃ tu nopalabhyate /
children.translated_text: Since the undifferentiated and the rest are established in the manifest from its being constituted of three <s>guṇas</s>, and because of the absence of a contrary state, and because the effect has the nature of the <s>guṇas</s> of the cause — the unmanifest too is established — if you say this is false, [arguing that] in the world what is not perceived does not exist, [we reply:] just so, <s>Pradhāna</s> too exists, but is simply not perceived.
Because of the finitude of the differentiated [effects], because of homogeneity, because of [the effect] proceeding from potency,
because of the distinction between cause and effect, and because of the non-separation of the universal form — || 15 ||

children.text: kāraṇamastyavyaktamiti kriyākārakasambandhaḥ / bhedānāṃ parimāṇāloke yatra karttāsti tasya parimāṇaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yathā kulālaḥ parimitairmṛtpiṇḍaiḥ parimitāneva ghaṭān karoti evaṃ mahadapi mahadādiliṅgaṃ parimitaṃ bhedataḥ pradhānakāryamekā buddhireko 'haṃkāraḥ pañca tanmātrāṇi ekādaśendriyāṇi pañcatanmātrāṇi ekādaśendriyāṇi pañcamahābhūtānītyevaṃ bhedānāṃ parimāṇādasti pradhānaṃ kāraṇaṃ yadvyaktaṃ parimitamutpādayati /yadi pradhānaṃ na syāttadā niḥparimāṇamidaṃ vyaktamapi na syāt parimāṇācca bhedānāmasti pradhānaṃ yasmādvyaktamutpannam / tathā samanvayādiha loke prasiddhirdṛṣṭā yathā vratadhāriṇaṃ baṭuṃ dṛṣṭvā samanvayati nūnamasya pitarau brāhmaṇāviti evamidaṃ triguṇaṃ mahadādiliṅgaṃ dṛṣṭvā sādhayāmo 'sya yat kāraṇaṃ bhaviṣyatīti ataḥ samanvayādasti pradhānam / tathā śaktitaḥ pravṛtteśca iha yo yasmin śaktaḥ sa tasminnevārthe pravarttate yathā kulālo ghaṭāsya karaṇe samartho ghaṭameva karoti na paṭaṃ rathaṃ vā / tathāsti pradhānaṃ kāraṇaṃ kutaḥ kāraṇakāryavibhāgāt / karotīti kāraṇam / kriyata iti kāryam / kāraṇasya kāryasya ca vibhāgo yathā ghaṭo dadhimadhūdakapayasāṃ dhāraṇe samartho na tathā taktāraṇaṃ mṛtpiṇḍaḥ / mṛtpiṇḍo vā ghaṭaṃ niṣpādayati na caivaṃ ghaṭo mṛtpiṇḍam / evaṃ mahadādiliṅgaṃ dṛṣṭvānumīyate / asti vibhaktaṃ tat kāraṇaṃ yasya vibhāga idaṃ vyaktamiti / itaśca avibhāgādvaiśvarūpasya viśvaṃ jagat tasya rūpaṃ vyaktiḥ / viśvarūpasya bhāvo vaiśvarūpaṃ tasyāvibhāgādasti pradhānaṃ yasmātrailokyasya pañcānāṃ pṛthivyādīnāṃ mahābhūtānāṃ parasparaṃ vibhāgo nāsti mahābhūteṣvantarbhūtāstrayo lokā iti pṛthivyāpastejovāyurākāśamiti etāni pañcamahābhūtāni pralayakāle sṛṣṭikrameṇaivāvibhāgaṃ yānti tanmātreṣu pariṇāmiṣu tanmātrāṇyekādaśendriyāṇi cāhaṃkāre ahaṃkāro buddhau buddhiḥ pradhāne evaṃ trayo lokāḥ pralayakāle prakṛtāvavibhāgaṃ gacchanti tasmādavibhāgāt kṣīradadhivadvyaktāvyaktayoravyaktaṃ kāraṇam // 15 //
children.translated_text: The cause exists — [namely] the unmanifest — this is a relation of action and agent. 'Because of the finitude of the differentiated [effects]' — in the world, wherever there is an agent, its finitude is observed; just as a potter makes only a finite number of pots from a finite quantity of clay — so <s>Mahat</s> too, the <s>liṅga</s> beginning with <s>Mahat</s>, is finite in its differentiated [forms], being the effect of <s>Pradhāna</s>: one <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect), one <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-sense), five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements), eleven <s>indriyas</s> (sense organs), five <s>tanmātras</s>, eleven <s>indriyas</s>, five <s>mahābhūtas</s> (gross elements) — thus, because of the finitude of the differentiated [effects], there exists <s>Pradhāna</s> as the cause which produces a finite manifest. If <s>Pradhāna</s> did not exist, then this manifest, being without finite measure, would also not exist; but because of the finitude of the differentiated [effects], <s>Pradhāna</s> exists, from which the manifest has arisen. Likewise, 'because of homogeneity' — here in the world, inference is well established; just as, seeing a student observing religious vows, one infers: 'Surely his parents are Brahmins' — so, seeing this manifest constituted of three <s>guṇas</s> beginning with <s>Mahat</s>, we establish that its cause must exist; hence, because of homogeneity, <s>Pradhāna</s> exists. Likewise, 'because of [the effect] proceeding from potency' — here, whoever is capable in whatever [task] proceeds only in that very matter; just as a potter, being capable of making pots, makes only pots, not cloth or chariots. And <s>Pradhāna</s> as cause exists — why? 'Because of the distinction between cause and effect.' What makes is the cause; what is made is the effect. The distinction between cause and effect is as follows: a pot is capable of holding yogurt, honey, water, and milk, but a potter's wheel or a lump of clay is not so capable; and a lump of clay can produce a pot, but a pot cannot produce a lump of clay. Thus, observing the <s>liṅga</s> beginning with <s>Mahat</s>, one infers: there exists a distinct cause of which this manifest is the differentiation. Furthermore, 'because of the non-separation of the universal form' — the universe is the world; its form is its manifestation; the state of having universal form is 'universality of form'; because of the non-separation of that — <s>Pradhāna</s> exists; for the three worlds comprised of the five <s>mahābhūtas</s> (gross elements) beginning with earth are not mutually separate from each other; the three worlds are contained within the <s>mahābhūtas</s>. Earth, water, fire, air, and space — these five <s>mahābhūtas</s>, at the time of dissolution, merge back in the order of creation into the <s>tanmātras</s>; the <s>tanmātras</s> and the eleven <s>indriyas</s> [merge] into <s>Ahaṃkāra</s>; <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> into <s>Buddhi</s>; <s>Buddhi</s> into <s>Pradhāna</s>. Thus the three worlds, at the time of dissolution, merge without separation into <s>Prakṛti</s>; therefore, because of [this] non-separation — like milk and yogurt in the relationship of manifest and unmanifest — the unmanifest is the cause. // 15 //
And therefore:
The cause exists — [namely] the unmanifest; it operates because of [its being composed of] the three <s>guṇas</s> and because of combination;
through transformation, like water, because of the specific substrate of each respective <s>guṇa</s>. || 16 ||

children.text: avyaktaṃ prakhyātaṃ kāraṇamasti yasmānmahadādiliṅgaṃ pravarttate / triguṇataḥ triguṇāt sattvarajastamoguṇā yasmiṃstattriguṇaṃ tatkimuktaṃ bhavati sattvarajastamasāṃ sāmyāvasthā pradhānam / tathā samudayāt yathā gaṃgāśrotāṃsi triṇī rudramūrddhani patitāni ekaṃ sroto janayati evaṃ triguṇamavyaktamekaṃ vyaktaṃ janayati tathā vā tantavaḥ samuditāḥ paṭaṃ janayanti evamavyaktaṃ gunasamudayānmahadādi janayatīti triguṇataḥ samudayācca vyaktaṃ jagat pravarttate / yasmādekasmāt pradhānādvyaktaṃ tasmādekarūpeṇa bhavitavyam / naiṣa doṣaḥ pariṇāmataḥ salilavat pratipratiguṇāśrayaviśeṣādekasmāt pradhānāt trayo lokāḥ samutpannāstulyabhāvā na bhavanti devāḥ sukhena yuktā manuṣyā duḥkhena tiryañco mohena ekasmāt pradhānāt pravṛttaṃ vyaktaṃ pratipratiguṇāśrayaviśeṣāt pariṇamātaḥ salilavadbhavati / pratipratīti vīpsā / guṇānāmāśrayo guṇāśrayastadviśeṣastaṃ guṇāśrayaviśeṣaṃ pratinidhāya pratipratiguṇāśrayaviśeṣaṃ pariṇāmāt pravarttate vyaktaṃ yathā ākāśādekarasaṃ salilaṃ patitaṃ nānārūpātsaṃśleṣādbhidyate tadrasāntarairevamekasmāt pradhānāt pravṛttāstrayo lokā naikasvabhāvā bhavanti deveṣu sattvamutkaṭaṃ rajastamasī udāsīne tena te 'tyantasukhino manuṣyeṣu raja utkaṭaṃ bhavati sattvatamasī udāsīne tena te 'tyantaduḥkhino tiryakṣu tama utkaṭaṃ bhavati sattvajasī udāsīne tena te 'tyantamūḍhāḥ // 16 //
children.translated_text: The unmanifest is the well-known cause, since from it the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) beginning with <s>Mahat</s> proceeds. 'From the three <s>guṇas</s>' — that in which there are the three <s>guṇas</s> of <s>Sattva</s>, <s>Rajas</s>, and <s>Tamas</s> is called <s>triguṇa</s> (constituted of three guṇas). What is stated [by this]? The equilibrium of <s>Sattva</s>, <s>Rajas</s>, and <s>Tamas</s> is <s>Pradhāna</s> (the primary source). Likewise, 'because of combination' — just as the three streams of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, having fallen upon the head of <s>Rudra</s>, produce one stream, so the unmanifest, constituted of three <s>guṇas</s>, produces one manifest [world]. Or similarly, just as threads combined together produce a cloth, so the unmanifest, through the combination of <s>guṇas</s>, produces <s>Mahat</s> and the rest — thus from the three <s>guṇas</s> and from combination, the manifest world proceeds. Since the manifest [arises] from the one <s>Pradhāna</s>, it should be of one form. This is not a defect — through transformation, like water, because of the specific substrate of each respective <s>guṇa</s>: from the one <s>Pradhāna</s> the three worlds have arisen but are not of equal nature — the gods are endowed with pleasure, humans with pain, animals with delusion. The manifest that has proceeded from the one <s>Pradhāna</s> exists through transformation, like water, because of the specific substrate of each respective <s>guṇa</s>. 'Prati-prati' is a repetitive expression. The substrate of the <s>guṇas</s> is <s>guṇāśraya</s>; its particular [configuration] is <s>guṇāśrayaviśeṣa</s>; placing that <s>guṇāśrayaviśeṣa</s> [in each case], 'because of the specific substrate of each respective guṇa,' through transformation the manifest proceeds — just as water of one flavor, having fallen from the sky, becomes differentiated through contact with various [soils and minerals] by their different flavors, so the three worlds that have proceeded from the one <s>Pradhāna</s> are not of one nature: among the gods, <s>Sattva</s> is predominant while <s>Rajas</s> and <s>Tamas</s> are quiescent, therefore they are supremely happy; among humans, <s>Rajas</s> is predominant while <s>Sattva</s> and <s>Tamas</s> are quiescent, therefore they are supremely suffering; among animals, <s>Tamas</s> is predominant while <s>Sattva</s> and <s>Rajas</s> are quiescent, therefore they are supremely deluded. // 16 //
Thus, by the two verses [just given], the existence of <s>Pradhāna</s> is accepted. Next, in order to establish the existence of <s>Puruṣa</s>, [the author] says:
Because of the composite [nature of things serving] another's purpose, because of [the need for] the reversal of the three <s>guṇas</s> and the rest, because of [the need for] a controller,
<s>Puruṣa</s> exists — because of the nature of being an experiencer, and because of activity directed toward <s>Kaivalya</s> (liberation). || 17 ||

children.text: yaduktaṃ vyaktāvyaktavijñānānmokṣaḥ prāpyata iti tatra vyaktādanantaramavyaktaṃ pañcabhiḥ kāraṇairadhigatamavyaktavat puruṣo 'pi sūkṣmastasyādhunānumitāstitvaṃ pratikriyate / asti puruṣaḥ kasmāt saṃghātaparārthatvāt / yo 'yaṃ mahadādi saṃghātaḥ sa puruṣārtha ityanumīyate acetanatvāt paryaṅgavat / yathā paryaṅka pratyekaṃ gātrotpalakapādavaṭatūlīprachādanapaṭopadhānasaṃghataḥ parārtho nahi svārthaḥ paryaṅkasya nahi kiñcidapi gātrotpalādyavayavānāṃ parasparaṃ kṛtyamasti / ato 'vagamyate 'sti puruṣo yaḥ paryaṅke śete yasyārthaṃ paryaṅkastatparārthamidaṃ śarīraṃ pañcānāṃ mahābhūtānāṃ saṃghāto varttate 'sti puruṣo yasyedaṃ bhogyaśarīraṃ bhogyaṃ mahadādisaṃghātarūpaṃ samutpannamiti / itaścātmāsti triguṇādiviparyayāt yaduktaṃ pūrvasyāmāryāyāṃ trigunamavivekiviṣaya ityādi / tasmādviparyayādyenoktaṃ tadviparītastathā pumān / adhiṣṭhānādyatheha laṃghanalpavanadhāvanasamarthairaśvairyukto rathaḥ sārathinādhiṣṭhitaḥ pravarttate tathātmādhiṣṭhānāccharīramiti / tathā coktaṃ ṣaṣṭhitantre puruṣādhiṣṭhitaṃ pradhānaṃ pravarttate / ato 'styātmābhoktṛtvāt / yathā madhurāmlalavaṇakaṭutiktakaṣāyaṣaḍrasopabṛṃhitsya saṃyktasyānnasya sādhyate evaṃ mahadādiliṅgasya bhoktṛtvābhāvādasti sa ātmā yasyedaṃ bhogyaṃ śarīramti / itaśca kaivalyārthama pravṛtteśca kevalasya bhāvaḥ kaivalyaṃ tannimitaṃ yā ca pravṛttistasyāḥ svakaivalyārthaṃ pravṛtteḥ sakāśādanumīyate astyātmeti yato sarvo vidvānavidvāṃśca saṃsārasantānakṣayamicchati / evamebhirhetubhirastyātmā śarīrādvyatiriktaḥ // 17 //
children.translated_text: It was stated that liberation is attained from the knowledge of the manifest, the unmanifest, and the knower. There, the unmanifest has been ascertained next after the manifest by five reasons; like the unmanifest, <s>Puruṣa</s> too is subtle — now its existence is demonstrated by inference. <s>Puruṣa</s> exists — why? Because of the composite [nature of things serving] another's purpose. This composite [body] beginning with <s>Mahat</s> is inferred to serve the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>, since it is non-sentient, like a bed. Just as a bed — the composite of legs, a frame, feet, cotton, a covering cloth, and a pillow — serves another's purpose, for the bed has no purpose of its own, and none of the component parts such as legs and frame have any function for each other — from this it is understood: there exists a <s>Puruṣa</s> who sleeps on the bed, for whose sake the bed [exists]. For that [same] purpose this body, a composite of the five great elements, exists; there exists a <s>Puruṣa</s> for whom this body, which is to be experienced, [exists] — the object of experience having arisen in the form of the composite beginning with <s>Mahat</s>. Furthermore, the self exists because of the reversal of the three <s>guṇas</s> and the rest — as was stated in the previous verse, 'the unmanifest is constituted of three guṇas, undiscriminating,' and so on. From that reversal — by which it was stated [that <s>Pradhāna</s> has certain qualities], <s>Puruṣa</s> is the opposite of those. Because of [the need for] a controller — just as here a chariot yoked with horses capable of galloping, slow trotting, and running proceeds [only] when directed by a charioteer, so the body [proceeds] from the direction of the self. And so it is stated in the <s>Ṣaṣṭitantra</s>: '<s>Pradhāna</s> operates when directed by <s>Puruṣa</s>.' Therefore the self exists because of being an experiencer. Just as food, prepared and combined with the six flavors — sweet, sour, salty, pungent, bitter, and astringent — [requires an eater], so because the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) beginning with <s>Mahat</s> lacks the capacity of experiencing, there exists that self for whom this body is the object of enjoyment. And furthermore, because of activity directed toward <s>Kaivalya</s> — <s>Kaivalya</s> (isolation) is the state of being alone (<s>kevala</s>); that activity which has <s>Kaivalya</s> as its aim — from [the observation of] activity directed toward one's own liberation, it is inferred that the self exists, since every person, whether learned or unlearned, desires the cessation of the continuity of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration). Thus by these reasons the self exists as distinct from the body. // 17 //

children.text: atha sa kimekaha sarvaśarīre 'dhiṣṭhātā maṇirasanātmakasūtravat āhosvidbahava ātmānaḥ pratiśarīramadhiṣṭhātāra ityatrocyate /
children.translated_text: Now, is that [<s>Puruṣa</s>] one — a single controller in all bodies, like a thread of the nature of a jewel-string — or are the selves many, a controller in each body? To this it is said:
Because of the individual allotment of birth, death, and sense-organs, because of non-simultaneous activity,
the plurality of <s>Puruṣas</s> is established — and also because of the reversal of the three <s>guṇas</s>. || 18 ||

children.text: janma ca maraṇaṃ ca karaṇāni ca janmamaraṇakaraṇāni teṣāṃ pratiniyamāt pratyekaniyamādityarthaḥ / yadyeka eva ātmā syāttata ekasya janmani sarva eva jāyeran ekasya maraṇe sarve 'pi mriyeran ekasya karaṇavaikalye bādhiryāndhamūkatvakuṇatvakhaṃjatvalakṣaṇe sarve 'pi badhirāndhakuṇikhaṃjāḥ syurna caivaṃ bhavati tasmājjanmamaraṇakaraṇānāṃ pratiniyamāt puruṣabahutvaṃ siddham / itaścāyugapat pravṛtteśca yugapadekakālaṃ na yugapadayugapat pravarttanaṃ yasmādayugapaddharmādiṣu pravṛttirdṛśyate eke dharme pravṛttā anye 'dharme vairāgye 'nye jñāne 'nye pravṛttāḥ tasmādayugapat pravṛtteśca bahava iti siddham / kiñcānyattraiguṇyāviparyayāccaiva triguṇabhāvaviparyayācca puruṣabahutvaṃ siddham / yathā sāmānye janmani ekaḥ sāttvikaḥ sukhī / anyo rājaso duḥkhī / anyastāmaso mohavān / evaṃ traiguṇyaviparyayādbahutvaṃ siddhamiti // 18 //
children.translated_text: Birth and death and the sense-organs — these are 'birth-death-sense-organs'; because of their individual allotment, meaning because of the allotment to each individual. If there were only one self, then at the birth of one, all would be born; at the death of one, all would die; at the impairment of the sense-organs of one — characterized by deafness, blindness, muteness, lameness, and crippledness — all would be deaf, blind, lame, and crippled. But this is not so; therefore, because of the individual allotment of birth, death, and sense-organs, the plurality of <s>Puruṣas</s> is established. Furthermore, because of non-simultaneous activity — 'not simultaneous' means not at one time; 'non-simultaneous engagement' — since non-simultaneous engagement in <s>Dharma</s> and the rest is observed: some are engaged in <s>Dharma</s> (righteousness), others in <s>Adharma</s> (unrighteousness), others in <s>Vairāgya</s> (dispassion), others are engaged in <s>Jñāna</s> (knowledge) — therefore, because of non-simultaneous activity, it is established that [the selves] are many. Moreover, because of the reversal of the three <s>guṇas</s> as well — the plurality of <s>Puruṣas</s> is established because of the reversal of the condition of the three <s>guṇas</s>. Just as in a common birth, one person is <s>sāttvika</s> (of the nature of sattva) and happy, another is <s>rājasa</s> (of the nature of rajas) and suffering, another is <s>tāmasa</s> (of the nature of tamas) and deluded — thus because of the reversal of the three <s>guṇas</s>, plurality is established. // 18 //
<s>Puruṣa</s> is a non-agent — this is now stated:
And therefore, from that reversal, the witnesshood of this <s>Puruṣa</s> is established,
[as well as his] isolation, neutrality, status as seer, and non-agency. || 19 ||

children.text: tasmācca viparyāsāttasmācca yathoktatraiguṇyaviparyāsādviparyayānnirguṇaḥ puruṣo vivekī bhoktetyādiguṇānāṃ puruṣasya yo viparyāsa uktastasmāt sattvarajastamaḥsu karttṛbhūteṣu sākṣitvaṃ siddhaṃ puruṣasyeti yo 'yamadhikṛto bahutvaṃ prati / guṇā eva karttāraḥ pravarttante sākṣī na pravattate nāpi nivarttata eva / kiṃcānyat kaivalyaṃ kevalabhāvaḥ kaivalyamanyatvamityarthaḥ / triguṇebhyaḥ kevalaḥ / anyanmādhyasthyaṃ madhyasthabhāvaḥ parivrājakavat madhyasthaḥ puruṣaḥ / yathā kaścit parivrājako grāmīṇeṣu karṣaṇārtheṣu pravṛtteṣu kevalo madhyasthaḥ puruṣo 'pyevaṃ guṇeṣu varttamāneṣu na pravarttate / tasmāddraṣṭṛtvamakarttṛbhāvāśca yasmānmadhyasthastasmāddraṣṭā tasmādakarttā puruṣasteṣāṃ karmaṇāmiti sattvarajastamāṃsi trayo guṇāḥ karmakarttṛbhāvena pravarttante na puruṣa evaṃ puruṣasyāstitvaṃ ca siddham / yasmātkarttā puruṣastatkathamadhyavasāyaṃ karoti dharmaṃ kariṣyāmyadharmaṃ na kariṣyāmītyataḥ karttā bhavati na ca karttā puruṣa evamubhayātra doṣaḥ syāditi // 19 //
children.translated_text: 'And therefore, from that reversal' — and from the aforementioned reversal of the three <s>guṇas</s>, from the reversal: <s>Puruṣa</s> is without <s>guṇas</s>, discriminating, an experiencer, and so on — from the reversal of the <s>guṇas</s> with respect to <s>Puruṣa</s> that was stated, when <s>Sattva</s>, <s>Rajas</s>, and <s>Tamas</s> are the agents, the witnesshood of <s>Puruṣa</s> is established — [this refers to] the one who has been introduced [as subject] with respect to plurality. The <s>guṇas</s> alone are agents and engage [in activity]; the witness neither engages nor withdraws. Moreover, <s>Kaivalya</s> (isolation) is the state of being alone — <s>Kaivalya</s> means otherness, separateness. He is separate from the three <s>guṇas</s>. Another [quality is] <s>Mādhyasthya</s> (neutrality) — the state of being neutral; <s>Puruṣa</s> is neutral like a wandering ascetic. Just as a certain wandering ascetic, when the villagers are engaged in agricultural work, remains alone and neutral, so too <s>Puruṣa</s>, when the <s>guṇas</s> are operating, does not engage. Therefore, [there is] the status of being a seer and non-agency — since he is neutral, therefore he is a seer; therefore <s>Puruṣa</s> is a non-agent with respect to those actions. The three <s>guṇas</s> — <s>Sattva</s>, <s>Rajas</s>, and <s>Tamas</s> — engage as agents of action, not <s>Puruṣa</s>. Thus the existence of <s>Puruṣa</s> is also established. [Objection:] Since <s>Puruṣa</s> is [said to be] an agent, how then does he form the resolve 'I shall do <s>Dharma</s>, I shall not do <s>Adharma</s>'? Thus he becomes an agent, yet <s>Puruṣa</s> is not an agent — in both cases there would be a fault. // 19 //
To this it is said:
Therefore, from that conjunction, the non-sentient <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) [appears] as if sentient,
and though the <s>guṇas</s> are the agents, the uninvolved [<s>Puruṣa</s>] likewise appears as if he were the agent. || 20 ||

children.text: iha puruṣaścetanākṛt tena cetanāvabhāsaṃ yuktaṃ mahadādiliṅgaṃ cetanāvadiva bhavati yathā loke ghaṭāḥ śītasaṃyuktaḥ śīta uṣṇasaṃyukta uṣṇa evaṃ mahadādi liṅgaṃ tasya saṃyogāt puruṣasaṃyogāccetanāvadiva bhavati tasmādguṇā adhyavasāyaṃ kurvanti na puruṣaḥ / yadyapi loke puruṣaḥ karttā gaṃtetyādi prayujyate tathāpyakarttā puruṣaḥ kathaṃ guṇakarttṛtve ca tathā kartteva bhavatyudāsīno guṇānāṃ karttṛtve sati udāsīno 'pi puruṣaḥ kartteva bhavati na karttā / atra dṛṣṭānto bhavati yathācauraścauraiḥ saha gṛhītaścaura ityavagamyata evaṃ trayo guṇāḥ karttārastaiḥ saṃyuktaḥ puruṣo 'karttāpi karttā bhavati karttṛsaṃyogāt / evaṃ vyaktāvyaktajñānāṃ vibhāgo vikhyāto yadvibhāgānmokṣaprāptiriti // 20 //
children.translated_text: Here, <s>Puruṣa</s> is the source of consciousness; through him the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) beginning with <s>Mahat</s> is reasonably illumined with consciousness, appearing as if sentient — just as in the world a pot in contact with cold [becomes] cold, [or] in contact with heat [becomes] hot, so the <s>liṅga</s> beginning with <s>Mahat</s>, from that conjunction — from conjunction with <s>Puruṣa</s> — appears as if sentient. Therefore the <s>guṇas</s> perform the act of determination, not <s>Puruṣa</s>. Although in common usage <s>Puruṣa</s> is [called] an agent — 'he goes' and so forth — nevertheless <s>Puruṣa</s> is a non-agent. How [then is it that] though the <s>guṇas</s> are the agents, the uninvolved [<s>Puruṣa</s>] likewise appears as if he were the agent? When the <s>guṇas</s> are the agents, <s>Puruṣa</s>, though uninvolved, appears as if he were the agent, [but] he is not the agent. Here there is an illustration: just as a thief seized together with [other] thieves is taken to be a thief, so the three <s>guṇas</s> are the agents, and <s>Puruṣa</s>, conjoined with them, though a non-agent, becomes [regarded as] an agent because of conjunction with agents. Thus the distinction between the manifest, the unmanifest, and the knower is set forth, from the knowledge of which distinction liberation is attained. // 20 //

children.text: athaitayoḥ pradhānapuruṣayoḥ kiṃ hetuḥ saṃghāta ucyate /
children.translated_text: Now, what is the cause of the conjunction of these two — <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>? The union is stated:
For the purpose of <s>Puruṣa's</s> seeing, and for the purpose of <s>Pradhāna's</s> <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation/liberation),
the conjunction of both is like [that of] the lame and the blind; from that [conjunction] proceeds creation. || 21 ||

children.text: puruṣasya pradhānena saha saṃyogo darśanārthaṃ prakṛtiṃ mahadādikāryabhūtaparyantaṃ puruṣaḥ paśyati etadarthaṃ pradhānasyāpi puruṣeṇa saṃyogaḥ / kaivalyārthaṃ sa ca saṃyogaḥ paṅgvandhavadubhayorapi draṣṭavyaḥ yathā ekaḥ paṅgurekaścāndha etau dvāvapi gacchantau mahatā sāmarthyenāṭavyāṃ sārthasya stenakṛtādupaplavāt svabandhuparityakto daivāditaśceruśca svagatyā ca tau saṃyogamupayātau punastayoḥ svavacaso viśvastatvena saṃyogo gamanārthaṃ darśanārthaṃ ca bhavatyandhena paṃguḥ skandhamāropitaḥ evaṃ śarīrārūḍhapaṃgudarśitena mārgeṇāndho yāti paṃguścāndhaskandhārūḍhaḥ / evaṃ puruṣe darśanaśaktirasti paṃguvannakriyā pradhāne kriyāśaktirastyandhavannadarśanaśaktiḥ / yathā vānayoḥ paṃgvandhayoḥ kṛtārthayorvibhāgo bhaviṣyatīpsitasthānaprāptayorevaṃ pradhānamapi puruṣasya mokṣaṃ kṛtvā nivarttate puruṣo 'pi pradhānaṃ dṛṣṭvā kaivalyaṃ gacchati tayoḥ kṛtārthayorvibhāgo bhaviṣyati / kiṃ cānyat tatkṛtaḥ sargastena saṃyogena kṛtastatkṛtaḥ sargaḥ sṛṣṭiḥ / yathā strī puruṣasaṃyogāt sutotpattistataḥ pradhānapuruṣasaṃyogāt sargasyotpattiḥ // 21 //
children.translated_text: The conjunction of <s>Puruṣa</s> with <s>Pradhāna</s> is for the purpose of seeing — <s>Puruṣa</s> sees <s>Prakṛti</s>, the entire series of effects from <s>Mahat</s> down to the [gross] elements; for this purpose, the conjunction of <s>Pradhāna</s> too with <s>Puruṣa</s> [exists]. For the purpose of <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation). And this conjunction of both should be seen as like [that of] the lame and the blind — just as one is lame and one is blind, and these two, traveling together with great effort through a forest, [having been] abandoned by their kinsmen due to a disaster caused by bandits upon the caravan, wandered by fate and by their own [fortune], and they came together; then, trusting each other's words, their conjunction serves the purposes of going and seeing — the lame one is mounted on the blind one's shoulders; thus, by the path shown by the lame one mounted on the body, the blind one walks, and the lame one rides upon the blind one's shoulders. So too, <s>Puruṣa</s> has the power of seeing but, like the lame one, has no activity; <s>Pradhāna</s> has the power of activity but, like the blind one, has no power of seeing. Just as the separation of those two — the lame and the blind — will occur when their purpose is fulfilled and they reach their desired destination, so too <s>Pradhāna</s>, having effected the liberation of <s>Puruṣa</s>, withdraws; and <s>Puruṣa</s>, having seen <s>Pradhāna</s>, attains <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation); the separation of those two whose purposes are fulfilled will occur. Moreover, 'from that [conjunction] proceeds creation' — creation produced by that conjunction. Just as from the union of a woman and a man, a son is produced — so from the conjunction of <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, creation arises. // 21 //
Now, for the purpose of showing the complete differentiation [of categories], he says:
From <s>Prakṛti</s> [arises] <s>Mahat</s> (the Great); from that, <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-sense); from that, the group of sixteen;
and from five of that group of sixteen, the five <s>bhūtas</s> (gross elements). || 22 ||
