children.text: prakṛtiḥ pradhānaṃ brahma avyaktaṃ bahudhānakaṃ māyeti paryāyāḥ / aliṅgasyāḥ prakṛteḥ sakāśānmahānutpadyate mahān buddhirāsurī matiḥ khyātirjñānaṃ prajñāparyāyairutpadyate tasmācca mahato 'haṃkāra utpadyate 'haṃkāro bhūtādivaikṛtastaijaso 'bhimāna iti paryāyāḥ tasmādgaṇaśca ṣoḍaśakaḥ tasmādahaṃkārācchoḍaśakaḥ ṣoḍaśasvarūpeṇa guṇa utpadyate / sa yathā / pañcatanmātrāṇi śabdatanmātraṃ sparśatanmātraṃ rupatanmātraṃ rasatanmātraṃ gandhatanmātramiti / tanmātrasūkṣmaparyāyavācyāni / tata ekādaśendriyāṇi śrotraṃ tvak cakṣuṣī jihvā ghrāṇamiti pañca buddhīndriyāṇi / vākpāṇipādapāyūpasthāḥ pañcakarmendriyāṇyubhayātmakamekādaśaṃ mana eṣa ṣoḍaśako gaṇo 'haṃkārādutpadyate / kiṃca pañcabhyaḥ pañca bhūtāni tasmācchoḍaśakādgaṇāt pañcabhyastanmātrebhyaḥ sakāśāt pañca vai mahābhūtānyutpadyante / yaduktaṃ śabdatanmātrādākāśaṃ sparśatanmātrādvāyuḥ rūpatanmātrāttejaḥ rasatanmātrādāpaḥ gandhatanmātrāt pṛthivī evaṃ pañcabhyaḥ paramāṇubhyaḥ pañcamahābhūtānyutpadyante // 22 //
children.translated_text: <s>Prakṛti</s>, <s>Pradhāna</s>, <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Avyakta</s> (the Unmanifest), <s>Bahudhānaka</s> (the Manifold), and <s>Māyā</s> — these are synonyms. From this <s>Prakṛti</s>, which is without a mark (<s>aliṅga</s>), <s>Mahat</s> is produced — <s>Mahat</s> is produced under the synonyms <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>Āsurī</s>, <s>Mati</s> (thought), <s>Khyāti</s> (discernment), <s>Jñāna</s> (knowledge), and <s>Prajñā</s> (wisdom). And from that <s>Mahat</s>, <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> is produced — <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> has the synonyms <s>Bhūtādi</s>, <s>Vaikṛta</s>, <s>Taijasa</s>, and <s>Abhimāna</s> (self-conceit). 'From that, the group of sixteen' — from that <s>Ahaṃkāra</s>, a group of sixteen is produced, constituting sixteen in nature. They are as follows: the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) — the <s>śabda-tanmātra</s> (sound), <s>sparśa-tanmātra</s> (touch), <s>rūpa-tanmātra</s> (form), <s>rasa-tanmātra</s> (taste), and <s>gandha-tanmātra</s> (smell)

children.text:
yaduktaṃ vyaktāvyaktajñavijñānānmokṣa iti tatra mahadādibhūtāntaṃ trayoviṃśatibhedaṃ vyākhyātamavyaktamapi bhedānāṃ parimāṇādityādinā vyākhyātaṃ puruṣo 'pi saṃghātaparārthatvādityādibhirhetubhirvyākhyātaḥ / evametāni pañcaviṃśatitattvāni yastrailokyaṃ vyāptaṃ jānāti tasya bhāvo 'stitvaṃ tattvaṃ yathoktam /
  pañcaviṃśatitattvajño yatra tatrāśrame rataḥ /
  jaṭī muṇḍī śikhī vāpi mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ /
tāni yathā prakṛtiḥ puruṣo buddhirahaṃkāraḥ pañcatanmātrā ekādaśendriyāṇi pañcamahābhūtāni ityetāni pañcaviṃśatitattvāni / tatroktaṃ prakṛtermahānutpadyate tasya mahataḥ kiṃ lakṣaṇamityetadāha /
children.translated_text:
It was stated that liberation comes from the knowledge of the manifest, the unmanifest, and the knower. Therein, the twenty-three-fold [categories] from <s>Mahat</s> down to the [gross] elements have been explained; the unmanifest too has been explained through [arguments such as] 'because of the finitude of the differentiated [effects]' and so on; and <s>Puruṣa</s> too has been explained through reasons such as 'because of the composite being for another's purpose' and so on. Thus, one who knows these twenty-five <s>tattvas</s> (principles) by which the three worlds are pervaded — his being, his existence, is <s>tattva</s> (truth). As stated:
'One who knows the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s>, wherever and in whichever stage of life he may dwell,
whether wearing matted locks, shaven-headed, or bearing a topknot — he is liberated; there is no doubt about this.'
Determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>) is <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect); <s>dharma</s> (virtue), knowledge, dispassion, and sovereignty —
this is its <s>sāttvika</s> (pure) form; its <s>tāmasa</s> (dark) form is the reverse of this. || 23 ||

children.text: adhyavasāyo buddhilakṣaṇam / adhyavasanamadhyavasāyaḥ yathā bīje bhaviṣyadvṛttiko 'ṅkurastadvadadhyavasāyo 'yaṃ ghaṭo 'yaṃ paṭa ityevaṃ syati yā sā buddhiriti lakṣyate sā ca buddhiraṣṭāṅgikā sāttvikatāmasarūpabhedāt tatra buddheḥ sāttvikaṃ rūpaṃ caturvidhaṃ bhavati dharmo jñānaṃ vairāgyamaiśvaryaṃ ceti tatra dharmo nāma dayādānayamaniyamalakṣaṇastatra yamā niyamāśca pātañjale 'bhihitā ahiṃsāsatyāsteyabrahmacaryāparigrahā yamāḥ śaucasaṃtoṣatapaḥsvādhyāyeśvarapraṇidhā niyamāḥ / jñānaṃ prakāśo 'vagamo bhānamiti paryāyāstacca dvividhaṃ bāhyamābhyantaraṃ ceti tatra bāhyaṃ nāma vedāḥ śikṣā kalpo vyākaraṇaṃ niruktaṃ chandojyotiṣākhyaṣaḍaṅgasahitāḥ purāṇāni nyāyamīmāṃsādharmaśāstrāṇi ceti / ābhyantaraṃ prakṛtipuruṣajñānamiyaṃ prakṛtiḥ sattvarajastamasāṃ sāmyāvasthāyaṃ puruṣaḥ siddho nirguṇovyāpī cetana iti / tatra bāhyajñānena lokapaṃktirlokānurāga ityarthaḥ / ābhyantareṇa jñānena mokṣa ityarthaḥ vairāgyamapi dvividhaṃ bāhyamābhyantaraṃ ca bāhyaṃ dṛṣṭaviṣayavaitṛṣṇyamarjanarakṣaṇakṣayasaṃgahiṃsādoṣadarśanāt viraktasyābhyantaraṃ pradhānamapyatra svapnendrajālasadṛśamiti viraktasya gokṣepsoryadutpadyate tadābhyantaraṃ vairāgyam / aiśvaryamīśvarabhāvastaccāṣṭaguṇamaṇimā mahimā garimā laghimā prāptiḥ prākāmyamīśitvaṃ vaśitvaṃ yatrakāmāvasāyitvaṃ ceti / aṇorbhāvo 'ṇimā sūkṣmo bhūtvā jagati vicaratīti / mahimā mahān bhūtvā vicaratīti / laghimā mṛṇālītūlāvayavādapi laghutayā puṣpakesarāgreṣvapi tiṣṭhati / prāptirabhimataṃ vastu yatra tatrāvasthitaḥ prāpnoti / prākāmyaṃ prakāmato yadeveṣyati tadeva vidadhāti / īśitvaṃ prabhutayā trailokyamapīṣṭe / vaśitvaṃ sarvaṃ vaśībhavati / yatra kāmāvasāyitvaṃ brahmādistambaparyantaṃ yatra kāmastatraivāsya svecchayā sthānāsanavihārānācaratīti / catvāra etāni buddheḥ sāttvikāni rūpāṇi yadā sattvena rajastamasī abhibhūte tadā pumān buddhiguṇān dharmādīnāpnoti / kiṃcānyat tāmasamasmādviparyastamasmāddharmāderviparītaṃ tāmasaṃ buddhirūpaṃ dharmādviparīto 'dharma evamajñānamavairāgyamānaiśvaryamiti / evaṃ sāttvikaistāmasaiḥ svarūpairaṣṭāṃgā buddhistriguṇādavyaktādutpadyate // 23 //
children.translated_text: Determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>) is the defining characteristic of <s>Buddhi</s>. Determining is <s>adhyavasāya</s> — just as in a seed, the sprout will come into being in the future, so too determination [functions]: 'this is a pot, this is a cloth' — she who determines thus is characterized as <s>Buddhi</s>. And that <s>Buddhi</s> is eightfold, due to the division into <s>sāttvika</s> (pure) and <s>tāmasa</s> (dark) forms. Therein, the <s>sāttvika</s> form of <s>Buddhi</s> is fourfold: <s>dharma</s> (virtue), <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), and <s>aiśvarya</s> (sovereignty). Of these, <s>dharma</s> is characterized by compassion, charity, <s>yama</s> (restraints), and <s>niyama</s> (observances). Therein, the <s>yamas</s> and <s>niyamas</s> have been stated in the <s>Pātañjala</s> [system]: non-violence, truth,
Thus the defining characteristic of <s>Buddhi</s> has been stated; the defining characteristic of <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-sense) is now stated:
Self-conceit (<s>abhimāna</s>) is <s>Ahaṃkāra</s>; from it proceeds a twofold creation:
the group of eleven [organs] and the group of five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements). || 24 ||

children.text: ekādaśakaśca gaṇa ekādaśendriyāṇi tathā tanmātro gaṇaḥ pañcakaḥ pañcalakṣaṇopetaḥ śabdatanmātrasparśatanmātrarūpatanmātrarasatanmātragandhatanmātralakṣaṇopetaḥ // 24 //
children.translated_text: The group of eleven — the eleven <s>indriyas</s> (sense organs); and likewise the group of <s>tanmātras</s> is fivefold — having five characteristics: the <s>śabda-tanmātra</s> (sound), <s>sparśa-tanmātra</s> (touch), <s>rūpa-tanmātra</s> (form), <s>rasa-tanmātra</s> (taste), and <s>gandha-tanmātra</s> (smell). // 24 //
From which kind [of <s>Ahaṃkāra</s>] does [each] creation proceed? He says:
The group of eleven, which is <s>sāttvika</s> (pure), proceeds from the <s>Vaikṛta</s> (modified) <s>Ahaṃkāra</s>;
the <s>tanmātras</s> [proceed] from the <s>Bhūtādi</s> (elemental), which is <s>tāmasa</s> (dark); both [proceed] from the <s>Taijasa</s> (fiery). || 25 ||

children.text: sattvenābhibhūte yadā rajastamasī ahaṃkāre bhavatastadā so 'haṃkāraḥ sāttvikastasya ca pūrvācāryaiḥ saṃjñā kṛtā vaikṛta iti tasmādvikṛtādahaṃkārādekādaśaka indriyagaṇa utpadyate / tasmāt sāttvikāni viśuddhānīndriyāṇi svaviṣayasamarthāni tasmāducyate sāttvika ekādaśaka iti / kiṃcānyadbhūtādestanmātraḥ sa tāmasaḥ tamasābhibhūte sattvarajasī ahaṃkāre yadā bhavataḥ so 'haṃkārastāmasa ucyate tasya pūrvācāryakṛtā saṃjñā bhūtādistasmādbhūtāderahaṃkārāttanmātraḥ pañcako gaṇa utpadyate bhūtānāmādibhūtastamobahulastenoktaḥ sa tāmasa iti / tasmādbhūtādeḥ pañcatanmātrako gaṇaḥ kiṃca taijasādubhayaṃ yadārajasābhibhūte sattvatamasī bhavatastadā tasmāt so 'haṃkārastaijasa iti saṃjñāṃ labhate tasmāttaijasādubhayamutpadyate / ubhayamiti ekādaśo gaṇastanmātraḥ pañcakaḥ / yo 'yaṃ sāttviko 'haṃkāro vaikṛtiko vaikṛto bhūtvā ekādaśendriyāṇyutpādayati sa taijasamahaṃkāraṃ sahāyaṃ gṛhṇāti sāttviko niṣkriyaḥ sa taijasayukta indriyotpattau samarthaḥ tathā tāmaso 'haṃkāro bhūtādiḥ saṃjñito niṣkriyatvāttaijasenāhaṃkāreṇa kriyāvatā yuktastanmātrāṇyutpādayati tenoktaṃ taijasādubhayamiti evaṃ taijasenāhaṃkāreṇaindriyāṇyekādaśa pañcatanmātrāṇi kṛtāni bhavanti // 25 //
children.translated_text: When <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> are overpowered by <s>sattva</s> in the <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-principle), then that <s>ahaṃkāra</s> is called <s>sāttvika</s>, and the earlier teachers gave it the designation <s>vaikṛta</s> (modified). From that modified <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, the group of eleven sense-faculties (<s>indriyagaṇa</s>) arises. Therefore the sense-faculties, being <s>sāttvika</s>, are pure and capable in their respective domains — hence it is said 'the <s>sāttvika</s> group of eleven.' Furthermore, what else? From <s>bhūtādi</s> (the source of elements) [come] the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements); that is <s>tāmasa</s>. When <s>sattva</s> and <s>rajas</s> are overpowered by <s>tamas</s> in the <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, that <s>ahaṃkāra</s> is called <s>tāmasa</s>; the earlier teachers gave it the designation <s>bhūtādi</s>. From that <s>bhūtādi</s> <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, the group of five <s>tanmātras</s> arises. Being the source (<s>ādi</s>) of the [gross] elements (<s>bhūta</s>) and being predominantly <s>tamas</s>, it is therefore called <s>tāmasa</s>. From that <s>bhūtādi</s>, the group of five <s>tanmātras</s> [arises]. Furthermore, from the <s>taijasa</s> (fiery one), both [arise]. When <s>sattva</s> and <s>tamas</s> are overpowered by <s>rajas</s>, then that <s>ahaṃkāra</s> obtains the designation <s>taijasa</s>; from that <s>taijasa</s>, both arise. 'Both' means the group of eleven [sense-faculties] and the five <s>tanmātras</s>. The <s>sāttvika</s> <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, which is <s>vaikṛtika</s>, having undergone modification (<s>vaikṛta</s>), produces the eleven sense-faculties; it takes the <s>taijasa</s> <s>ahaṃkāra</s> as its assistant. The <s>sāttvika</s> [<s>ahaṃkāra</s>] is inactive by itself; joined with the <s>taijasa</s>, it becomes capable of producing the sense-faculties. Likewise, the <s>tāmasa</s> <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, designated <s>bhūtādi</s>, being inactive, produces the <s>tanmātras</s> when joined with the <s>taijasa</s> <s>ahaṃkāra</s> which possesses activity. Hence it is said 'from the <s>taijasa</s>, both.' Thus, through the <s>taijasa</s> <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, the eleven sense-faculties and five <s>tanmātras</s> are produced. (25)

children.text: ekādaśaka ityuktaḥ yo vaikṛtāt sāttvikādahaṃkārādutpadyate tasya kā saṃjñetyāha /
children.translated_text: The group of eleven has been mentioned. That which arises from the <s>vaikṛta</s> <s>sāttvika</s> <s>ahaṃkāra</s> — what is its designation? He states:
The <s>buddhīndriyāṇi</s> (cognitive sense-faculties) are those of seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting, and touching.
Speech, hands, feet, anus, and genitals are declared to be the <s>karmendriyāṇi</s> (active sense-faculties). (Sāṃkhyakārikā 26)

children.text: cakṣurādīni sparśanaparyantāni buddhīndriyāṇyucyante / spṛśyate aneneti sparśanaṃ tvagindriyaṃ tadvācī siddhaḥ sparśanaśabdo 'sti tenedaṃ paṭhyate sparśanakānīti śabdasparśarūparasagandhān pañcaviṣayān budhyante avagacchantīti pañca buddhīndriyāṇi / vākpāṇipādapāyūpasthān karmendriyāṇyāhuḥ karma kurvantīti karmendriyāṇi / tatra vāgvadati hastau nānāvyāpāraṃ kurutaḥ pādau gamanāgamanaṃ pāyurutsargaṃ karoti upastha ānaṃdaṃ prajotpattyā // 26 //
children.translated_text: The [faculties] beginning with the eye and ending with the touch-organ are called <s>buddhīndriyāṇi</s> (cognitive sense-faculties). 'That by which one touches' is the touch-organ, meaning the skin-faculty; the word <s>sparśana</s> is an established term for it — hence the text reads 'those of touching.' They cognize, that is, they apprehend the five objects: sound, touch, form, taste, and smell — therefore they are the five <s>buddhīndriyāṇi</s>. Speech, hands, feet, anus, and genitals are declared to be the <s>karmendriyāṇi</s> (active sense-faculties). They perform actions, therefore they are <s>karmendriyāṇi</s>. Among these: speech speaks, the two hands perform various operations, the two feet [perform] coming and going, the anus performs the excretion [of waste], and the genitals [perform] pleasure through the production of offspring. (26)

children.text: evaṃ buddhīndriyakarmendriyabhedena daśendriyāṇi vyākhyātāni mana ekādaśakaṃ kimātmakaṃ kiṃ svarūpaṃ ceti taducyate /
children.translated_text: Thus, ten sense-faculties have been explained as divided into <s>buddhīndriya</s> (cognitive) and <s>karmendriya</s> (active). The mind (<s>manas</s>), the eleventh — what is its nature, what is its essential character? That is now stated:
The mind (<s>manas</s>) here is of a dual nature; it is the deliberating faculty and also a sense-faculty, because of its similarity [to both].
The diversity [of the sense-faculties arises] from the specific modifications of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), and also from the difference of external [objects]. (Sāṃkhyakārikā 27)

children.text: atrendriyavarge mana ubhayātmakaṃ buddhīndriyeṣu buddhīndriyavat karmendriyeṣu karmendriyavat kasmādbuddhīndriyāṇāṃ pravṛttiṃ kalpayati karmendriyāṇāṃ ca tasmādubhayātmakaṃ manaḥ saṃkalpayatīti saṃkalpakam / kiṃcānyadindriyaṃ ca sādharmyāt samānadharmabhāvāt sāttvikāhaṃkārādbuddhīndriyāṇi karmendriyāṇi manasā sahotpadyamānāni manasaḥ sādharmyaṃ prati tasmātsādharmyānmano 'pīndriyamevametānyekādaśendriyāṇi sāttvikādvaikṛtādahaṃkārādutpannāni / tatra manasaḥ kā vṛttiriti / saṃkalpo vṛttiḥ / buddhīndriyāṇāṃ śabdādayo vṛttayaḥ karmendriyāṇāṃ vacanādayo 'thaitānīndriyāṇi bhinnāni bhinnārthagrāhakāṇi kimīśvareṇota svabhāvena kṛtāni yataḥ pradhānabuddhyahaṃkārā acetanāḥ puruṣo 'pyakarttetyatrāha / iha sāṃkhyānāṃ svabhāvo nāma kaścitkāraṇamasti / atrocyate guṇapariṇāmaviśeṣānnānātvaṃ bāhyabhedāśca / imānyekādaśendriyāṇi śabdasparśarūparasagandhāḥ pañcānāṃ vacanādānaviharaṇotsargānandāśca pañcānāṃ saṃkalpaśca manasa evamete bhinnānāmevendriyāṇāmarthāḥ guṇapariṇāmaviśeṣāt guṇānāṃ pariṇāmo guṇapariṇāmastasya viśeṣādindriyāṇāṃ nānātvaṃ bāhyārthabhedāśca / athaitannānātvaṃ neśvareṇa nāhaṃkāreṇa na buddhyā na pradhānena na puruṣeṇa svabhāvāt kṛtaguṇapariṇāmeneti / guṇānāmacetanatvānna pravarttate pravarttata eva kathaṃ vakṣyatīhaiva vatsavivṛddhinimittaṃ kṣīrasya yathā pravṛttirajñasya puruṣasya vimokṣārthaṃ tathā pravṛttiḥ pradhānasya / evamacetanaguṇāḥ ekādaśendriyabhāvena pravarttante viśeṣā api tatkṛtā eva yenoccaiḥ pradeśe cakṣuḥkhalokanāya sthitaṃ tathā ghrāṇaṃ tathā śrotraṃ tathā jihvā svadeśe svārthagrahaṇāya / evaṃ karmendriyāṇyapi yathāyathaṃ svārthasamarthāni svadeśāvasthitāni svabhāvato guṇapariṇāmaviśeṣādeva na tadarthā api yata uktaṃ śāstrāntare / guṇā guṇeṣu varttante guṇānāṃ yā vṛttiḥ sā guṇaviṣayā eveti bāhyārthā vijñeyā guṇakṛtā evetyarthaḥ / pradhānaṃ yasya kāraṇamiti // 27 //
children.translated_text: Here, in the group of sense-faculties, the mind is of dual nature: among the cognitive sense-faculties it is like a cognitive sense-faculty, and among the active sense-faculties it is like an active sense-faculty. Why? Because it directs the activity of the cognitive sense-faculties and also of the active sense-faculties — therefore the mind is of dual nature. It deliberates, hence it is the deliberating faculty (<s>saṃkalpaka</s>). Furthermore, it is also a sense-faculty, because of similarity (<s>sādharmya</s>), that is, because of having a common property. The cognitive and active sense-faculties arise from the <s>sāttvika</s> <s>ahaṃkāra</s> together with the mind — in this the mind has similarity [with them]; therefore, because of similarity, the mind too is a sense-faculty. Thus these eleven sense-faculties have arisen from the <s>sāttvika</s> <s>vaikṛta</s> <s>ahaṃkāra</s>. What then is the function of the mind? Deliberation (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) is its function. The functions of the cognitive sense-faculties are [the apprehension of] sound and so forth; the functions of the active sense-faculties are speaking and so forth. Now, these sense-faculties are diverse, apprehending diverse objects — were they made by God, or by their own nature? Since <s>pradhāna</s> (primal matter), <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), and <s>ahaṃkāra</s> are non-conscious, and <s>puruṣa</s> (self) too is non-agent — to this he replies: In this <s>Sāṃkhya</s> [system], there is a certain cause called <s>svabhāva</s> (own-nature). Here it is stated: the diversity [arises] from the specific modifications of the <s>guṇas</s>, and also from external differences. These eleven sense-faculties — the five [apprehend] sound, touch, form, taste, and smell; the five [perform] speaking, grasping, locomotion, excretion, and pleasure; and deliberation is [the function] of the mind itself. Thus these are the objects of the diverse sense-faculties, arising from the specific modification of the <s>guṇas</s> — the modification of the <s>guṇas</s> is <s>guṇapariṇāma</s>, and from its specificity [comes] the diversity of the sense-faculties, as well as the difference of external objects. Now, this diversity is not made by God, nor by <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, nor by <s>buddhi</s>, nor by <s>pradhāna</s>, nor by <s>puruṣa</s>, but by the transformation of the <s>guṇas</s> according to their own nature. [Objection:] Since the <s>guṇas</s> are non-conscious, they do not act. [Reply:] They do indeed act. How? It will be stated right here [in a later verse]: 'Just as the activity of milk is for the nourishment of the calf, so is the activity of <s>pradhāna</s> for the liberation of <s>puruṣa</s>.' Thus the non-conscious <s>guṇas</s> function in the form of the eleven sense-faculties; the specificities too are produced by them alone — whereby the eye is placed at a high point for the purpose of seeing, likewise the nose, likewise the ear, likewise the tongue, each at its own place for apprehending its own object. Similarly, the active sense-faculties too are situated at their own places, capable of their own objects, by their own nature, from the specific modification of the <s>guṇas</s> alone — not purposively designed. As it is stated in another treatise: 'The <s>guṇas</s> operate among the <s>guṇas</s>; the activity of the <s>guṇas</s> pertains only to the domain of the <s>guṇas</s>.' The external objects should be understood as produced by the <s>guṇas</s> alone — this is the meaning. [That] whose cause is <s>pradhāna</s>. (27)
Now, what is the function of which sense-faculty? This is stated:
The function of the five [cognitive sense-faculties] with regard to sound and the rest is held to be mere apprehension.
Speaking, grasping, locomotion, excretion, and pleasure are [the functions] of the five [active sense-faculties]. (Sāṃkhyakārikā 28)

children.text: mātraśabdo viśeṣārthaḥ / aviśeṣavyāvṛtyartho yathā bhikṣā mātraṃ labhyate nānyo viśeṣa iti / tatha cakṣū rūpamatre na rasādiṣu evaṃ śeṣāṇyapi tadyathā cakṣuṣo rūpaṃ jihvāyā raso ghrāṇasya gandhaḥ śrotrasya śabdaḥ tvacaḥ sparśaḥ / evameṣāṃ buddhīndriyāṇāṃ vṛttiḥ kathitā karmendriyāṇāṃ vṛttiḥ kathyate vacanādānaviharaṇotsargānandāśca pañcānāṃ karmendriyāṇāmityarthaḥ / vāco vacanaṃ hastayorādānaṃ pādayorviharaṇaṃ pāyorbhuktasyāhārasya pariṇatamalotsargaḥ upasthasyānandaḥ sutotpattirviṣayā vṛttiriti sambandhaḥ // 28 //
children.translated_text: The word 'mere' (<s>mātra</s>) is used in the sense of specification — for the purpose of excluding what is unspecified, just as [one says] 'only alms-food is obtained, nothing else special.' Similarly, the eye [apprehends] form only, not taste and so forth; likewise the remaining [cognitive sense-faculties] also. Specifically: the eye's [object is] form, the tongue's is taste, the nose's is smell, the ear's is sound, the skin's is touch. Thus the function of these <s>buddhīndriyāṇi</s> (cognitive sense-faculties) has been stated. The function of the <s>karmendriyāṇi</s> (active sense-faculties) is stated: speaking, grasping, locomotion, excretion, and pleasure are [the functions] of the five active sense-faculties — this is the meaning. Speech's [function is] speaking, the hands' is grasping, the feet's is locomotion, the anus's is the excretion of digested food-waste, and the genitals' is pleasure through the production of offspring — this is the relation of object and function. (28)
Now [the functions] of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-principle), and <s>manas</s> (mind) are stated:
The function of these three is characterized by their own distinctive marks; it is uncommon.
The common function of the instruments [of cognition] is the five breaths (<s>vāyu</s>) beginning with <s>prāṇa</s>. (Sāṃkhyakārikā 29)

children.text: svalakṣaṇasvabhāvā svālakṣaṇyā / adhyavasāyo yo buddhiriti lakṣaṇamuktaṃ saiva buddhivṛttiḥ / tathābhimāno 'haṃkāra ityabhimānalakṣaṇo 'bhimānavṛttiśca / saṃkalpakaṃ mana iti lakṣaṇamuktaṃ tena saṃkalpa eva manaso vṛttiḥ / trayasya buddhyahaṃkāramanasāṃ svālakṣaṇyā vṛttirasāmānyā yā prāgabhihitā buddhīndriyāṇāṃ ca vṛttiḥ sāpyasāmānyaiveti / idānīṃ sāmānyā vṛttirākhyāyate / sāmānyakāranavṛttiḥ sāmānyena karaṇānāṃ vṛttiḥ prāṇādyā vāyavaḥ pañca prāṇāpānasamānodānavyānā iti pañca vāyavaḥ sarvendriyāṇāṃ sāmānyā vṛttiryataḥ / prāṇo nāma vāyurmukhanāsikāntargocarastasya yat spandanaṃ karma tat trayodaśavidhasyāpi sāmānyā vṛttiḥ sati prāṇe yasmāt karaṇānāmātmalābha iti / prāṇo 'pi pañcaraśakunivat sarvasya calanaṃ karotīti / prāṇanāt prāṇa ityucyate / tathāpanayanādapānastatra yatspandanaṃ tadapi sāmānyavṛttirindriyasya / tathā samāno madhyadeśavartī ya āhārādinayanātsamaṃ nayanāt samāno vāyustatra yatspandanaṃ tat sāmānyaṃ karaṇavṛttiḥ / tathā ūrdhvārohaṇādutkarṣādunnayanādvā udāno nābhideśamastakāntargocarastatrodāne yatspandanaṃ tat sarvendriyāṇāṃ sāmānyā vṛttiḥ / kiṃca śarīravyāptirabhyantaravibhāgaśca yena kriyate 'sau śarīravyāptyākāśavadvyānastatra yat spandanaṃ tat karaṇajālasya sāmānyā vṛttiriti / evamete pañca vāyavaḥ sāmānyakaraṇavṛttiriti vyākhyātāḥ trayodaśavidhasyāpi karaṇasāmānyā vṛttirityarthaḥ // 29 //
children.translated_text: Having their own distinctive marks as their nature is <s>svālakṣaṇya</s> (own-characterization). The defining mark stated as '<s>buddhi</s> (intellect) is determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>)' — that itself is the function of <s>buddhi</s>. Likewise, '<s>ahaṃkāra</s> is self-attribution (<s>abhimāna</s>)' — this is its defining mark and its function is self-attribution. 'The mind is the deliberating faculty (<s>saṃkalpaka</s>)' — this defining mark was stated; therefore deliberation alone is the function of the mind. The function of these three — <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, and <s>manas</s> — characterized by their own distinctive marks, is uncommon [i.e., specific to each]; likewise the function of the cognitive sense-faculties stated earlier is also uncommon. Now the common function is explained. The common function of the instruments (<s>karaṇa</s>) is the five breaths (<s>vāyu</s>) beginning with <s>prāṇa</s>: <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, <s>samāna</s>, <s>udāna</s>, and <s>vyāna</s> — these five breaths are the common function of all the sense-faculties. <s>Prāṇa</s> is the breath operating within the mouth and nostrils; its movement is the common function of all thirteen instruments, since the instruments gain their very existence when <s>prāṇa</s> is present. <s>Prāṇa</s>, like a bird in a cage, causes movement of all — because it enlivens (<s>prāṇana</s>), it is called <s>prāṇa</s>. Likewise, because of carrying downward (<s>apanayana</s>), [it is called] <s>apāna</s>; its movement too is a common function of the sense-faculties. Likewise, <s>samāna</s> operates in the middle region; because it carries equally (<s>samaṃ nayana</s>), such as conveying food and the like, the breath <s>samāna</s> — its movement is a common function of the instruments. Likewise, because of ascending upward, superiority, or carrying upward, [it is called] <s>udāna</s>, operating in the region between the navel and the top of the head; the movement of <s>udāna</s> is a common function of all the sense-faculties. Furthermore, that which pervades the entire body and creates internal division, pervading [the body] like space — that is <s>vyāna</s>; its movement is a common function of the entire network of instruments. Thus these five breaths have been explained as the common function of the instruments — this means the common function of all thirteen instruments. (29)

children.text: yugapaccatuṣṭayasya tu vṛttiḥ kramaśaśca tasya nirdiṣṭā /
children.translated_text: The functioning of the four [internal and one external organ] simultaneously, and also their sequential [functioning], has been stated.
In the seen [present], as well as in the unseen [past and future], the functioning of the three [inner organs] is preceded by that [external organ]. // <s>ISk</s> 30 //

children.text: yugapaccatuṣṭayasya buddhyahaṃkāramanasāmekaikendriyasambandhe sati catuṣṭayaṃ bhavati catuṣṭayasya dṛṣṭe prativiṣayādhyavasāye yugapadvṛtirbuddhyahaṃkāramanaścakṣūṃṣi yugapadekakālaṃ rūpaṃ paśyati sthāṇurayamiti / buddhyahaṃkāramanojihvā yugapadrasaṃ gṛhṇanti / buddhyahaṃkāramanoghrāṇāni yugapadgandhaṃ gṛhṇanti / tathā tvakśrotre api / kiṃca kramaśaśca tasya nirdiṣṭā tasyeti catuṣṭayasyakramaśaśca vṛttirbhavati / yathā kaścit pathi gacchan dūrādeva dṛṣṭvā sthāṇurayaṃ puruṣo veti saṃśaye sati tatroparūḍhāṃ valliṃ talliṅgaṃ paśyati śakuniṃ vā tato tasya manasā saṃkalpite saṃśaye vyavacchedabhūtā buddhirbhavati sthāṇurayamityato 'haṃkāraśca niścayārthaḥ sthāṇurevetyevaṃ buddhyahaṃkāramanaścakṣuṣāṃ kramaśo vṛttirdṛṣṭā yathā rūpe tathā śabdādiṣvapi boddhavyā dṛṣṭe dṛṣṭaviṣaye / kiṃcānyattathāpyadṛṣṭe trayasya tatpūrvikā vṛttiradṛṣṭe 'nāgate 'tīte ca kāle buddhyahaṃkāramanasāṃ rūpe cakṣuḥ pūrvikā trayasya vṛttiḥ sparśe tvakpūrvikā gandhe ghrāṇapūrvikā rase rasanapūrvikā śabde śravaṇapūrvikā buddhyahaṃkāramanasāmanāgate bhaviṣyati kāle 'tīte ca tat kramaśo vṛttirvarttamāne yugapat kramaśaśceti // 30 //
children.translated_text: 'Simultaneously of the four' — when <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego), and <s>manas</s> (mind) are connected with a single sense-organ, there is a group of four. The simultaneous functioning of the four occurs in the determination of a present object: <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, <s>manas</s>, and the eyes simultaneously, at one time, see a form — 'this is a post.' <s>Buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, <s>manas</s>, and the tongue simultaneously grasp a taste. <s>Buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, <s>manas</s>, and the nose simultaneously grasp an odor. Similarly for touch and hearing. Moreover, 'and their sequential [functioning] has been stated' — 'their' means of the four; sequential functioning also occurs. For example, someone going on a path, having seen from afar, when there is doubt 'Is this a post or a person?' — there he sees a creeper growing on it, or a bird as its mark; then, when this is conceptualized by <s>manas</s>, the determining <s>buddhi</s> arises from the doubt: 'This is a post.' Then <s>ahaṃkāra</s> [functions] for the purpose of certainty: 'It is indeed a post.' Thus, the sequential functioning of <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, <s>manas</s>, and the eye is observed. As with form, so with sound etc. should be understood — in the seen, i.e., the visible object. Moreover, another [point]: 'as well as in the unseen — the functioning of the three is preceded by that' — in the unseen, i.e., in the future and past time, the functioning of <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, and <s>manas</s> regarding form is preceded by the eye; regarding touch, preceded by skin; regarding smell, preceded by the nose; regarding taste, preceded by the tongue; regarding sound, preceded by hearing. For <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, and <s>manas</s>, in the future and past time, the functioning is sequential; in the present, both simultaneous and sequential. // 30 //
Moreover:
They undertake their respective functions, motivated by each other's intent.
The purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> (Spirit) alone is the motive; no one causes the instrument to act. // <s>ISk</s> 31 //

children.text: svāṃ svāmiti vīpsā buddhyahaṃkāramanāṃsi svāṃ svāṃ vṛttiṃ parasparākūtahetukāmākūtakādarāsambhrama iti pratipadyante puruṣārthakaraṇāya / buddherahaṃkārādayo buddhirahaṃkārākūtaṃ jñātvā svasvaviṣayaṃ pratipadyate kimarthamiti cet puruṣārtha eva hetuḥ puruṣārthaḥ karttavya ityevamarthaṃ guṇānāṃ pravṛttistasmādetāni karaṇāni puruṣārthaṃ prakāśayanti kathaṃ svayaṃ pravartante na kenacit kāryate karaṇaṃ puruṣārtha evaikaḥ kārayatīti vākyārtho na kenacidīśvareṇa puruṣeṇa kāryate prabodhyate karaṇam // 31 //
children.translated_text: 'Their respective' — the repetition (<s>vīpsā</s>) [emphasizes that] <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, and <s>manas</s> each undertake their own respective function, motivated by each other's intent (<s>ākūta</s>) — eagerness, regard, and haste — for the purpose of [serving] <s>Puruṣa</s>. From <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṃkāra</s> and the rest; <s>buddhi</s>, knowing the intent of <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, engages its own object. For what purpose? 'The purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> alone is the motive' — the activity of the <s>guṇas</s> is for the purpose that '<s>Puruṣa's</s> purpose must be accomplished.' Therefore, these instruments illuminate the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>. How do they operate by themselves? 'No one causes the instrument to act' — the meaning of the sentence is: the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> alone causes [them to act]; no <s>Īśvara</s> (God) or [other] <s>puruṣa</s> causes or impels the instrument. // 31 //
'Of how many kinds is [the group] beginning with <s>buddhi</s>?' This is now stated:
The instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) is of thirteen kinds; it produces grasping, holding, and illuminating.

children.text: kāryaṃ ca tasya daśadhāhāryaṃ dhāryaṃ prakāśyaṃ ca || 32 ||
children.translated_text: And its effect is tenfold: the graspable, the holdable, and the illuminable. // <s>ISk</s> 32 //

children.text: karaṇaṃ mahadādi trayodaśavidhaṃ boddhyavyaṃ pañcabuddhīndriyāṇi cakṣurādīni pañca karmendriyāṇi vāgādīnīti trayodaśavidhaṃ karaṇaṃ tatkiṃ karotītyetadāha tadāharaṇadhāraṇaprakāśakaram / tatrāharaṇaṃ dhāraṇaṃ ca karmendriyāṇi kurvanti prakāśaṃ buddhīndriyāṇi / katividhaṃ kāryaṃ tasyeti taducyate / kāryaṃ ca tasya daśadhā tasya karaṇasya kāryaṃ kartavyamiti daśadhā daśaprakāraṃ śabdasparśarūparasagandhākhyaṃ vacanādānaviharaṇotsargānandākhyametaddaśavidhaṃ kāryaṃ buddhīndriyaiḥ prakāśitaṃ karmendriyāṇyāharanti dhārayanti ceti // 32 //
children.translated_text: The instrument beginning with <s>mahat</s> (the Great, i.e., <s>buddhi</s>) should be understood as thirteenfold: the five <s>buddhīndriyās</s> (sense-organs) beginning with the eye, and the five <s>karmendriyās</s> (action-organs) beginning with speech — thus the instrument is thirteenfold. 'What does it do?' — this is stated: 'it produces grasping, holding, and illuminating.' There, the <s>karmendriyās</s> perform grasping and holding; the <s>buddhīndriyās</s> perform illuminating. 'Of how many kinds is its effect?' This is stated: 'And its effect is tenfold' — the effect of that instrument, i.e., what is to be done, is tenfold: the ten kinds named sound, touch, form, taste, and smell; and speech, grasping, locomotion, excretion, and pleasure — this tenfold effect is illuminated by the <s>buddhīndriyās</s>, and the <s>karmendriyās</s> grasp and hold [it]. // 32 //

children.text: antaḥkaraṇaṃ trividhaṃ daśadhā bāhyaṃ trayasya viṣayākhyam /
children.translated_text: The internal instrument is threefold; the external is tenfold. The object of the three is called 'object.'
The external instrument [functions in] the present time; the internal instrument [functions in] all three times. // <s>ISk</s> 33 //

children.text: antaḥkaraṇamiti buddhyahaṃkāramanāṃsi trividhaṃ mahadādibhedāt / daśadhā bāhyaṃ ca buddhīndriyāṇi pañca karmendriyāṇi pañca daśavidhametatkaraṇaṃ bāhyaṃ tatra yasyāntaḥkaraṇasya viṣayākhyaṃ buddhyahaṃkāramanasāṃ bhogyaṃ sāmpratakālaṃ śrotraṃ varttamānameva śabdaṃ śṛṇoti nātītaṃ na ca bhaviṣyantaṃ cakṣurapi vartamānaṃ rūpaṃ paśyati nātītaṃ nānāgataṃ tvagvarttamānaṃ sparśaṃ jihvā varttamānaṃ rasaṃ nāsikā varttamānaṃ gandhaṃ nātītānāgataṃ ceti / evaṃ karmendriyāṇi vāgvarttamānaṃ śabdamuccārayati nātītaṃ nānāgataṃ pāṇī varttamānaṃ ghaṭamādadāte nātītamanāgataṃ pāyūpasthau ca varttamānāvutsargānandau kuruto nātītau nānāgatau / evaṃ bāhyaṃ karaṇaṃ sāmpratakālamuktaṃ trikālamābhyantaraṃ karaṇaṃ buddhyahaṃkāramanāṃsi trikālaviṣayāṇi buddhirvarttamānaṃ ghaṭaṃ budhyate atītamanāgataṃ ceti / ahaṃkāro varttamāne 'bhimānaṃ karotyatīte 'nāgate ca / tathā mano varttamāne saṃkalpaṃ kurute atīte 'nāgate ca evaṃ trikālamābhyantaraṃ karaṇamiti // 33 //
children.translated_text: 'Internal instrument' means <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, and <s>manas</s> — threefold, due to the distinction of <s>mahat</s> etc. 'The external is tenfold' — the five <s>buddhīndriyās</s> and five <s>karmendriyās</s> — this tenfold instrument is external. That which is the object (<s>viṣaya</s>) of the internal instrument is the enjoyable (<s>bhogya</s>) of <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, and <s>manas</s>. '[The external functions in] the present time' — the ear hears only the present sound, not the past or future. The eye too sees the present form, not the past or future. The skin [perceives] the present touch; the tongue, the present taste; the nose, the present smell — not the past or future. Similarly the <s>karmendriyās</s>: speech utters the present sound, not past or future; the hand grasps the present pot, not past or future; the excretory and generative organs also perform their functions in the present only, not past or future. Thus the external instrument is said to [function in] the present time. 'The internal instrument [functions in] the three times' — <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, and <s>manas</s> have all three times as their domain. <s>Buddhi</s> cognizes the present pot, the past, and the future. <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> produces self-identification in the present, past, and future. Similarly, <s>manas</s> conceptualizes in the present, past, and future. Thus the internal instrument [functions in] the three times. // 33 //

children.text: idānīmindriyāṇi kati saviśeṣaṃ viṣayaṃ gṛhṇanti kāni nirviśeṣamiti taducyate /
children.translated_text: Now, how many sense-organs grasp a differentiated (<s>saviśeṣa</s>) object, and how many [grasp] an undifferentiated (<s>nirviśeṣa</s>) [object]? This is stated:
The <s>buddhīndriyās</s> — five of them have differentiated and undifferentiated objects.
Speech has sound as its object; the remaining [action-organs] also have five objects. // <s>ISk</s> 34 //

children.text: buddhīndriyāṇi tāni saviśeṣaṃ viṣayaṃ gṛhṇāti saviśeṣaviṣayaṃ mānuṣāṇāṃ śabdasparśarūparasagandhān sukhaduḥkhamohaviṣayayuktān buddhīndriyāṇi prakāśayanti devānāṃ nirviśeṣānviṣayān prakāśayanti tathā karmendriyāṇāṃ madhye vāgbhavati śabdaviṣayā devānāṃ mānuṣāṇāṃ ca vāgvadati ślokādīnuccārayati tasmāddevānāṃ mānuṣāṇāṃ ca vāgindriyaṃ tulyaṃ śeṣāṇyapi vāgvyatiriktāni pāṇipādapāyūpasthasaṃjñitāni pañcaviṣayāṇi śabdādayo yeṣāṃ tāni pañcaviṣayāṇi śabdasparśarūparasagandhāḥ pāṇau santi pañcaśabdādilakṣaṇāyāṃ bhuvi pādo viharati pāyvindriyaṃ pañcaklṛptamutsargaṃ karoti tathopasthendriyaṃ pañcalakṣaṇaṃ śukramānandayati // 34 //
children.translated_text: The <s>buddhīndriyās</s> grasp a differentiated object — for humans, the <s>buddhīndriyās</s> illuminate sounds, touches, forms, tastes, and smells connected with pleasure, pain, and delusion. For gods, they illuminate undifferentiated objects. Similarly, among the <s>karmendriyās</s>, 'speech has sound as its object' — for both gods and humans, speech speaks and utters verses etc. Therefore, the speech-organ is equal for gods and humans. 'The remaining also [have] five objects' — the remaining [organs] other than speech, named hand, foot, excretory organ, and generative organ, have five objects, i.e., sounds etc. are their [objects]. The hand has the five [qualities] beginning with sound on the five-[quality]-characterized earth on which it operates; the foot moves; the excretory organ produces a five-[quality]-characterized excretion; similarly, the generative organ brings pleasure regarding the five-characterized semen. // 34 //
<s>Buddhi</s> together with the internal instruments apprehends all objects, because
therefore the threefold instrument is the doorway; the remaining [instruments] are the doors. // <s>ISk</s> 35 //

children.text: sāntaḥkaraṇā buddhirahaṃkāramanaḥsahitetyarthaha yasmāt sarvaṃ viṣayamavagāhate gṛhṇāti triṣvapi kāleṣu śabdādīn gṛhṇāti tasmāttrividhama karaṇaṃ dvāri dvārāṇi śeṣāṇi śeṣāni karaṇānīti vākyaśeṣaḥ // 35 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Buddhi</s> together with the internal instruments' means combined with <s>ahaṃkāra</s> and <s>manas</s>. Because it apprehends, i.e., grasps, all objects in all three times — sounds etc. — therefore the threefold instrument is the doorway; 'the remaining are the doors' — the remaining instruments — this completes the sentence. // 35 //
What else?
These, like lamps, are the particular modifications of the <s>guṇas</s>, mutually distinct from one another.
Having illuminated the entire purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>, they present [it] to <s>buddhi</s>. // <s>ISk</s> 36 //

children.text: yāni karaṇānyuktāni ete guṇaviśeṣāḥ kiṃ viśiṣṭāḥ pradīpakalpāḥ pradīpavadviṣayaprakāśakāḥ parasparavilakṣaṇā asadṛśā bhinnaviṣayā ityarthaḥ / guṇaviṣayā ityarthaḥ / guṇaviśeṣā guṇebhyo jātāḥ / kṛtsnaṃ puruṣasyārthaṃ buddhīndriyāni karmendriyāṇyahaṃkāro manaścaitāni svaṃ svamarthaṃ puruṣasya prakāśya buddhau prayacchanti buddhisthaṃ kurvantītyarthaḥ / yato buddhisthaṃ sarvaṃ viṣayaṃ sukhādikaṃ puruṣa upalabhyate // 36 //
children.translated_text: The instruments that have been described — 'these particular modifications of the <s>guṇas</s>' — what are they characterized by? 'Like lamps' — like a lamp, they illuminate objects. 'Mutually distinct from one another' — dissimilar, i.e., having different objects. 'Particular modifications of the <s>guṇas</s>' — born from the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities of <s>Prakṛti</s>). 'The entire purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>' — the <s>buddhīndriyās</s>, <s>karmendriyās</s>, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, and <s>manas</s> — these, having illuminated each their own purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>, present [it] to <s>buddhi</s>, i.e., make it established in <s>buddhi</s>. Because <s>Puruṣa</s> perceives all objects — pleasure etc. — as established in <s>buddhi</s>. // 36 //
And this is another [point]:
Since <s>buddhi</s> accomplishes all experience for <s>Puruṣa</s>,

children.text: saiva ca viśinaṣṭi tataḥ pradhānapuruṣāntaraṃ sūkṣmam || 37 ||
children.translated_text: it alone also discriminates the subtle difference between <s>Pradhāna</s> (Primal Matter) and <s>Puruṣa</s>. // <s>ISk</s> 37 //

children.text: sarvendriyagataṃ triṣvapi kāleṣu sarvaṃ pratyupabhogamupabhogaṃ prati devamanuṣyatiryag buddhīndriyakarmendriyadvāreṇa sāntaḥkaraṇā buddhiḥ sādhayati sampādayati yasmāt tasmāt saiva ca viśinaṣṭi pradhānapuruṣayorviṣayavibhāgaṃ karoti pradhānapuruṣāntaraṃ nānātvamityarthaḥ / sūkṣmamityanadhikṛtatapaścaraṇairaprāpyamiyaṃ prakṛtiḥ sattvarajastamasāṃ sāmyāvasthā iyaṃ buddhirayamahaṃkāra etāni pañcatanmātrāṇyekādaśendriyāṇi pañcamahābhūtānyayamanyaḥ puruṣa ebhyo vyatirikta ityeva bodhayati buddhiryasyāvāyādapavargo bhavati // 37 //
children.translated_text: All [experience] pertaining to all the senses, in all three times — all experience (<s>upabhoga</s>) for gods, humans, and animals — <s>buddhi</s> together with the internal instruments accomplishes through the doorway of the <s>buddhīndriyās</s> and <s>karmendriyās</s>. Since it [accomplishes all this], therefore 'it alone also discriminates' — it makes the distinction of objects between <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>. 'The difference between <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>' means their distinctness. 'Subtle' — not attainable by those who have not undertaken austerities. [<s>Buddhi</s> teaches:] 'This is <s>Prakṛti</s>, the state of equilibrium of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>; this is <s>buddhi</s>; this is <s>ahaṃkāra</s>; these are the five <s>tanmātras</s>; [these are] the eleven <s>indriyas</s>; [these are] the five gross elements; this other one is <s>Puruṣa</s>, distinct from all these' — thus <s>buddhi</s> teaches, [and] from this knowledge, liberation (<s>apavarga</s>) results. // 37 //

children.text: pūrvamuktaṃ viśeṣāviśeṣaviṣayāṇi tat ke viṣayāstacca darśayati /
children.translated_text: It was previously stated that [the sense organs] have both <s>viśeṣas</s> (specific) and <s>aviśeṣas</s> (non-specific) as their objects. What are those objects? This he shows:
The <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) are the <s>aviśeṣas</s> (non-specific); from them, the five <s>bhūtas</s> (gross elements) [arise] from the five [<s>tanmātras</s>].

children.text: ete smṛtā viśeṣāḥ śāntā ghorāśca mūḍhāśca || 38 ||
children.translated_text: These are known as the <s>viśeṣas</s> (specific) — [they are] tranquil, turbulent, and stupefying. || 38 ||

children.text: yāni pañca tanmātrāṇyahaṃkārādutpadyante te śabdatanmātraṃ sparśatanmātraṃ rūpatanmātraṃ rasatanmātraṃ gandhatanmātrametānyaviśeṣā ucyante devānāmete sukhalakṣaṇā viṣayā duḥkhamoharahitāstebhyaḥ pañcabhyastanmātrebhyaḥ pañcamahābhūtāni pṛthivyaptejovāyvākāśasaṃjñitāni yānyutpadyante / ete smṛtā viśeṣāḥ / gandhatanmātrāt pṛthivī rasatanmātrādāpo rūpatanmātrāttejaḥ sparśatanmātrādvāyuḥ śabdatanmātrādākāśamityevamutpannānyetāni mahābhūtānyete viśeṣā mānuṣāṇāṃ viṣayāḥ śāntā sukhalakṣaṇā ghorā duḥkhalakṣaṇā mūḍhā mohajanakā yathākāśaṃ kasyacidanavakāśādantargṛhādernirgatasya sukhātmakaṃ śāntaṃ bhavati tadeva śītoṣṇavātavarṣābhibhūtasya duḥkhātmakaṃ ghoraṃ bhavati tadeva panthānaṃ gacchato vanamārgāt bhraṣṭasya diṅ mohānmūḍhaṃ bhavati / evaṃ vāyurgharmārtasya śānto bhavati śītārtasya ghoro dhūlīśarkarāvimiśro 'tivān mūḍha iti / evaṃ tejaḥ prabhṛtiṣu draṣṭavyam // 38 //
children.translated_text: The five <s>tanmātras</s> that arise from <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> are: the <s>śabda-tanmātra</s> (sound), <s>sparśa-tanmātra</s> (touch), <s>rūpa-tanmātra</s> (form), <s>rasa-tanmātra</s> (taste), and <s>gandha-tanmātra</s> (smell) — these are called <s>aviśeṣas</s> (non-specific). For the gods, these are objects characterized by pleasure alone, free from suffering and delusion. From these five <s>tanmātras</s>, the five <s>mahābhūtas</s> (gross elements) arise, designated as <s>pṛthivī</s> (earth), <s>ap</s> (water), <s>tejas</s> (fire), <s>vāyu</s> (air), and <s>ākāśa</s> (space). These are known as <s>viśeṣas</s> (specific). From the <s>gandha-tanmātra</s> arises <s>pṛthivī</s>; from the <s>rasa-tanmātra</s>, <s>āpas</s>; from the <s>rūpa-tanmātra</s>, <s>tejas</s>; from the <s>sparśa-tanmātra</s>, <s>vāyu</s>; from the <s>śabda-tanmātra</s>, <s>ākāśa</s> — thus these <s>mahābhūtas</s> arise. These <s>viśeṣas</s> are the objects of humans — 'tranquil' means characterized by pleasure; 'turbulent' means characterized by suffering; 'stupefying' means producing delusion. For example, <s>ākāśa</s> (space) is tranquil and pleasurable for someone who comes out from a confined indoor space; that same [space] becomes turbulent and painful for one afflicted by cold, heat, wind, or rain; that same [space] becomes stupefying due to the delusion of direction for a traveler who has lost his way in a forest path. Likewise, <s>vāyu</s> (air) is tranquil for one oppressed by heat; turbulent for one oppressed by cold; and stupefying when mixed with dust and pebbles and excessively violent. The same should be understood for <s>tejas</s> (fire) and the rest. // 38 //
Now, the other <s>viśeṣas</s> (specific [bodies]):

children.text: sūkṣmā mātāpitṛjāḥ saha prabhūtaistridhā viśeṣāḥ syuḥ /
children.translated_text: Subtle, born of mother and father, together with gross [elements] — <s>viśeṣas</s> (specific bodies) are threefold.
Of these, the subtle ones are permanent; those born of mother and father are subject to destruction. || 39 ||

children.text: sūkṣmāstanmātrāṇi yatsaṃgṛhītaṃ tanmātrikaṃ sūkṣmaśarīraṃ mahadādiliṅgaṃ sadā tiṣṭhati saṃsarati ca te sūkṣmāstathā mātāpitṛjā sthūlaśarīropacāyakā ṛtukāle mātāpitṛsaṃyoge śoṇitaśukramiśrībhāvenodarāntaḥ sūkṣmaśarīrasyopacayaṃ kurvīta tat sūkṣmaśarīraṃ punarmāturaśitapītanānāvidharasena nābhīnibandhenāpyāyate tathā prārabdhaṃ śarīraṃ sūkṣmairmātāpitṛjaiśca saha mahābhūtaistrividhā viśeṣaiḥ pṛṣṭhodarajaṃghākaṭyuraḥ śiraḥ prabhṛti ṣāṭ kauśikaṃ pañcabhautikaṃ rudhiramāṃsasnāyuśukrāsthimajjāsaṃbhṛtamākāśo 'vakāśadānādvāyurvarddhanāt tejaḥ pākādāpaḥ saṃgrahātpṛthivī dhāraṇāt samastāvayavopetaṃ māturudarādbahirbhavati / evamete trividhā viśeṣā syuḥ / atrāha ke nityāḥ ke vānityāḥ sūkṣmāsteṣāṃ niyatāḥ sūkṣmāstanmātrasaṃjñakāsteṣāṃ madhye niyatā nityāstairārabdhaṃ śarīraṃ karmavaśāt paśumṛgapakṣisarīsṛpasthāvarajātiṣu saṃsarati dharmavaśādindrakādilokeṣvevametanniyataṃ sūkṣmaśarīraṃ sarati yāvat jñānamutpadyate utpanne jñāne vidvāṃñcharīraṃ tyaktvā mokṣaṃ gacchati tasmādete viśeṣā sūkṣmā nityā iti mātāpitṛjā nivartante tat sūkṣmaśarīraṃ parityajyehaiva prāṇatyāgavelāyāṃ mātāpitṛjā nivartante maraṇakāle mātāpitṛjaṃ śarīramihaiva nivarttya bhūmyādiṣu pralīyate yathā tattvaṃ // 39 //
children.translated_text: 'Subtle' refers to the <s>tanmātras</s> — the subtle body (<s>sūkṣma-śarīra</s>) composed of <s>tanmātras</s>, the <s>liṅga</s> (indicator) beginning with <s>Mahat</s>, always persists and transmigrates. And 'born of mother and father' — those that nourish the gross body: at the appropriate season, through the union of mother and father, through the mixture of blood and semen, within the womb, [the elements] produce the growth of the subtle body; that subtle body is then nourished through the umbilical cord by the various juices of what the mother has eaten and drunk; the body thus begun [develops] through subtle [elements] from the mother and father
And how does the subtle [body] transmigrate? He says:
Produced at the beginning [of creation], unattached, permanent, extending from <s>Mahat</s> down to the subtle [elements],
the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) transmigrates without [direct] experience, imbued with <s>bhāvas</s> (dispositions). || 40 ||

children.text: yadā lokānupannāḥ pradhānādisarge tadā sūkṣmaśarīramutpannamiti / kiṃcānyadasaktaṃ na saṃyuktaṃ tiryagyonidevamānuṣasthāneṣu sūkṣmatvāt kutracidasaktaṃ parvatādiṣvapratihataprasaraṃ sarti gacchati / nityaṃ yāvannajñānamutpadyate tāvat saṃsarati tacca mahadādisūkṣmaparyantaṃ mahānādau yasya tanmahadādi buddhirahaṃkāro mana iti pañca tanmātrāṇi sūkṣmaparyantaṃ tanmātraparyantaṃ saṃsarati śūlagrahapipīlikāvat trīnapi lokān / nirupabhogaṃ bhogarahitaṃ tat sūkṣmaśarīraṃ pitṛmātṛjena bāhyenopacayena kriyādharmagrahaṇāt bhogeṣu samarthaṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ / bhāvairadhivāsitaṃ purastādbhāvān dharmādīn vakṣyāmastairadhivāsitamuparaṃjitaṃ liṃgamiti / pralayakāle mahadādisūkṣmaparyantaṃ karaṇopetaṃ pradhāne līyate asaṃsaraṇayuktaṃ sadā sargakālamatra varttate prakṛtimohabandhanabaddhaṃ sat saṃsaraṇādikriyāsvasamarthamiti punaḥ sargakāle saṃsarati tasmālliṃgaṃ sūkṣmam // 40 //
children.translated_text: When the worlds had not yet been produced, at the time of the creation from <s>Pradhāna</s> and so forth, then the subtle body was produced. Moreover, it is 'unattached' — not bound; due to its subtlety, it is unattached to any [specific] station among animals, gods, or humans — it moves and goes unobstructed even through mountains and the like, penetrating [everything]. It is 'permanent' — it transmigrates as long as knowledge has not arisen. And it extends 'from <s>Mahat</s> down to the subtle [elements]' — that which has <s>Mahat</s> and the rest at its beginning is 'beginning with <s>Mahat</s>': <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-sense), <s>Manas</s> (mind), the five <s>tanmātras</s> — the subtle

children.text: kiṃ prayojanena trayodaśavidhaṃ karaṇaṃ saṃsaratītyevaṃ codite satyāha /
children.translated_text: When it is objected: 'For what purpose does the thirteenfold instrument transmigrate?' — he says:

children.text: citraṃ yathāśrayamṛte sthāṇvādibhyo yathā vinā chāyā /
children.translated_text: Just as a painting does not stand without a support, and just as a shadow [does not stand] without posts and the like,
so too, without the <s>viśeṣas</s> (specific elements), the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) does not stand without a support. || 41 ||

children.text: citraṃ yathā kuḍyāśrayamṛte na tiṣṭhati sthāṇvādibhyaḥ kīlakādibhyo vinā chāyā na tiṣṭhati tairvinā na bhavatyādigrahaṇādyathā śaityaṃ vinā nāpo bhavanti śaityaṃ vādbhirvinā / agniruṣṇaṃ vinā vāyuḥ sparśaṃ vinā ākāśamavakāśaṃ vinā pṛthivī gandhaṃ vinā tadvadetena dṛṣṭāntena nyāyana vinā viśeṣairaviśeṣaistanmātrairvinā na tiṣṭhati / atha viśeṣabhūtānyucyante śarīraṃ pañcabhūtamayaṃ vaiśeṣiṇā śarīreṇa vinā kva liṅgasthānaṃ ceti kva ekadehamujjhati tadevānyamāśrayati nirāśrayamāśrayarahitaṃ liṅgaṃ trayodaśa vidhaṃ karaṇamityarthaḥ // 41 //
children.translated_text: Just as a painting does not stand without the support of a wall, and a shadow does not stand without posts, pegs, and the like — without them it does not exist; and by the word 'and so forth' [further examples are given]: just as water does not exist without coldness, nor coldness without water; fire without heat; air without touch; space without giving room; earth without smell — so by this illustration, the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) does not stand without the <s>viśeṣas</s> (specific elements), that is, without the <s>aviśeṣas</s> (non-specific), the <s>tanmātras</s>. Now, [regarding] the specific elements —
For what purpose is this stated?
This [creation functions] for the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>, through the connection of cause and effect;
the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) operates like a dancer, through the capacity of <s>Prakṛti's</s> pervasive power. || 42 ||

children.text: puruṣārthaḥ kartavya iti pradhānaṃ pravarttate sa ca dvividhaḥ śabdādyupalabdhilakṣaṇo guṇapuruṣāntaro labdhilakṣaṇaśca / śabdādyupalabdhirbrahmādiṣu lokeṣu gandhādibhogāvāptiḥ guṇapuruṣāntaropalabdhirmokṣa iti tasamāduktaṃ puruṣārthahetukamidaṃ sūkṣmaśarīraṃ pravarttata iti / nimittanaimittikaprasaṃgena nimittaṃ dharmādi naimittikamūrddhvagamanādi purastādeva vakṣyāmaḥ prasaṃgena prasaktyā prakṛteḥ pradhānasya vibhutvayogādyathā rājā svarāṣṭre vibhutvādyadyadicchati tattat karotīti tathā prakṛteḥ sarvatra vibhutvayogānnimittanaimittakaṃ prasaṃgena vyavatiṣṭhate pṛthak pṛthagdehadhāraṇe liṅgasya vyavasthāṃ karoti / liṃgaṃ sūkṣmaḥ paramāṇubhistanmātrairūpacitaṃ śarīraṃ trayodaśavidhakaraṇopetaṃ mānuṣadevatiryagyoniṣu vyavatiṣṭhate kathaṃ naṭavat yathā naṭaḥ paṭāntareṇa praviśya devo bhūtvā nirgacchati punarmānuṣaḥ punarvidūṣakaḥ / evaṃ liṃgaṃ nimittanaimittikaprasaṃgenodarāntaḥ praviśya hastī strī pumān bhavati // 42 //
children.translated_text: The purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> is to be accomplished — thus <s>Pradhāna</s> operates. And that [purpose] is twofold: characterized by the experience of sound and the like, and characterized by the attainment of the distinction between the <s>guṇas</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>. The experience of sound and the like means the attainment of the enjoyment of smell and other [sensory experiences] in the worlds of <s>Brahmā</s> and so forth; the attainment of the distinction between the <s>guṇas</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> is liberation. Therefore it is stated: 'This [subtle body] operates for the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>.' 'Through the connection of cause and effect' — the cause is <s>dharma</s> (virtue) and the like; the effect is upward movement [through higher realms] and the like.

children.text: bhāvairadhivāsitaṃ liṃgaṃ saṃsaratītyuktaṃ tat ke bhāvā ityāha /
children.translated_text: It was stated that 'the <s>liṅga</s> transmigrates imbued with <s>bhāvas</s> (dispositions).' What are those <s>bhāvas</s>? He says:
The <s>bhāvas</s> are innate (<s>sāṃsiddhika</s>), natural (<s>prākṛtika</s>), and modified (<s>vaikṛtika</s>) — <s>dharma</s> (virtue) and the rest.
They are observed as residing in the instrument [<s>karaṇa</s>]; and those residing in the effect — beginning with the embryonic stage (<s>kalala</s>). || 43 ||

children.text: bhāvāstrividhāścintyante sāṃsiddhikāḥ prākṛtā vaikṛtāśca / tatra sāṃsiddhikā yathā bhavagataḥ kapilasyādisarge utpadyamānasya catvāro bhāvāḥ sahotpannāḥ dharmo jñānaṃ vairāgyamaiśvaryamiti / prākṛtāḥ kathyante brahmaṇaścatvāraḥ putrāḥ sanakasanandanasanātanasanatkumārā babhūvuḥ / teṣāmutpannakāryakāraṇānāṃ śarīriṇāṃ ṣoḍaśavarṣāṇāmete bhāvāścatvāraḥ samutpannāstasmādete prākṛtāḥ / tathā vaikṛtā yathā ācāryamūrttiṃ nimittaṃ kṛtvāsmadādīnāṃ jñānamutpadyate jñānādvairāgyaṃ vairāgyāddharmo dharmādaiśvaryamiti / ācāryamūrttirapi vikṛtiriti tasmādvaikṛtā ete bhāvā ucyante yairadhivāsitaṃ liṅgaṃ saṃsarati ete catvāro bhāvāḥ sātvikāstāmasāviparītāḥ sāttvikametadrūpaṃ tāmasamasmādviparyastamityatra vyākhyātā evamaṣṭau dharmo jñānaṃ vairāgyamaiśvaryamadharmo 'jñānamavairāgyamanaiśvaryamityaṣṭau bhāvāḥ / etaduktamadhyavasāyo buddhiḥ dharmo jñānamiti kāryaṃ dehastadāśrayāḥ kalalādyā ye mātṛjā ityuktāḥ śukraśoṇitasaṃyoge vivṛddhihetukāḥ kalalādyā budbudamāṃsapeśīprabhṛtayaḥ / tathā kaumārayauvanasthaviratvādayo bhāvā annapānarasanimittā niṣpadyanta ataḥ kāryāśrayiṇa ucyanta annādiviṣayabhoganimittā jāyante // 43 //
children.translated_text: The <s>bhāvas</s> (dispositions) are considered to be of three kinds: <s>sāṃsiddhika</s> (innate), <s>prākṛta</s> (natural), and <s>vaikṛta</s> (acquired). Among these, the <s>sāṃsiddhika</s> are as follows: the blessed <s>Kapila</s>, at the beginning of creation, when being born, had four <s>bhāvas</s> arisen simultaneously with him — <s>dharma</s> (merit), <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), and <s>aiśvarya</s> (sovereignty). The <s>prākṛta</s> are described thus: <s>Brahmā</s> had four sons — <s>Sanaka</s>, <s>Sanandana</s>, <s>Sanātana</s>, and <s>Sanatkumāra</s>. For them, as embodied beings in whom cause and effect had arisen, at the age of sixteen years these four <s>bhāvas</s> arose; therefore these are called <s>prākṛta</s>. Likewise the <s>vaikṛta</s> are as follows: taking the form of a teacher as the instrumental cause, knowledge arises in people such as ourselves; from knowledge comes dispassion, from dispassion comes merit, and from merit comes sovereignty. Since the teacher's form is itself a modification (<s>vikṛti</s>), therefore these <s>bhāvas</s> are called <s>vaikṛta</s>. The <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) transmigrates pervaded by these dispositions. These four <s>bhāvas</s> are <s>sāttvika</s> (of the nature of <s>sattva</s>); the <s>tāmasa</s> (of the nature of <s>tamas</s>) are their opposites. The <s>sāttvika</s> form is as described; the <s>tāmasa</s> is the reverse of this — thus it has been explained. In this way there are eight: <s>dharma</s> (merit), <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), <s>aiśvarya</s> (sovereignty), <s>adharma</s> (demerit), <s>ajñāna</s> (ignorance), <s>avairāgya</s> (attachment), and <s>anaiśvarya</s> (powerlessness) — these are the eight <s>bhāvas</s>. What has been stated is this: determination is <s>buddhi</s> (intellect); <s>dharma</s>, <s>jñāna</s>, and so forth are its functions; the body is the effect, and its substrates are the <s>kalala</s> (embryonic stages) and so on, which are said to be born from the mother — arising from the union of semen and blood, they are the causes of growth, beginning with <s>kalala</s>, then bubble, flesh-mass, and so forth. Likewise, states such as childhood, youth, and old age are produced through the instrumentality of food, drink, and vital essence; therefore they are called dependent on effects. They arise through the instrumentality of enjoyment of objects such as food and the rest.
Regarding the connection of cause and effect that was mentioned, the following is stated here.
By <s>dharma</s> (merit) there is movement upward; movement downward occurs by <s>adharma</s> (demerit);
And by <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) comes <s>apavarga</s> (liberation); from its opposite (<s>ajñāna</s>, ignorance) <s>bandha</s> (bondage) is taught.

children.text: dharmeṇa gamanamūrddhvaṃ dharmaṃ nimittaṃ kṛtvorddhvamupanayati ūrddhvamityaṣṭau sthānāni gṛhyante / tadyathā / brāhmaṃ prājāpatyaṃ saumyamaindraṃ gāndharvaṃ rākṣasaṃ paiśācamiti tat sūkṣmaṃ śarīraṃ gacchati paśumṛgapakṣisarīsṛpasthāvarānteṣvadharmo nimittam / kiṃca jñānena cāpavargaśca pañcaviṃśatitattvajñānaṃ tena nimittenāpavargo mokṣaḥ tataḥ sūkṣmaṃ śarīraṃ nivartate paramātmā ucyate / viparyayādiṣyate bandhaḥ ajñānaṃ nimittaṃ sa caiṣa naimittikaḥ prākṛto vaikāriko dākṣiṇikaśca bandha iti vakṣyati purastāt yadidamuktam / 'prākṛtena ca bandhena tathā vaikārikeṇa ca / dakṣiṇābhistṛtīyena baddho nānyena mucyate'; // 44 //
children.translated_text: By <s>dharma</s> there is movement upward — taking <s>dharma</s> as the instrumental cause, it leads upward. 'Upward' means eight stations are understood, namely: <s>brāhma</s> (of <s>Brahmā</s>), <s>prājāpatya</s> (of <s>Prajāpati</s>), <s>saumya</s> (of <s>Soma</s>), <s>aindra</s> (of <s>Indra</s>), <s>gāndharva</s> (of the <s>Gandharvas</s>), <s>rākṣasa</s> (of the <s>Rākṣasas</s>), and <s>paiśāca</s> (of the <s>Piśācas</s>) — to these the subtle body goes. Among animals, deer, birds, reptiles, and immobile beings, <s>adharma</s> is the cause. Furthermore, by <s>jñāna</s> comes <s>apavarga</s> — knowledge of the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s> (principles); by that instrumental cause comes <s>apavarga</s>, which is <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation); from that the subtle body ceases — this is called the supreme self (<s>paramātman</s>). From the opposite (<s>viparyaya</s>) <s>bandha</s> (bondage) is taught — <s>ajñāna</s> (ignorance) is the cause. And this bondage, which is caused, will be described ahead as <s>prākṛta</s> (natural), <s>vaikārika</s> (modified), and <s>dākṣiṇika</s> (meritorious) bondage, as has been stated: 'By natural bondage and likewise by modified bondage, and by the third consisting of meritorious gifts — one who is bound is not freed by any other means.'
And there is yet another cause.
From <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion) comes dissolution into <s>Prakṛti</s>; <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) occurs from <s>rāga</s> (attachment) born of <s>rajas</s>;
From <s>aiśvarya</s> (sovereignty) comes unobstructedness; from its opposite comes the reverse of that.

children.text: yathā kasyacidvairāgyamasti na tattvajñānaṃ tasmādajñānapūrvādvairāgyāt prakṛtilayo mṛto 'ṣṭāsu prakṛtiṣu pradhānabuddhyahaṅkāratanmātreṣu līyate na mokṣaḥ tato bhūyo 'pi saṃsarati / tathā yo 'yaṃ rājaso rāgaḥ yajāmi dakṣiṇāṃ dadāmi yenāmuṣmiṃlloke 'tra yaddivyaṃ mānuṣaṃ sukhamanubhavāmyetasmādrājasādrāgāt saṃsāro bhavati / tathā aiśvaryādavighātaḥ etadaiśvaryamaṣṭaguṇamaṇimādiyuktaṃ tasmādaiśvaryanimittādavighāto naimittiko bhavati brāhmādiṣu sthāneṣvaiśvaryaṃ na vihanyate / kiṃcānyadviparyayādviparyāsaḥ tasyāvighātastasya viparyāso vighāto bhavatyanaiśvaryāt sarvatra vihanyate / kiṃcānyadviparyādviparyāsaḥ syāvighātasya viparyāso vighāto bhavatyanaiśvaryāt sarvatra vihanyate // 45 //
children.translated_text: Just as someone may possess <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion) but not <s>tattvajñāna</s> (knowledge of the principles) — from such dispassion preceded by ignorance, the one who has died dissolves into the eight <s>prakṛtis</s>: <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter), <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego), and the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements). This is not <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation); from there one transmigrates again. Likewise, the <s>rājasa</s> attachment — 'I shall sacrifice, I shall give gifts' — by which one experiences divine and human pleasures in the other world and this world; from such <s>rājasa</s> attachment, <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) occurs. Likewise, from <s>aiśvarya</s> (sovereignty) comes unobstructedness — this sovereignty endowed with the eight powers beginning with <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness); from sovereignty as the instrumental cause, unobstructedness that is caused arises — in stations such as that of <s>Brahmā</s> and others, sovereignty is not obstructed. Furthermore, from the opposite comes the reverse — the reverse of that unobstructedness is obstruction, which occurs from <s>anaiśvarya</s> (powerlessness); everywhere one is obstructed. Furthermore, from the opposite comes the reverse — the reverse of unobstructedness is obstruction, which occurs from <s>anaiśvarya</s>; everywhere one is obstructed.

children.text: eṣa nimittaiḥ saha naimittikaḥ ṣoḍaśavidho vyākhyātaḥ / sa kimātmaka ityāha /
children.translated_text: This caused [creation], together with its causes, has been explained as being of sixteen kinds. What is its nature? He says:
This is the <s>pratyayasarga</s> (intellectual creation), called <s>viparyaya</s> (error), <s>aśakti</s> (incapacity), <s>tuṣṭi</s> (contentment), and <s>siddhi</s> (attainment);
From the imbalance and friction of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), its subdivisions are fifty.

children.text: yathā eṣa ṣoḍaśavidho nimittanaimittabhedo vyākhyāta eṣa pratyayasarga ucyate / pratyayo buddhirityuktādhyavasāyo buddhirdharmo jñānamityādi sa ca pratyayasargaścaturdhā bhidyate viparyayāśaktituṣṭisiddhākhyabhedāt / tatra saṃśayo 'jñānam / yathā kasyacit sthāṇudarśane sthāṇurayaṃ puruṣo veti saṃśayaḥ / aśaktiryathā / tameva sthāṇuṃ samyadgṛṣṭvā saṃśayaṃ chettuṃ na śaknotītyaśaktiḥ / evaṃ tṛtīyastuṣṭyākhyo yathā / tameva sthāṇuṃ jñātuṃ saṃśayituṃ vā necchati kimanenāsmākamityeṣā tuṣṭiḥ / caturthaḥ siddhākhyo yathā / ānanditendriyaḥ sthāṇumārūḍhāṃ valliṃ paśyati śakuniṃ vā tasya siddhirbhavati sthāṇurayamiti / evamasya caturvidhasya pratyayasargasya guṇavaiṣamyavimardde tasya bhedāstu pañcāśat yo 'yaṃ sattvarajastamoguṇānāṃ vaiṣamyo vimarddaḥ tena tasya pratyayasargasya pañcāśadbhedā bhavanti tathā kvāpi sattvamutkaṭaṃ rajastamasī udāsīne kvāpi rajaḥ kvāpi tama iti // 46 //
children.translated_text: As this sixteen-fold division of cause and effect has been explained, this is called the <s>pratyayasarga</s> (intellectual creation). <s>Pratyaya</s> means <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), as stated — determination is <s>buddhi</s>; <s>dharma</s>, <s>jñāna</s>, and so forth. And this intellectual creation is divided fourfold by the distinction into <s>viparyaya</s> (error), <s>aśakti</s> (incapacity), <s>tuṣṭi</s> (contentment), and <s>siddhi</s> (attainment). Among these, <s>viparyaya</s> is doubt or ignorance — for example, when someone sees a post, the doubt arises: 'Is this a post or a person?' <s>Aśakti</s> (incapacity) is as follows: having properly perceived that same post, one is unable to cut through the doubt — this is incapacity. Similarly, the third, called <s>tuṣṭi</s> (contentment), is as follows: one does not even wish to know that post or to doubt it, thinking 'What is this to us?' — this is contentment. The fourth, called <s>siddhi</s> (attainment), is as follows: one with delighted senses sees a creeper climbing the post or a bird upon it, and attainment occurs for him — 'This is a post.' Thus, through the imbalance and friction of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), the subdivisions of this fourfold intellectual creation are fifty — the imbalance and friction of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> produce fifty varieties of that intellectual creation. Thus, in some cases <s>sattva</s> predominates while <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> are dormant; in some cases <s>rajas</s> predominates; in some cases <s>tamas</s>.
The subdivisions are now described.
The subdivisions of <s>viparyaya</s> (error) are five; and those of <s>aśakti</s> (incapacity), due to the deficiency of the <s>karaṇas</s> (organs),
Are twenty-eight; <s>tuṣṭi</s> (contentment) is ninefold; <s>siddhi</s> (attainment) is eightfold.

children.text: pañca viparyayabhedāste yathā tamo moho mahāmohastāmisro 'ndhatāmisra ityeṣāṃ bhedānāṃ nānātvaṃ vakṣyate 'nantarameveti / aśaktestvaṣṭāviṃśatibhedā bhavanti karaṇavaikalyāt tānapi vakṣyāmastathā ca tuṣṭirnavadhā ūrddhvasrotasi rājasāni jñānāni / tathāṣṭavidhā siddhiḥ sāttvikāni jñānāni tatraivorddhvasrotasi / etat krameṇaiva vakṣyante // 47 //
children.translated_text: The five subdivisions of <s>viparyaya</s> (error) are as follows: <s>tamas</s> (darkness), <s>moha</s> (delusion), <s>mahāmoha</s> (great delusion), <s>tāmisra</s> (gloom), and <s>andhatāmisra</s> (blind darkness). The differentiation of these subdivisions will be stated immediately after. The subdivisions of <s>aśakti</s> (incapacity) are twenty-eight, due to the deficiency of the <s>karaṇas</s> (organs) — these too we shall describe. Likewise, <s>tuṣṭi</s> (contentment) is ninefold — in the upward stream, these are <s>rājasic</s> forms of knowledge. And <s>siddhi</s> (attainment) is eightfold — <s>sāttvic</s> forms of knowledge, also in that upward stream. These will be explained in due order.
Now the subdivisions of <s>viparyaya</s> (error) are stated.
The subdivisions of <s>tamas</s> (darkness) are eightfold; <s>moha</s> (delusion) is tenfold; <s>mahāmoha</s> (great delusion)
Is eighteenfold; likewise <s>andhatāmisra</s> (blind darkness) is also [eighteenfold], and <s>tāmisra</s> (gloom) is eighteenfold.

children.text: tamasastāvadaṣṭadhā bhedaḥ pralayo 'jñānādvibhajyate so 'ṣṭāsu prakṛtiṣu līyate pradhānabuddhyahaṃkārapañcatanmātrāṣṭāsu tatra līnamātmānaṃ manyate mukto 'hamiti tamo bheda eṣo 'ṣṭavidhasya mohasya bhedo 'ṣṭavidha evetyarthaḥ / yatrāṣṭaguṇamaṇimādyaiśvaryaṃ tatra saṃgādindrādayo devā na mokṣaṃ prāpnuvanti punaśca tat kṣaye saṃsarantyeṣo 'ṣṭavidho moha iti / daśavidho mahāmohaḥ śabdasparśarūparasagandhā devānāmete pañcaviṣayāḥ sukhalakṣaṇāḥ mānuṣāṇāmapyete eva śabdādayaḥ pañca viṣayā evameteṣu daśasu mahāmoha iti / tāmisro 'ṣṭadaśadhāṣṭāvidhamaiśvaryaṃ dṛṣṭānuśravikā viṣayā daśa eteṣāmaṣṭādaśānāṃ sampadamanunandanti vipadaṃ nānumodantyeṣo 'ṣṭādaśavidho vikalpastāmisro / tathā tāmisramaṣṭaguṇamaiśvaryaṃ dṛṣṭānuśravikā daśaviṣayāstathāndhatāmisro 'pyaṣṭādaśabheda eva kiṃtu viṣayasampattau sambhogakāle ya eva mriyate 'ṣṭaguṇaiśvaryādvā bhraśyate tatastasya mahadduḥkhamutpadyate so 'ndhatāmisra iti / evaṃ viparyayabhedāstamaḥ prabhṛtayaḥ pañca pratyekaṃ bhidyamānā dviṣaṣṭibhedāḥ saṃvṛttā iti // 48 //
children.translated_text: First, <s>tamas</s> (darkness) is eightfold: dissolution from ignorance is divided thus — one dissolves into the eight <s>prakṛtis</s>: <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter), <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego), and the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) — these eight. There, one considers oneself as dissolved, thinking 'I am liberated' — this is the eightfold subdivision of <s>tamas</s>. The subdivision of <s>moha</s> (delusion) is also eightfold in this sense: where there is the eightfold sovereignty of <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness) and other powers, there <s>Indra</s> and other gods, due to attachment, do not attain <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), and when that [sovereignty] is exhausted, they transmigrate again — this is the eightfold <s>moha</s>. <s>Mahāmoha</s> (great delusion) is tenfold: sound, touch, form, taste, and smell — these are the five sense-objects of the gods, characterized by pleasure; and for humans too, these same five beginning with sound are the sense-objects — thus in these ten there is <s>mahāmoha</s>. <s>Tāmisra</s> (gloom) is eighteenfold: the eightfold sovereignty and the ten perceived and heard-of sense-objects — regarding these eighteen, one rejoices in their attainment but does not accept their loss — this eighteenfold alternative is <s>tāmisra</s>. Likewise, <s>andhatāmisra</s> (blind darkness) also has eighteen subdivisions: the eightfold sovereignty and the ten perceived and heard-of sense-objects — but the one who dies at the very time of enjoying the objects, or falls from the eightfold sovereignty, for him great suffering arises — this is <s>andhatāmisra</s>. Thus the subdivisions of <s>viparyaya</s> (error), beginning with <s>tamas</s>, are five, and when each is individually subdivided, they amount to sixty-two varieties in total.
The subdivisions of <s>aśakti</s> (incapacity) are now described.
The disabilities of the eleven <s>indriyas</s> (sense organs), together with the disabilities of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), are designated as <s>aśakti</s> (incapacity);
The disabilities of <s>buddhi</s> are seventeen, being the reverse of <s>tuṣṭi</s> (contentment) and <s>siddhi</s> (attainment).

children.text: bhavantyaśakteśca karaṇavaikalyādaṣṭāviṃśatibhedā ityuddiṣṭaṃ tatraikādaśendriyavadhāḥ bādhiryamandhatāprasuptirupahvikāghrāṇapāko mūkatā kuṇitvaṃ khāṃjyaṃ klaibyamunmāda iti / saha buddhivadhairaśaktiruddiṣṭā ye buddhivadhāstaiḥ sahāśakteraṣṭāviṃśatibhedā bhavanti saptadaśavadhā buddheḥ saptadaśavadhāste tuṣṭibhedasiddhibhedavaiparītyena tuṣṭibhedā nava siddhibhedā aṣṭau ye te viparītaiḥ saha ekādaśa vidhā evamaṣṭāviṃśativikalpā aśaktiriti viparyayāt siddhituṣṭīnāmeva bhedakramo draṣṭavyaḥ // 49 //
children.translated_text: And twenty-eight varieties [of incapacity arise] from the impairment of the senses and the incapacity of the incapable — this has been stated. Therein, the eleven impairments of the sense organs are: deafness, blindness, numbness, loss of taste, destruction of the sense of smell, dumbness, lameness of the hand, lameness of the leg, impotence, and madness. Together with the impairments of <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect), incapacity is stated — with those impairments of <s>Buddhi</s>, the twenty-eight varieties of incapacity arise. The seventeen impairments of <s>Buddhi</s> — the seventeen impairments are the reversals of the varieties of contentment (<s>tuṣṭi</s>) and attainment (<s>siddhi</s>): nine varieties of contentment and eight varieties of attainment, whose reversals, together with the eleven [sense impairments], make twenty-eight varieties of incapacity. Thus, the order of division [for incapacity] should be seen from the [categories of] error through [the reversals of] attainment and contentment. // 49 //
Therein, contentment (<s>tuṣṭi</s>) is described as ninefold:
The internal [contentments] are four, called <s>Prakṛti</s> (nature), <s>Upādāna</s> (means), <s>Kāla</s> (time), and <s>Bhāgya</s> (fortune).
The external ones, arising from abstention from objects, are five — thus nine contentments are declared. || 50 ||

children.text: ādhyātmikāścatasraḥ tuṣṭayo 'dhyātmani bhavā ādhyātmikā tāśca prakṛtyupādānakālabhāgyākhyāḥ / tatra prakṛtyākhyā yathā kaścit prakṛtiṃ vetti tasyāḥ saguṇanirguṇatvaṃ ca tena tattvaṃ tat kāryaṃ vijñāyaiva kevalaṃ tuṣṭastasya nāsti mokṣa eṣā prakṛtyākhyā / upādānākhyā yathā kaścidavijñāyaiva tattvānyupādānagrahaṇaṃ karoti tridaṇḍakamaṇḍaluvividikābhyo mokṣa iti tasyāpi nāstyeṣā upādānākhyā / tathā kālākhyā kālena mokṣo bhaviṣyatīti kiṃ tattvābhyāsenetyeṣā kālākhyā tuṣṭistasya nāsti mokṣa iti / tathā bhāgyākhyā bhāgyenaiva mokṣo bhaviṣyatīti bhāgyākhyā / caturddhā tuṣṭiriti / bāhyāviṣayoparamācca pañca / bāhyāstuṣṭayaḥ pañca viṣayoparamāt śabdasparśarūparasagandhebhya uparato 'rjanarakṣaṇakṣayasaṃgahiṃsādarśanāt / vṛddhinimittaṃ pāśupālyavāṇijyapratigrahasevāḥ kāryā etadarjanaṃ duḥkhamarjitānāṃ rakṣaṇe duḥkhamupabhogāt kṣīyata iti kṣayaduḥkham / tathā viṣayopabhogasaṃge kṛte nāstīndriyāṇāmupaśama iti saṃgadoṣaḥ / tathā na anupahatya bhūtānyupabhoga ityeṣa hiṃsādoṣaḥ / evamarjjanādidoṣadarśanāt pañcaviṣayoparamāt pañca tuṣṭayaḥ / evamādhyātmikabāhyabhedānnava tuṣṭayastāsāṃ nāmāni śāstrāntare proktāni / ambhaḥ salilamogho vṛṣṭiḥ sutamo pāraṃ sunetraṃ nārīkamanuttamāṃbhasikamiti / āsāṃ tuṣṭīnāṃ viparītāśaktibhedādbuddhibadhā bhavanti // 50 //
children.translated_text: The four internal contentments — 'internal' means pertaining to the self. And they are called <s>Prakṛti</s>, <s>Upādāna</s>, <s>Kāla</s>, and <s>Bhāgya</s>. Of these, the one called '<s>Prakṛti</s>' is as follows: someone knows <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) and its states of being with <s>guṇas</s> and without <s>guṇas</s>; having understood that <s>tattva</s> (principle) and its effect, he is merely content — for him there is no liberation; this is the contentment called '<s>Prakṛti</s>.' The one called '<s>Upādāna</s>' (means) is as follows: someone, without having understood the <s>tattvas</s>, takes up material means — [thinking] 'liberation [comes] from the triple staff, water-pot, and sacrificial implements' — for him too there is no [liberation]; this is the one called '<s>Upādāna</s>.' Likewise, the one called '<s>Kāla</s>' (time): 'Liberation will come in due time; what is the need of practicing the <s>tattvas</s>?' — this is the contentment called '<s>Kāla</s>'; for him there is no liberation. Likewise, the one called '<s>Bhāgya</s>' (fortune): 'Liberation will come by fortune alone' — this is the one called '<s>Bhāgya</s>.' Thus contentment is fourfold. And the external ones arising from abstention from objects are five. The five external contentments [arise] from abstention from sound, touch, form, taste, and smell, due to seeing the faults of acquisition, preservation, decay, attachment, and injury. Activities such as animal-keeping, trade, receiving gifts, and service must be performed for the purpose of increase — this is the suffering of acquisition; preserving what has been acquired involves suffering; through enjoyment [things] are diminished — this is the suffering of decay. Likewise, when attachment to the enjoyment of objects is formed, there is no peace for the senses — this is the fault of attachment. Likewise, one cannot enjoy without harming beings — this is the fault of injury. Thus, from seeing the faults of acquisition and the rest, the five contentments [arise] from abstention from the five objects. Thus, from the division into internal and external, the nine contentments [are established]. Their names are stated in another treatise: <s>Ambhas</s> (water), <s>Salila</s> (stream), <s>Ogha</s> (flood), <s>Vṛṣṭi</s> (rain), <s>Sutamas</s>, <s>Pāra</s>, <s>Sunetra</s>, <s>Nārīkama</s>, and <s>Anuttamāmbhasika</s>. From the reversal of these contentments, the impairments of <s>Buddhi</s> arise through the varieties of incapacity. // 50 //
That is, from the reversal — 'not-<s>Ambhas</s>,' 'not-<s>Salila</s>,' 'not-<s>Ogha</s>,' and so on — arise the impairments of <s>Buddhi</s>. Now attainment (<s>siddhi</s>) is stated:
Reasoning, verbal instruction, study, the threefold removal of suffering, the attainment of a friend,
and generosity — these are the eight attainments; the goad that precedes attainment is threefold. || 51 ||

children.text: ūho yathā kaścinnatyamūhate kimiha satyaṃ kiṃ paraṃ kiṃ naiśreyasaṃ kiṃ kṛtārthaḥ syāmiti cintayato jñānamutpadyate pradhānādanya eva puruṣa ityanyā buddhiranyo 'haṃkāro 'nyāni tanmātrāṇīndriyāṇi pañcamahābhūtānītyevaṃ tattvajñānamutpadyate yena mokṣo bhavati eṣā ūhākhyā prathamā siddhiḥ / tathā śabdajñānāt pradhānapuruṣabuddhyahaṃkāratanmātrendriyapañcamahābhūtaviṣayaṃ jñānaṃ bhavati tato mokṣa ityeṣā śabdākhyā siddhiḥ / adhyayanādvedādiśāstrādhyayanāt pañcaviṃśatitattvajñānaṃ prāpya mokṣaṃ yāti ityeṣā tṛtīyā siddhiḥ / duḥkhavighātatrayamādhyātmikādhibhautikādhidaivikaduḥkhatrayavighātāya guruṃ samupagamya tata upadeśānmokṣaṃ yātyeṣā caturthī siddhiḥ / eṣaiva duḥkhatrayabhedāt tridhā kalpanīyā iti ṣaṭ siddhayaḥ / tathā suhṛtprāptiryathā kaścit suhṛt jñānamadhigamya mokṣaṃ gacchati eṣā saptamī siddhiḥ / dānaṃ yathā kaścidbhagavatāṃ pratyāśrayauṣadhitridaṇḍakuṇḍikādīnāṃ grāsācchādanādīnāṃ ca dānenopakṛtya tebhyo jñānamavāpya mokṣaṃ yātyeṣāṣṭamī siddhiḥ / āsāmaṣṭānāṃ siddhīnāṃ śāstrāntare saṃjñāḥ kṛtāstāraṃ sutāraṃ tāratāraṃ pramodaṃ pramuditaṃ pramodamānaṃ ramyakaṃ sadāpramuditamiti / āsāṃ viparyayāt budderbandhā ye viparītāsta aśaktau nikṣiptā yathātāramasutāramatāratāramityādidraṣṭavyamaśaktibhedā aṣṭāviṃśatiruktāste saha buddhibandhairekādaśendriyabandhā iti / tatra tuṣṭiviparyayā nava siddhīnāṃ viparyayā aṣṭau evamete saptadaśa buddhibandhā etaiḥ sahendriyabandhā aṣṭāviṃśatiraśaktibhedāḥ paścāt kathitā iti viparyayāśaktituṣṭisiddhīnāmevoddeśo nirdeśaśca kṛta iti / kiṃ cānyat siddheḥ pūrvo 'ṅkuśastrividhaḥ siddheḥ pūrvā yā viparyayāśaktituṣṭayastā eva siddheraṃkuśastadbhedādevaṃ trividho yathā hastī gṛhītāṃkuśena vaśo bhavatyeva viparyayāśaktituṣṭibhirgṛhīto loko 'jñānamāpnoti tasmādetāḥ parityajya siddhiḥ sevyā sasiddhestattvajñānamutpadyate tanmokṣa iti // 51 //
children.translated_text: Reasoning (<s>ūha</s>): for example, someone constantly reasons — 'What is the truth here? What is supreme? What is the highest good? How may I become fulfilled?' — and from such reflection, knowledge arises: '<s>Puruṣa</s> is indeed different from <s>Pradhāna</s>; <s>Buddhi</s> is different, <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> is different, the <s>tanmātras</s>, the <s>indriyas</s>, and the five <s>mahābhūtas</s> are different' — thus the knowledge of the <s>tattvas</s> arises, by which liberation occurs; this is the first attainment, called 'reasoning.' Likewise, from verbal knowledge (<s>śabda</s>) — from the knowledge of <s>Pradhāna</s>, <s>Puruṣa</s>, <s>Buddhi</s>, <s>Ahaṃkāra</s>, <s>tanmātras</s>, <s>indriyas</s>, and the five <s>mahābhūtas</s> — knowledge pertaining to [these] arises; from that, liberation — this is the attainment called '<s>śabda</s>' (verbal instruction). From study (<s>adhyayana</s>) — from the study of the <s>Vedas</s> and other scriptures, having attained the knowledge of the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s>, one goes to liberation — this is the third attainment. The threefold removal of suffering — for the removal of the threefold suffering (<s>ādhyātmika</s>, <s>ādhibhautika</s>, <s>ādhidaivika</s>), one approaches a teacher, and from his instruction one goes to liberation — this is the fourth attainment; this very same [attainment], because of the division of the threefold suffering, should be considered as three — thus there are six attainments. Likewise, the attainment of a friend (<s>suhṛtprāpti</s>): for example, a certain friend, having attained knowledge, goes to liberation — this is the seventh attainment. Generosity (<s>dāna</s>): for example, someone, having served the venerable ones with gifts of medicines, triple staffs, water-pots, food, clothing, and the like, and having thereby obtained knowledge from them, goes to liberation — this is the eighth attainment. The names of these eight attainments are given in another treatise: <s>Tāra</s>, <s>Sutāra</s>, <s>Tāratāra</s>, <s>Pramoda</s>, <s>Pramudita</s>, <s>Pramodamāna</s>, <s>Ramyaka</s>, and <s>Sadāpramudita</s>. From the reversal of these, the bonds of <s>Buddhi</s> arise — those which are reversed are placed under incapacity: 'not-<s>Tāra</s>,' 'not-<s>Sutāra</s>,' 'not-<s>Tāratāra</s>,' and so on should be understood as the varieties of incapacity. The twenty-eight [varieties of] incapacity have been stated — they, together with the <s>Buddhi</s>-bonds, are the eleven sense-bonds. Of these, the reversals of the nine contentments and the reversals of the eight attainments — thus these seventeen are the <s>Buddhi</s>-bonds; together with the sense-bonds, they make the twenty-eight varieties of incapacity as stated later.
