Thus the enumeration and exposition of error, incapacity, contentment, and attainment have been made. Moreover, 'the goad that precedes attainment is threefold' — the error, incapacity, and contentments that precede attainment are themselves the goad of attainment; being of three kinds, they are thus threefold. Just as an elephant is brought under control by a goad, so too the world, seized by error, incapacity, and contentment, attains ignorance; therefore, abandoning these, one should pursue attainment; from attainment, knowledge of the <s>tattvas</s> arises; that is liberation. // 51 //

children.text: atha yaduktaṃ bhāvairadhivāsitaṃ liṃgaṃ tatra bhāvā dharmādayo 'ṣṭāvuktā buddhipariṇāmā viparyayāśaktituṣṭisiddhipariṇatāḥ sa bhāvākhyaḥ pratyayasargaḥ liṃgaṃ ca tanmātrasargaścaturdaśabhūtaparyanta uktastatraikenaiva sargeṇa puruṣārthasiddhau kimubhayavidhasargeṇetyata āha /
children.translated_text: Now, it was stated that 'the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) transmigrates imbued with <s>bhāvas</s> (dispositions).' The eight <s>bhāvas</s> beginning with <s>dharma</s> have been stated as transformations of <s>Buddhi</s>, transformed as error, incapacity, contentment, and attainment. That is called the <s>bhāva</s>-creation (intellectual creation). And the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body), the <s>tanmātra</s>-creation, the fourteen [worlds] down to the elements — [all this] has been stated. If the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> can be accomplished by one creation alone, why [is there need for] both types of creation? Therefore he says:

children.text: na vinā bhāvairliṅgaṃ na vinā liṅgena bhāvanirvṛttiḥ /
children.translated_text: Without the <s>bhāvas</s> (dispositions), the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) [cannot function]; without the <s>liṅga</s>, the <s>bhāvas</s> are not accomplished.
Therefore a twofold creation proceeds — called the <s>liṅga</s>-[creation] and the <s>bhāva</s>-[creation]. || 52 ||

children.text: bhāvaiḥ pratyayasargairvinā liṃgaṃ na tanmātrasargo na pūrvapūrvasaṃskārādṛṣṭakāritatvāduttarottaradehalambhasya liṃgena tanmātrasargeṇa ca vinā bhāvanirvṛttirna sthūlasūkṣmadehasādhyatvāddharmāderanāditvācca sargasya bījāṃkurāvanyonyāśrayau na doṣāya tattajjātīyāpekṣitatve 'pi tattadvyaktīnāṃ parasparānapekṣitvāttasmādbhāvākhyo liṃgākhyaśca dvividhaḥ pravarttate sarga iti // 52 //
children.translated_text: Without the <s>bhāvas</s> — the intellectual creation — the <s>liṅga</s>, the <s>tanmātra</s>-creation, does not [function]; because the attainment of successive bodies is caused by the <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit/demerit) produced by prior dispositions. And without the <s>liṅga</s> — the <s>tanmātra</s>-creation — the <s>bhāvas</s> are not accomplished, because <s>dharma</s> and the rest are accomplished through gross and subtle bodies, and because creation is beginningless — the seed and sprout, mutually dependent, do not constitute a fault, since although each class depends on the other, individual instances do not depend on each other. Therefore a twofold creation proceeds — called the <s>bhāva</s>-[creation] and the <s>liṅga</s>-[creation]. // 52 //
Moreover:
The divine [creation] is eightfold; the animal [creation] is fivefold.
And the human [creation] is of one kind — this, in brief, is the elemental (<s>bhautika</s>) creation. || 53 ||

children.text: tatra daivamaṣṭaprakāraṃ brāhmaṃ prājāpatyaṃ saumyamaindraṃ gāndharvaṃ yākṣaṃ rākṣasaṃ paiśācamiti / paśumṛgapakṣisarīsṛpasthāvarāṇi bhūtānyeva pañcavidhastairaśca / mānuṣayonirekaiva iti caturdaśabhūtāni // 53 //
children.translated_text: Therein, the divine is of eight kinds: <s>Brāhma</s>, <s>Prājāpatya</s>, <s>Saumya</s>, <s>Aindra</s>, <s>Gāndharva</s>, <s>Yākṣa</s>, <s>Rākṣasa</s>, and <s>Paiśāca</s>. Domestic animals, wild animals, birds, reptiles, and plants — these beings constitute the fivefold animal [creation]. And the human birth is just one kind. Thus [there are] fourteen types of beings. // 53 //

children.text: triṣvapi lokeṣu guṇatrayamasti tatra kasmin kimadhikamucyate /
children.translated_text: In all three worlds the triad of <s>guṇas</s> exists. Which [<s>guṇa</s>] is predominant in which [world]? This is stated:
Above, the creation abounds in <s>sattva</s>; below, from the root, it abounds in <s>tamas</s>;
in the middle, it abounds in <s>rajas</s> — from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass. || 54 ||

children.text: ūrddhvamityaṣṭasu devasthāneṣu sattvaviśālaṃ sattvavistāraḥ sattvotkaṭa ūrddhvasattva iti / tatrāpi rajastamasī staḥ / tamoviśālo mūlataḥ paśvādiṣu sthāvarānteṣu sarvaḥsargastamasādhikyena vyāptastatrāpi sattvarajasī staḥ / madhye mānuṣye raja utkaṭaṃ tatrāpi sattvatamasī vidyete tasmādduḥkhaprāyā manuṣyāḥ / evaṃ brahmādistambaparyantaḥ brahmādisthāvarāntaḥ ityarthaḥ / evamabhautikaḥ sargo liṃgasargo bhāvasargo bhūtasargo daivamānuṣatairyagyonaya ityeṣaḥ pradhānakṛtaḥ ṣoḍaśaḥ sargaḥ // 54 //
children.translated_text: 'Above' means in the eight stations of the gods — <s>sattva</s> abounds, meaning the expansion of <s>sattva</s>, <s>sattva</s> predominant, <s>sattva</s> uppermost. Even there, <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> exist. '<s>Tamas</s> abounds from the root' — in animals and down to plants, all creation is pervaded by a preponderance of <s>tamas</s>; even there, <s>sattva</s> and <s>rajas</s> exist. 'In the middle' — in the human [realm], <s>rajas</s> is predominant; even there, <s>sattva</s> and <s>tamas</s> exist; therefore humans are predominantly characterized by suffering. Thus, 'from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass' means from <s>Brahmā</s> down to plants. Thus the non-elemental creation is the <s>liṅga</s>-creation; the <s>bhāva</s>-creation and the <s>bhūta</s>-creation — divine, human, and animal — this is the sixteenfold creation produced by <s>Pradhāna</s>. // 54 //

children.text: tatra jarāmaraṇakṛtaṃ duḥkhaṃ prāpnoti cetanaḥ puruṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therein, the sentient <s>Puruṣa</s> experiences suffering caused by old age and death,
because of the non-cessation of the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body); therefore, suffering [exists] in brief. || 55 ||

children.text: tatreti teṣu devamānuṣatiryagyoniṣu jarākṛtaṃ maraṇakṛtaṃ caiva duḥkhaṃ cetanaḥ caitanyavān puruṣaḥ prāpnoti na pradhānaṃ na buddhirnāhaṃkāro na tanmātrāṇīndriyāṇi mahābhūtāni ca / kiyantaṃ kālaṃ puruṣo duḥkhaṃ prāpnotīti tadvivinakti / liṃgasyāvinivṛtteryattanmahadādi liṃgaśarīreṇāviśya tatra vyaktībhavati tadyāvannivarttate saṃsāraśarīramiti saṃkṣepeṇa triṣu sthāneṣu puruṣo jarāmaraṇakṛtaṃ duḥkhaṃ prāpnoti liṃgasyāvinivṛtteḥ liṃgasya vinivṛttiṃ yāvat / liṃganivṛttau mokṣo mokṣaprāptau nāsti duḥkhamiti / tatpunaḥ kena nivarttate yadā pañcaviṃśatitattvajñānaṃ syāt sattvapuruṣānyathākhyātilakṣaṇamidaṃ pradhānamiyaṃ buddhirayamahaṃkāra imāni pañcatanmātrāṇyekādaśendriyāṇi pañca mahābhūtāni yebhyo 'nyaḥ puruṣo visadṛśa ityevaṃ jñānālliṃganivṛttistato mokṣa iti // 55 //
children.translated_text: There — in those births among gods, humans, and animals — the conscious one, the <s>Puruṣa</s> possessed of <s>caitanya</s> (consciousness), experiences suffering caused by old age and suffering caused by death; not <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter), not <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect), not <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (ego), not the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements), the <s>indriyas</s> (sense organs), or the <s>mahābhūtas</s> (gross elements). As to how long <s>Puruṣa</s> experiences suffering, he distinguishes thus: due to the non-cessation of the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) — that which, beginning with <s>Mahat</s> and the rest, pervades the <s>liṅga-śarīra</s> (subtle body) and manifests therein — so long as the body of transmigration does not cease. In brief, in the three stations <s>Puruṣa</s> experiences suffering caused by old age and death due to the non-cessation of the <s>liṅga</s>, until the cessation of the <s>liṅga</s>. Upon the cessation of the <s>liṅga</s> there is <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation); upon attaining <s>mokṣa</s> there is no suffering. Then by what means does it cease? When there arises knowledge of the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s> (principles), characterized by the discrimination between <s>Sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> — 'this is <s>Pradhāna</s>, this is <s>Buddhi</s>, this is <s>Ahaṃkāra</s>, these are the five <s>tanmātras</s>, the eleven <s>indriyas</s>, the five <s>mahābhūtas</s>, and distinct from all these is <s>Puruṣa</s>, who is dissimilar' — from such knowledge comes the cessation of the <s>liṅga</s>, and from that, <s>mokṣa</s>. [55]
Beginning with what is the cause of activity, it is stated:
Thus this activity brought about by <s>Prakṛti</s> (primal nature), extending from <s>Mahat</s> and the rest down to the specific gross elements,
is undertaken for the liberation of each <s>Puruṣa</s> — an undertaking that appears to be for its own sake but is actually for the sake of another. [<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 56]

children.text: ityeṣa parisamāptau nirddeśe ca prakṛtivikṛtau prakṛtikaraṇe prakṛtikriyāyāṃ ya ārambho mahadādiviśeṣabhūtaparyantaḥ prakṛtermahān mahato 'haṃkārastasmāttanmātrāṇyekādaśendriyāṇi tanmātrebhyaḥ pañcamahābhūtānītyeṣaḥ pratipuruṣavimokṣārthaṃ puruṣaṃ prati devamanuṣyatiryagbhāvaṃ gatānāṃ vimokṣārthamārambhaḥ kathaṃ svārtha iva parārthamārambhaḥ yathā kaścit svārthaṃ tyaktvā mitrakāryāṇi karoti evaṃ pradhānam / puruṣo 'tra pradhānasya na kiñcit pratyupakāraṃ karoti / svārtha iva na ca svāthaḥ parārtha evārthaḥ śabdādiviṣayopalabdhirguṇapuruṣāntaropalabdhiśca triṣu lokeṣu śabdādiviṣayaiḥ puruṣā yojayitavyā ante ca mokṣeṇeti pradhānasya pravṛttistathā coktam / kumbhavat pradhānaṃ puruṣārthaṃ kṛtvā nivarttata iti // 56 //
children.translated_text: Thus this — in the complete enumeration and exposition of <s>Prakṛti</s> and its modifications, in the instrument of <s>Prakṛti</s>, in the activity of <s>Prakṛti</s> — the undertaking extending from <s>Mahat</s> and the rest down to the specific gross elements: from <s>Prakṛti</s> comes <s>Mahat</s>, from <s>Mahat</s> comes <s>Ahaṃkāra</s>, from that the <s>tanmātras</s> and eleven <s>indriyas</s>, from the <s>tanmātras</s> the five <s>mahābhūtas</s> — this undertaking is for the liberation of each <s>Puruṣa</s>, for the liberation of those who have gone into the conditions of gods, humans, and animals. How is an undertaking that appears to be for its own sake actually for the sake of another? Just as someone abandons his own interests and performs the tasks of a friend, so does <s>Pradhāna</s>. <s>Puruṣa</s> here does nothing in return for <s>Pradhāna</s>. It appears to be for its own sake but is not; the purpose is entirely for the other — the experience of objects such as sound and the rest, and the discrimination between the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) and <s>Puruṣa</s>. In the three worlds, <s>Puruṣas</s> are to be connected with objects such as sound and the rest, and ultimately with <s>mokṣa</s> — such is the activity of <s>Pradhāna</s>. And thus it has been said: 'Like a pot, <s>Pradhāna</s>, having accomplished the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>, ceases.' [56]

children.text: atrocyate 'cetanaṃ pradhānaṃ cetanaḥ puruṣa iti mayā triṣu lokeṣu śabdādibhirviṣayaiḥ puruṣo yojyo 'nte mokṣaḥ karttavya iti kathaṃ cetanavat pravṛtiḥ / satyaṃ kiṃtvacetanānāmapi pravṛttirdṛṣṭā nivṛttiśca yasmādityāha /
children.translated_text: Here it is objected: <s>Pradhāna</s> is non-conscious, <s>Puruṣa</s> is conscious — so when I say that in the three worlds <s>Puruṣa</s> is to be connected with objects such as sound and the rest, and ultimately <s>mokṣa</s> is to be accomplished, how can there be activity as if it were conscious? True, but the activity and cessation of even non-conscious things is observed — therefore he says:
Just as the activity of unintelligent milk is for the purpose of the nourishment of the calf,
so too is the activity of <s>Pradhāna</s> for the purpose of the liberation of <s>Puruṣa</s>. [<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 57]

children.text: yathā tṛṇādikaṃ gavā bhakṣitaṃ kṣīrabhāvena pariṇamya vatsavivṛddhiṃ karoti puṣṭe ca vatse nivarttata evaṃ puruṣavimokṣanimittaṃ pradhānam / ajñasya pravṛttirita // 57 //
children.translated_text: Just as grass and the like, eaten by a cow, transforms into the form of milk and nourishes the calf, and when the calf is nourished it ceases — so too <s>Pradhāna</s> acts for the purpose of the liberation of <s>Puruṣa</s>. This is the activity of the unintelligent. [57]
Moreover:
Just as people engage in activities for the purpose of alleviating restlessness,
so too the <s>Avyakta</s> (unmanifest) engages for the purpose of the liberation of <s>Puruṣa</s>. [<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 58]

children.text: yathā loka ityaustukye sati tasya nivṛttyarthaṃ kriyāsu pravarttate gamanāgamanakriyāsu kṛtakāryo nivarttate tathā puruṣasya vimokṣārthaṃ śabdādiviṣayopabhogopalabdhilakṣaṇaṃ guṇapuruṣāntaropalabdhilakṣaṇaṃ ca dvividhamapi puruṣārthaṃ kṛtvā pradhānaṃ nivartate // 58 //
children.translated_text: Just as people, when restlessness arises, engage in activities for the purpose of its cessation — in activities of going and coming — and having accomplished their purpose, they cease; so too <s>Pradhāna</s>, having accomplished the twofold purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> — characterized by the experience of objects such as sound and the rest, and characterized by the discrimination between the <s>guṇas</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> — ceases. [58]
What else?

children.text: raṅgasya darśayitvā nivartate nartakī yathā nṛtyāt /
children.translated_text: Just as a <s>nartakī</s> (dancer) retires from the dance after having displayed herself to the audience,
so too <s>Prakṛti</s> (nature), having revealed herself to <s>Puruṣa</s>, withdraws. [<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 59]

children.text: yathā narttakī śṛṅgārādirasauritihāsādibhāvaiśca nibaddhagītavāditravṛttāni raṅgasya darśayitvā kṛtakāryā nṛtyānnivarttate tathā prakṛtirapi puruṣasyātmānaṃ prakāśya buddhyahaṃkāratanmātrendiyamahābhūtabhedena nivartate // 59 //
children.translated_text: Just as a <s>nartakī</s> (dancer), having displayed to the audience her compositions of song, instrumental music, and dance bound together with the <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) and other <s>rasas</s> (aesthetic sentiments) and the <s>itihāsa</s> (narrative) and other <s>bhāvas</s> (emotional states), retires from the dance having accomplished her purpose — so too <s>Prakṛti</s>, having revealed herself to <s>Puruṣa</s> in the differentiated forms of <s>Buddhi</s>, <s>Ahaṃkāra</s>, <s>tanmātras</s>, <s>indriyas</s>, and <s>mahābhūtas</s>, withdraws. [59]
How, and what would be the cause of cessation? To this he says:
The <s>guṇavatī</s> (one possessed of qualities, i.e., <s>Prakṛti</s>) serves the <s>Puruṣa</s> who is without qualities, by various means, rendering service to one who renders no service in return;
she acts for the purpose of that one who is purposeless. [<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 60]

children.text: nānāvidhairupāyaiḥ prakṛtiḥ puruṣasyopakāriṇyanupakāriṇaḥ puṃsaḥ kathaṃ devamānuṣatiryagbhāvena sukhaduḥkhamohātmakabhāvena śabdādiviṣayabhāvena evaṃ nānāvidhairupāyairātmānaṃ prakāśyāhamanyā tvamanya iti nivarttate 'to nityasya tasyārthamapārthaṃ kurute carati ca yathā kaścit paropakārī sarvasyopakurute nātmanaḥ pratyupakāramīhata evaṃ prakṛtiḥ puruṣārthaṃ kurute karotyapārthakam // 60 //
children.translated_text: <s>Prakṛti</s>, by various means, serves <s>Puruṣa</s> who renders no service in return — how? By revealing herself through the conditions of gods, humans, and animals, through states consisting of pleasure, pain, and delusion, through the forms of objects such as sound and the rest — having thus revealed herself by various means, she recognizes 'I am different, you are different,' and withdraws. Thus she acts for the purpose of that eternal one, acting without purpose for herself, just as a benefactor serves everyone without seeking anything in return for himself — so <s>Prakṛti</s> accomplishes the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>, acting without self-interest. [60]

children.text: paścāduktamātmānaṃ prakāśya nivarttate nivṛtta ca kiṃ karotītyāha /
children.translated_text: Having previously stated 'having revealed herself, she withdraws,' what does she do once she has withdrawn? He says:

children.text: prakṛteḥ sukumārataraṃ na kiñcidastīti me matirbhavati /
children.translated_text: Nothing is more modest than <s>Prakṛti</s> — such is my understanding;
she who, upon realizing 'I have been seen,' does not again come into the sight of <s>Puruṣa</s>. [<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 61]

children.text: loke prakṛteḥ sukumārataraṃ na kiñcidastītyevaṃ me matirbhavati yena parārtha evaṃ matirutpannā kasmādahamanena puruṣeṇa dṛṣṭāsmītyasya puṃso punardarśanaṃ nopaiti puruṣasyādarśanamupayātītyarthaḥ / tatra sukumārataraṃ varṇayati / īśvaraṃ kāraṇaṃ bruvate / "ajo janturanīśo 'yamātmā naḥ sukhaduḥkhayorīśvaraprerito gacchet svargaṃ narakameva vā //" apare svabhāvakāraṇikāṃ bruvate / kena śuklīkṛtā haṃsā mayūrāḥ kena citritāḥ / svabhāvenaiveti / atra sāṃkhyācāryā āhuḥ nirguṇatvādīśvarasya kathaṃ saguṇataḥ prajā jāyeran kathaṃ vā puruṣānnirguṇādeva tasmāt prakṛteryujyate yathā śuklebhyastantubhyaḥ śukla eva paṭo bhavati kṛṣṇebhyaḥ kṛṣṇa eveti / evaṃ triguṇāt pradhānāt trayo lokāstriguṇāḥ samutpannā iti gamyate / nirguṇa īśvaraḥ saguṇānāṃ lokānāṃ tasmādutpattirayukteti / anena puruṣo vyākhyātaḥ / tathā keṣāṃcit kālaḥ kāraṇamityuktaṃ ca / "kālaḥ pañcāsti bhūtāni kālaḥ saṃharate jagat / kālaḥ supteṣu jāgartti kālo hi duratikramaḥ //" vyaktamavyaktapuruṣāstrayaḥ padārthāstena kālo 'ntarbhūto 'sti sa vyaktaḥ sarvakartṛtvāt kālasyāpi pradhānameva kāraṇaṃ svabhāvo 'pyatraiva līnaḥ tasmāt kālo na kāraṇam / nāpi svabhāva iti / tasmāt prakṛtireva kāraṇaṃ na prakṛteḥ kāraṇāntaramastīti / na punardarśanamupayāti puruṣasya / ataḥ prakṛteḥ sukumārataraṃ subhogyataraṃ na kiñcidīśvarādikāraṇamastīti me matirbhavati // 61 //
children.translated_text: In the world, nothing is more modest (<s>sukumāratara</s>) than <s>Prakṛti</s> — such is my understanding. She, in whom the thought has arisen for the sake of the other, 'I have been seen by this <s>Puruṣa</s>' — does not again come into his sight; she departs from the view of <s>Puruṣa</s>, that is the meaning. Here he elaborates on what is most modest. Some declare <s>Īśvara</s> (God) to be the cause: 'The individual soul is unborn and not sovereign; it is directed by <s>Īśvara</s> to go to heaven or indeed to hell regarding our pleasure and pain.' Others declare <s>svabhāva</s> (inherent nature) to be the cause: 'By whom were swans made white? By whom were peacocks painted? By inherent nature alone.' Here the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> teachers say: since <s>Īśvara</s> is without <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), how can beings possessed of <s>guṇas</s> be born from him? How indeed from <s>Puruṣa</s> who is also without <s>guṇas</s>? Therefore it is fitting that they arise from <s>Prakṛti</s> — just as from white threads comes only a white cloth, and from black threads only a black one. Thus it is understood that from <s>Pradhāna</s> composed of three <s>guṇas</s>, the three worlds composed of three <s>guṇas</s> have arisen. <s>Īśvara</s>, being without <s>guṇas</s>, cannot be the source of worlds that possess <s>guṇas</s> — therefore that origin is unjustified. By this, <s>Puruṣa</s> is also explained. Likewise, some hold <s>Kāla</s> (time) to be the cause, as stated: '<s>Kāla</s> (time) rules over the five elements; <s>Kāla</s> withdraws the world; <s>Kāla</s> is awake when all sleep; <s>Kāla</s> is indeed difficult to transcend.' But the manifest, the unmanifest, and <s>Puruṣa</s> are three categories — time is included within these; it is manifest, because of its being the agent of all. Even for <s>Kāla</s>, <s>Pradhāna</s> alone is the cause; <s>svabhāva</s> too is absorbed in this alone. Therefore <s>Kāla</s> is not the cause, nor is <s>svabhāva</s>. Therefore <s>Prakṛti</s> alone is the cause; there is no other cause beyond <s>Prakṛti</s>. She does not again come into the sight of <s>Puruṣa</s>. Therefore nothing is more modest, more gracious than <s>Prakṛti</s> — not <s>Īśvara</s> or any other cause — such is my understanding. [61]

children.text: tathā ca śloke rūḍham / puruṣo muktaḥ puruṣaḥ saṃsārīti coditetyāha /
children.translated_text: And thus the verse has become established: '<s>Puruṣa</s> is liberated, <s>Puruṣa</s> transmigrates' — to this objection, he says:

children.text: tasmānna badhyate nāpi mucyate nāpi saṃsarati kaścit /
children.translated_text: Therefore no one is ever bound, nor liberated, nor does anyone transmigrate;

children.text: saṃsarati badhyate mucyate ca nānāśrayā prakṛtiḥ || 62 ||
children.translated_text: it is <s>Prakṛti</s>, abiding in various substrates, that transmigrates, is bound, and is liberated. [<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 62]

children.text: tasmāt kāraṇāt puruṣo na badhyate nāpi mucyate nāpi saṃsarati yasmāt kāraṇāt prakṛtireva nānāśrayā daivamānuṣatiryagyonyāśrayā buddhyahaṃkāratanmātrendriyabhūtasvarūpeṇa badhyate mucyate saṃsarati ceti / atha mukta eva svabhāvāt sa sarvagataśca kathaṃ saṃsaratyaprāptaprāpaṇārthaṃ saṃsaraṇamiti tena puruṣo badhyate puruṣo mucyate saṃsarati vyapadiśyate yena saṃsāritvaṃ na vidyate sattvapuruṣāntajñānāt tattvaṃ puruṣasyābhivyajyate / tadabhivyakto kevalaḥ śuddho muktaḥ svarūpapratiṣṭhaḥ puruṣa iti / atra yadi puruṣasya bandho nasti tato mokṣo 'pi nāsti / atrocyate prakṛtirevātmānaṃ badhnāti mocayati ca yatra sūkṣmaśarīraṃ tanmātrakaṃ trividhakaraṇopetaṃ tat trividhena bandhena badhyate / uktaṃ ca prākṛtena ca bandhena tathā vaikārikeṇa ca / dākṣiṇena tṛtīyena baddho nānyena mucyate / tat sūkṣmaṃ śarīraṃ dharmādharmaṃ saṃyuktam // 62 //
children.translated_text: For this reason, <s>Puruṣa</s> is neither bound, nor liberated, nor does he transmigrate, because it is <s>Prakṛti</s> alone, abiding in various substrates — the substrates of divine, human, and animal births, in the forms of <s>Buddhi</s>, <s>Ahaṃkāra</s>, <s>tanmātras</s>, <s>indriyas</s>, and <s>bhūtas</s> — that is bound, liberated, and transmigrates. Now, if he is by nature already liberated, and is all-pervading, how does he transmigrate? Transmigration is for the purpose of attaining what has not been attained. Thus it is said that <s>Puruṣa</s> is bound, <s>Puruṣa</s> is liberated, <s>Puruṣa</s> transmigrates — but such transmigrating nature does not truly exist. Through the knowledge of the distinction between <s>Sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, the true nature of <s>Puruṣa</s> is revealed. That revealed one is <s>Kevala</s> (isolated), pure, liberated, established in his own nature — such is <s>Puruṣa</s>. Here, if there is no bondage of <s>Puruṣa</s>, then there is no liberation either. To this it is replied: it is <s>Prakṛti</s> herself that binds herself and liberates herself. That <s>sūkṣma-śarīra</s> (subtle body) composed of <s>tanmātras</s>, equipped with the threefold instrument, is bound by threefold bondage. And it has been stated: by the bond of <s>prākṛta</s> (natural), and likewise by <s>vaikārika</s> (modified), and by <s>dākṣiṇa</s> (sacrificial) as the third — one bound thus is not freed by any other means. That subtle body is conjoined with <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit). [62]

children.text: prakṛtiśca badhyate prakṛtiśca mucyate saṃsaratīti kathaṃ taducyate /
children.translated_text: <s>Prakṛti</s> is bound and <s>Prakṛti</s> is liberated — it transmigrates. How is this stated?
By seven forms, <s>Prakṛti</s> thus binds herself by herself;
and she herself liberates [herself] for the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>, through one form. || 63 ||

children.text: rūpaiḥ saptabhirevaitāni sapta procyante dharmo vairāgyamaiśvaryamadharmo 'jñānamavairāgyamanaiśvaryyametāni prakṛteḥ saptarūpāṇi tairātmānaṃ svaṃ badhnāti prakṛtirātmānaṃ svameva saiva prakṛtiḥ puruṣasyārthaḥ puruṣārthaḥ karttavya iti vimocayatyātmānamekarūpeṇa jñānena // 63 //
children.translated_text: 'By seven forms' — these seven are declared: <s>dharma</s> (virtue), <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), <s>aiśvarya</s> (sovereignty), <s>adharma</s> (vice), <s>ajñāna</s> (ignorance), <s>avairāgya</s> (non-dispassion), and <s>anaiśvarya</s> (lack of sovereignty) — these are the seven forms of <s>Prakṛti</s>. By these, <s>Prakṛti</s> binds herself — her own self. That same <s>Prakṛti</s> liberates herself for the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> — the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> is to be accomplished — through one form: through knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>). // 63 //
How does that knowledge arise?
Thus, from the practice of the <s>tattvas</s> (principles), 'I am not, nothing is mine, there is no I' — completely, without remainder,
free from error, pure — sole (<s>kevala</s>) knowledge arises. || 64 ||

children.text: evamuktena kramena pañcaviṃśatitattvālocanābhyāsādiyaṃ prakṛtirayaṃ puruṣa etāni pañcatanmātrendriyamahābhūtānīti puruṣasya jñānamutpadyate nāsti nāhameva bhavāmi na me mama śarīraṃ tadyato 'hamanyaḥ śarīramanyannāhamityapariśeṣamahaṃkārarahitamapariśeṣamaviparyayādviśuddhaṃ viparyayaḥ saṃśayo 'viparyayādasaṃśayādviśuddhaṃ kevalaṃ tadeva nānyadastīti mokṣakāraṇamutpadyate 'bhivyajyate jñānaṃ pañcaviṃśatitattvajñānaṃ puruṣasyeti // 64 //
children.translated_text: Thus, in the manner described, from the repeated contemplation of the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s> — 'this is <s>Prakṛti</s>, this is <s>Puruṣa</s>, these are the five <s>tanmātras</s>, <s>indriyas</s>, and <s>mahābhūtas</s>' — knowledge arises in <s>Puruṣa</s>: 'I do not exist [as the body], I do not become, nothing is mine — this body, since I am other and the body is other — I am not [the body].' Without remainder — devoid of ego-sense, without residue. Free from error — error is doubt; free from error means free from doubt — pure. 'Sole' means 'that alone and nothing else' — [such knowledge] arises as the cause of liberation; the knowledge of the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s> is manifested for <s>Puruṣa</s>. // 64 //
What does <s>Puruṣa</s> do when knowledge [arises]?
Thereby, [seeing <s>Prakṛti</s> whose] production has ceased, who, due to having fulfilled the purpose, has withdrawn from the seven forms —
<s>Puruṣa</s> sees <s>Prakṛti</s>, standing like a spectator, abiding in himself. || 65 ||

children.text: tena viśuddhena kevalajñānena puruṣaḥ prakṛtiṃ paśyati prekṣakavat prekṣakeṇa tulyamavasthitaḥ svastho yathā raṃgaprekṣako 'vasthito narttakīṃ paśyatiḥ svasthaḥ svasmiṃstiṣṭhati svasthaḥ svasthānasthitaḥ / kathaṃbhūtāṃ prakṛtiṃ nivṛttaprasavāṃ nivṛttaḥ buddhyahaṃkārakāryyānarthavaśāt saptarūpavinivṛttāṃ nivarttitobhayapuruṣaprayojanavaśādyaiḥ saptabhī rūpairdharmādibhirātmānaṃ badhnāti tebhyaḥ saptabhyo rūpebhyo vinivṛttiṃ prakṛtiṃ paśyati // 65 //
children.translated_text: Through that pure, sole knowledge, <s>Puruṣa</s> sees <s>Prakṛti</s> like a spectator — abiding like a spectator, situated in himself. Just as a spectator at a theater, being seated, watches the dancer — 'abiding in himself' means standing in his own [nature], established in his own place. What kind of <s>Prakṛti</s>? One whose production has ceased — the production of <s>Buddhi</s>, <s>Ahaṃkāra</s>, and their effects having ceased — who, due to having fulfilled the purpose, has withdrawn from the seven forms: from those seven forms of <s>dharma</s> and the rest by which she binds herself — he sees <s>Prakṛti</s> who has withdrawn from those seven forms. // 65 //
Moreover:
'I have been seen,' [thinks] the one [<s>Prakṛti</s>], becoming indifferent; 'I have been seen,' [thinks] the other [<s>Puruṣa</s>], ceasing [to engage].

children.text: sati saṃyoge 'pi tayoḥ prayojanaṃ nāsti sargasya || 66 ||
children.translated_text: Though conjunction between the two persists, there is no purpose for creation. || 66 ||

children.text: raṃgastha iti yathā raṃgastha ityevamupekṣaka ekaḥ kevalaḥ śuddhaḥ puruṣastenāhaṃ dṛṣṭeti kṛtvā uparatā nivṛtā ekā ekaiva prakṛtiḥ trailokyasyāpi pradhānakāraṇabhūtā na dvitīyā prakṛtirasti mūrttibhede jātibhedādevaṃ prakṛtipuruṣayornirvṛttāvapi vyāpakatvāt saṃyogo 'sti na tu saṃyogāt kutaḥ sargo bhavati / sati saṃyoge 'pi tayoḥ prakṛtipuruṣayoḥ sarvagatatvāt satyapi saṃyoge prayojanaṃ nāsti sargasya sṛṣṭeścaritārthatvāt prakṛterdvividhaṃ prayojanaṃ śabdaviṣayopalabdhirguṇapuruṣāntaropalabdhiśca / ubhayatrāpi caritārthatvāt sargasya nāsti prayojanaṃ yaḥ punaḥ sarga iti / yathā dānagrahaṇanimitta uttamarṇādhamarṇayordravyaviśuddhau satyapi saṃyoge na kaścidarthasambandho bhavati / evaṃ prakṛtipuruṣayorapi nāsti prayojanamiti // 66 //
children.translated_text: 'One on the stage' — just as one on the stage [ceases performing], so the one who is indifferent, singular, pure <s>Puruṣa</s> — having determined 'I have been seen,' she who has ceased, withdrawn — one, the one and only <s>Prakṛti</s>, who is the primordial cause of the three worlds — there is no second <s>Prakṛti</s>; [apparent] differences of forms [arise] from differences of species. Thus, even when both <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> have accomplished their purposes, because of [<s>Prakṛti's</s>] all-pervasiveness, conjunction exists; but from that conjunction, no creation arises.

children.text: yadi puruṣasyotpanne jñāne mokṣo bhāti tato mama kasmānna bhavatīti / ata ucyate /
children.translated_text: If liberation appears for <s>Puruṣa</s> when knowledge has arisen, then why does it not happen for me? Therefore it is stated:
From the attainment of perfect knowledge, <s>dharma</s> and the rest no longer function as causes;
yet, due to the force of <s>saṃskāras</s> (latent impressions), [the sage] continues bearing the body, like the turning of a potter's wheel. || 67 ||

children.text: yadyapi pañcaviṃśatitattvajñānaṃ samyak jñānaṃ bhavati tathāpi saṃskāravaśāddhṛtaśarīro yogī tiṣṭhati kathaṃ cakrabhramavaccakrabhrameṇa tulyaṃ yathā kulālaścakraṃ bhramayitvā ghaṭaṃ karoti mṛtpiṇḍaṃ cakramāropya punaḥ kṛtvā ghaṭaṃ paryāmuñcati cakraṃ bhramatyeva saṃskāravaśādevaṃ samyagjñānādhigamādutpannasamyagjñānasya dharmādīnāmakāraṇaprāptau etāni sapta rūpāṇi bandhanabhūtāni samyagjñānena dagdhāni yathā nāgninā dagdhāni bījāni prarohaṇasamarthānyevametāni dharmādīni bandhanāni na samarthāni / dharmādīnāmakāraṇaprāptau saṃskāravaśāddhṛtaśarīrāstiṣṭhati jñānādvarttamānadharmādharmakṣayaḥ kasmānna bhavati varttamānatvādeva kṣaṇāntare kṣayamapyeti jñānaṃ tvanāgatakarma dahati varttamānaśarīreṇa ca yat karoti tadapīti vihitānuṣṭhānakaraṇāditi saṃskārakṣayāccharīrapāte mokṣaḥ // 67 //
children.translated_text: Although the perfect knowledge of the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s> constitutes right knowledge, nevertheless, due to the force of <s>saṃskāras</s>, the <s>yogin</s> continues bearing the body. How? 'Like the turning of a potter's wheel' — equal to the turning of a wheel: just as a potter, having turned the wheel and made a pot — having placed a lump of clay on the wheel, having made the pot and removed it — the wheel still continues turning due to the force of momentum. So too, from the attainment of perfect knowledge,
In what manner is he [distinguished]? It is stated:
When the separation of the body is attained, and with the cessation of <s>Pradhāna</s> because its purpose has been fulfilled,
[<s>Puruṣa</s>] attains <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation) — both absolute and final. || 68 ||

children.text: dharmādharmajanitasaṃskārakṣayāt prāpte śarīrabhede caritārthatvāt pradhānasya nivṛttau aikāntikamavaśyamātyantikamanantarhitaṃ kaivalyaṃ kevalabhāvānmokṣa ubhayamaikāntikātyantikamityeva viśiṣṭakaivalyamāpnoti // 68 //
children.translated_text: From the exhaustion of the <s>saṃskāras</s> (latent impressions) generated by <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, when the separation of the body is attained, and with the cessation of <s>Pradhāna</s> because its purpose has been fulfilled — [<s>Puruṣa</s>] attains <s>kaivalya</s> that is 'absolute' — certain, inevitable — and 'final' — without interruption. <s>Kaivalya</s> is from the state of being alone — liberation. Both — absolute and final — thus qualified, he attains <s>kaivalya</s>. // 68 //
This knowledge of the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>, a secret, was declared by the supreme sage.
Wherein the persistence, origination, and dissolution of beings are contemplated. || 69 ||

children.text: puruṣārtho mokṣastadarthaṃ jñānamidaṃ guhyaṃ rahasyaṃ paramarṣiṇā śrīkapilarṣiṇā samākhyātaṃ samyaguktaṃ yatra jñāne bhūtānāṃ vaikārikāṇāṃ sthityutpattipralayā avasthānāvirbhāvatirobhāvāścintyante vicāryante yeṣāṃ vicārāt samyak pañcaviṃśatitattvavivecanātmikā sampadyate saṃvittiriti // 69 //
children.translated_text: The purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> is liberation; the knowledge for that purpose — this secret, esoteric [teaching] — was properly declared by the supreme sage, the glorious sage <s>Kapila</s>. Wherein — in which knowledge — the persistence, origination, and dissolution of beings — of the modifications — meaning their continuance, manifestation, and disappearance — are contemplated, investigated. From the investigation of which, the complete understanding consisting of the discrimination of the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s> is achieved. // 69 //
The <s>Sāṃkhya</s> was proclaimed by the sage <s>Kapila</s> as the cause of liberation from <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) indeed.
Wherein these seventy <s>āryā</s> verses [are contained], and the commentary (<s>bhāṣya</s>) thereon was composed by <s>Gauḍapāda</s>.
Uncommented <s>kārikās</s>:
This most purifying and supreme [teaching], the sage, out of compassion, imparted to <s>Āsuri</s>;

children.text: āsurirapi pañcaśikhāya tena ca bahulīkṛtaṃ tantram || 70 ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Āsuri</s> to <s>Pañcaśikha</s>, and by him the doctrine was extensively elaborated. || 70 ||
Transmitted through a succession of disciples, this [teaching] was summarized in <s>āryā</s> verses by <s>Īśvarakṛṣṇa</s>,
of noble intellect, having properly understood the established doctrine. || 71 ||
The topics that are in the seventy [verses] are indeed the topics of the entire <s>Ṣaṣṭitantra</s> (Treatise of Sixty [Topics]),
without illustrative stories and without the refutation of opposing views. || 72 ||
